project.name: onixlabs-studio
project.description: ONIXLabs Studio — a cross-platform desktop IDE / agentic development environment (Electron + Angular 22, zoneless signals).

nodes.name: workspace-document-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Registry seam letting the active workspace register save and save-all handlers that ribbon and menu commands invoke without knowing the workspace internals.

nodes.name: WorkspaceDocumentCommands
nodes.summary: Registers and unregisters the active workspace's save/save-all handlers and forwards invocations to them.

nodes.name: workspace-find.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny registry service through which the active workspace exposes a reveal-Find-panel handler to ribbon and menu commands.

nodes.name: WorkspaceFind
nodes.summary: Registers the active workspace's Find-panel reveal handler and forwards reveal requests to it.

nodes.name: workspace-git.ts
nodes.summary: Per-workspace git status tracker: maintains file and ancestor-folder change status, binds to a repository, and debounces external refreshes driven by directory-watch events.

nodes.name: WorkspaceGit
nodes.summary: Tracks per-file and ancestor-folder git status for a workspace, binds to a repository, and coalesces external change events into scheduled refreshes.

nodes.name: workspace-source-control-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Registry seam for source-control commands (open view, commit, push, pull) that the active workspace registers and ribbon/menus invoke.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSourceControlCommands
nodes.summary: Registers the active workspace's source-control handlers and forwards open/commit/push/pull commands to them.

nodes.name: worktree-session.ts
nodes.summary: Manages the worktree session for a container root: labels and claims checkouts, tracks agent activity, refreshes worktree status, lists branches, and adds or removes worktrees.

nodes.name: WorktreeSession
nodes.summary: Session over a worktree container: initialises and activates checkouts, claims roots against concurrent use, tracks agent activity, refreshes status, and adds or removes worktrees.

nodes.name: agent-categories.ts
nodes.summary: Service persisting agent conversation categories over the IPC bridge with create/update/delete, ordering via sort-order allocation, and category clearing on delete.

nodes.name: AgentCategories
nodes.summary: CRUD store for agent conversation categories persisted over the bridge, allocating sort order for new categories and reloading on demand.

nodes.name: agent-conversations.ts
nodes.summary: Service for persisting agent conversations through bridge channels: list, load, save, update metadata, clear category assignments, and delete.

nodes.name: AgentConversations
nodes.summary: Persists agent conversations via IPC channels: listing (per context and all), load, save, metadata updates, category clearing, and deletion.

nodes.name: agent-prompts.ts
nodes.summary: Prompt-library service that saves and deletes reusable agent prompts, slugifies identifiers, and persists the collection in the settings store.

nodes.name: AgentPrompts
nodes.summary: Maintains the reusable prompt library: saves prompts under slugified ids, deletes them, and loads/persists the set through the settings store.

nodes.name: agent-quick-responses.ts
nodes.summary: Store of agent quick responses supporting add, remove and reorder, flattened for display and persisted through the settings store.

nodes.name: AgentQuickResponses
nodes.summary: Manages the quick-response list with add, remove and reorder operations, flattening for display and persisting via the settings store.

nodes.name: auxiliary-windows.ts
nodes.summary: Service that opens auxiliary child windows, adopts app styling into them, and watches for their close so resources are released.

nodes.name: AuxiliaryWindows
nodes.summary: Opens auxiliary child windows with adopted styling and close watching, cleaning up all open windows on destroy.

nodes.name: child-window-close.ts
nodes.summary: Utility exporting watchChildWindowClosed, which reliably observes a child window's close and invokes a listener exactly once.

nodes.name: watchChildWindowClosed
nodes.summary: Watches a child window and invokes the listener exactly once when the window closes, covering both event-driven and polled detection.

nodes.name: child-window-styling.ts
nodes.summary: Service that clones the main window's style nodes and root attributes into adopted child windows and keeps them synchronised via mutation observers.

nodes.name: ChildWindowStyling
nodes.summary: Adopts child windows by cloning style nodes and root attributes from the main document, keeping them in sync with mutation observers until released.

nodes.name: configure-dialog.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal service tracking whether the run-configuration dialog is open, exposing open and close operations for ribbon and view coordination.

nodes.name: ConfigureDialog
nodes.summary: Signals whether the run-configuration dialog is open and provides open/close transitions.

nodes.name: debug-adapters.ts
nodes.summary: Catalogue of DAP debug adapters: loads the adapter catalogue, resolves the adapter for a language, and persists per-language adapter choices in the settings store.

nodes.name: DebugAdapters
nodes.summary: Loads the debug-adapter catalogue and resolves or overrides the adapter used for each language, persisting choices in settings.

nodes.name: debugger.ts
nodes.summary: Global debugger facade: the active workspace registers its debug session, and launch/continue/pause/step/stop calls are delegated to whichever session is registered.

nodes.name: Debugger
nodes.summary: Facade over the registered debug session: register/unregister the active session and delegate launch, continue, pause, step, and stop.

nodes.name: directory-watch.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer-side directory watcher: asks the main process to watch or unwatch paths over file channels and fans change notifications out to subscribers.

nodes.name: DirectoryWatch
nodes.summary: Subscribes to main-process directory change notifications, reference-counting watch/unwatch requests and dispatching change callbacks.

nodes.name: dock-panel-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Registry seam through which the active view registers dock-panel toggle handlers, letting the View menu toggle panels without coupling to a specific view.

nodes.name: DockPanelCommands
nodes.summary: Registers per-view dock-panel toggle handlers and routes toggle commands from menus to the active view's handler.

nodes.name: editor-terminals.ts
nodes.summary: Tracks per-editor terminal state: visibility and mount status, queued commands awaiting a mounted terminal, and per-terminal state updates.

nodes.name: EditorTerminals
nodes.summary: Per-editor terminal bookkeeping: visibility and mount queries, show/hide/toggle, command queueing with take-pending semantics, and state updates.

nodes.name: feature-descriptor.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the feature registry: input contracts for feature views and document panels, the feature descriptor shape, and the default feature chrome constants.

nodes.name: feature-registry.ts
nodes.summary: Registry mapping feature identifiers to their view, ribbon, status, and document-panel components plus chrome settings, consumed by the shell when mounting tabs.

nodes.name: FeatureRegistry
nodes.summary: Stores feature descriptors and answers component lookups — view, ribbon, status, document panel, and chrome — by feature id.

nodes.name: provide-feature.ts
nodes.summary: Exports provideFeature, an environment-initializer helper that registers a feature descriptor with the FeatureRegistry at bootstrap.

nodes.name: provideFeature
nodes.summary: Creates providers that register a feature descriptor with the FeatureRegistry during application bootstrap.

nodes.name: code-runner.ts
nodes.summary: Small service that runs the active code file by resolving a run-file task from the task system and dispatching it.

nodes.name: CodeRunner
nodes.summary: Determines whether the active code file can run and dispatches a run-file task through the task system.

nodes.name: markdown-image-modal.ts
nodes.summary: Modal component for the markdown ribbon that collects an image URL or browsed file path plus alt text before inserting an image into the document.

nodes.name: MarkdownImageModal
nodes.summary: Form modal collecting image source (typed URL or browsed file) and alt text, with confirm/cancel/reset handling for markdown image insertion.

nodes.name: keyboard-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Settings section component for keyboard shortcuts: lists keybindings, captures replacement chords via keydown, reports rejections, and resets overrides.

nodes.name: KeyboardSettingsSection
nodes.summary: Keyboard settings UI: formats bindings for display, captures new chords from keydown events, surfaces rejection reasons, and resets overrides.

nodes.name: debug-session.ts
nodes.summary: Per-workspace DAP debug session: launches adapters, drives stepping and pause/continue, syncs breakpoints, refreshes call stacks, scopes and variables, evaluates expressions, and routes run-in-terminal requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Breakpoint re-sync is skipped via an order-independent definition signature that excludes transient verification state.

nodes.name: DebugSession
nodes.summary: Owns one debug adapter session end to end: launch and lifecycle, stepping commands, breakpoint synchronisation, call-stack/scope/variable inspection, expression evaluation, and run-in-terminal handling.

nodes.name: definitionSignature
nodes.summary: Builds an order-independent signature of every breakpoint's definition (excluding transient verification) so a re-sync can be skipped when only verification changed.

nodes.name: directory-host.ts
nodes.summary: Component that hosts a directory workspace tab: adopts the opened root, detects worktree containers, promotes checkouts, and hands the resolved root to the directory view.

nodes.name: DirectoryHost
nodes.summary: Adopts an opened directory root, recognises worktree containers, promotes or enters checkouts, and closes roots cleanly on teardown.

nodes.name: directory-ribbon.ts
nodes.summary: The workspace ribbon: exposes save/clipboard/find, build/run/debug with restart confirmations, source-control commands, worktree promotion, and full layout management (apply, save-as, rename, delete, templates).

nodes.name: DirectoryRibbon
nodes.summary: Handles every workspace ribbon command: document save, clipboard, find, build/run/debug with restart confirmation flows, source-control actions, worktree promotion, and layout selection/management.

nodes.name: directory-view.ts
nodes.summary: The main directory workspace view: mounts the dock layout, wires solution/packages/debug/logs panels, integrates source control, diagnostics, agents and run configurations, and registers workspace command seams.
nodes.languageNotes: Panels are synchronised to capability availability at render time; the dock blueprint seeds panels before the view constructor body runs.

nodes.name: DirectoryView
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the workspace surface: toggles and docks panels, syncs solution/packages/debug/logs panels to capabilities, runs default configurations, and bridges source-control and repository actions.

nodes.name: layout-templates.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the built-in layout templates (Default, Source Control, Agentic Engineering) that seed user layouts; templates are starting points copied into user-owned layouts, never shown directly in the ribbon.

nodes.name: package-explorer.ts
nodes.summary: Model backing the package browse experience: manages package sources, search queries, prerelease toggle, and paginated result fetching over the package-management bridge.

nodes.name: PackageExplorer
nodes.summary: Drives package browsing: source selection, query and prerelease filters, and incremental page fetching with reset handling.

nodes.name: package-model.ts
nodes.summary: Model of installed packages for a workspace project, with outdated-only filtering, ordered listing, and refresh over the package-management bridge channels.

nodes.name: PackageModel
nodes.summary: Holds the installed-package list for a project with outdated-only filtering, ordered presentation, and explicit refresh.

nodes.name: solution-model.ts
nodes.summary: The Solution Explorer tree model: lazily loads project items over the bridge, supports filtering, expansion, git-status decoration, follow-active-document, and distinguishes expansion-preserving reload from full refresh.
nodes.languageNotes: refresh() resets expansion state while reload() preserves it; item loading is pumped in batches to keep the tree responsive.

nodes.name: SolutionModel
nodes.summary: Lazily-loading solution tree: batched item pumping, filter-aware node appending, expansion bookkeeping, git-status toggling, follow-active-document, and reload-versus-refresh semantics.

nodes.name: settings-store.ts
nodes.summary: Small JSON key/value persistence abstraction over localStorage; every failure path degrades to the caller's fallback so settings never break application start-up.

nodes.name: shell-presence.ts
nodes.summary: Hides the main window when no tabs are open and shows it when one opens, so the welcome screen stands in for an empty IDE and no blank window flashes at cold start.

nodes.name: source-control-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Seam through which the directory ribbon's Source Control group invokes repo-global commands — fetch, stash and promote-to-worktree — on the active workspace's registered handler.

nodes.name: git-output.ts
nodes.summary: Pure parsers for git porcelain output: status, decorated log, refs, remote URLs, stashes and per-commit file lists, translated into the repository-data types.

nodes.name: git-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Git-backed implementation of the source-control provider contract: exposes the full command surface (status, commits, refs, stage/commit, branch, tag, remote, stash, merge and rebase operations) for one repository root via the git IPC API.

nodes.name: source-control-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Type-definition module describing the source-control provider contract: push targets, mutation results, blob access and the provider interface that GitProvider implements.

nodes.name: source-control-providers.ts
nodes.summary: Factory service that creates a source-control provider (currently always a GitProvider) for a given repository root.

nodes.name: source-control.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer client for the git IPC channels: createClient maps every source-control operation to its channel invocation and the SourceControl service exposes the resulting typed client.

nodes.name: studio-config.ts
nodes.summary: Loads and persists the workspace's .studio configuration — workspace settings, run configurations and user preferences — reloading on external directory changes while suppressing reloads caused by its own writes.

nodes.name: studio.ts
nodes.summary: Window-control service exposing minimize, maximize, close, show, hide and movable toggles over the bridge, plus platform identity and window-controls visibility.

nodes.name: workspace-run-configurations.ts
nodes.summary: Watches a workspace's stored run configurations, reloading them when the .studio directory changes externally and exposing the configurations and the default as signals.

nodes.name: tab-closer.ts
nodes.summary: Closes tabs behind a consistent unsaved-changes guard: walks the unsaved-work registry, prompts save/don't-save/cancel via the native dialog, and releases each source's document before removing the tab.

nodes.name: action-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Detects a workspace's build family (dotnet, gradle, maven, cmake, make, cargo, go, node) from marker files and maps build, rebuild and clean actions to concrete shell commands at both solution and project scope.

nodes.name: build-runner.ts
nodes.summary: Registered Builds handler that discovers workspace tasks per build family, dispatches builds and run configurations into terminal sessions, parses compiler output into diagnostics via problem matchers, and reports outcomes as notifications.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds run in real terminal sessions rather than a background task runner; problems are published to the diagnostics service per run.

nodes.name: builds.ts
nodes.summary: Seam between the UI and the build system: a registered handler receives build, run and cancel requests while the service exposes task lists, running state and busy signals to ribbons and menus.

nodes.name: run-file-task-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Task provider that runs the active file directly — resolving an interpreter command per language over the run IPC channels — and contributes the resulting task to the task system.

nodes.name: SettingsStore
nodes.summary: Reads and writes JSON-serialised values in localStorage, degrading to fallbacks on any storage or parse failure, and reports external changes.

nodes.name: ShellPresence
nodes.summary: Effect that shows the main window when tabs exist and hides it when none do, keeping an empty IDE window off screen.

nodes.name: SourceControlCommands
nodes.summary: Registers/unregisters the active view's command handler and forwards fetch, stash and promote-to-worktree, exposing availability signals for the ribbon.

nodes.name: mapStatus
nodes.summary: Translates a git status letter into the GitChangeStatus union.

nodes.name: workingChange
nodes.summary: Builds a GitFileChange for a working-tree entry from its path, status letters, staged flag and rename source.

nodes.name: parseStatus
nodes.summary: Parses `git status --porcelain=v2` output into staged and unstaged file-change lists with branch and tracking info.

nodes.name: parseDecorations
nodes.summary: Parses a commit's ref decoration string into GitRef badges (head, branches, remotes, tags).

nodes.name: parseLog
nodes.summary: Parses formatted `git log` output into GitCommit records with hashes, parents, authorship and decorations.

nodes.name: parseRefs
nodes.summary: Parses `git for-each-ref` output into branches, remote branches and tags with tracking (ahead/behind) details.

nodes.name: parseRemoteUrls
nodes.summary: Parses `git remote -v` output into a map of remote names to fetch/push URLs.

nodes.name: mergeRemoteUrls
nodes.summary: Merges parsed remote URLs into the remote list so each remote carries its fetch and push URLs.

nodes.name: parseStashes
nodes.summary: Parses `git stash list` output into GitStash records with index, branch and message.

nodes.name: parseCommitFiles
nodes.summary: Parses a commit's name-status diff output into per-file changes against the given parent.

nodes.name: GitProvider
nodes.summary: Implements the source-control provider contract with git: every query and mutation delegates to the git IPC API for the provider's repository root, parsing output where needed.

nodes.name: SourceControlProviders
nodes.summary: Creates a GitProvider bound to a repository root using the SourceControl client.

nodes.name: createClient
nodes.summary: Builds the typed source-control client, mapping each git operation (status, log, refs, stage, commit, branch, tag, remote, stash, merge, rebase) to its IPC channel invocation.

nodes.name: SourceControl
nodes.summary: Injectable holder of the source-control IPC client created by createClient.

nodes.name: StudioConfig
nodes.summary: Loads, mutates and persists the .studio workspace configuration, tracking generations and suppressing reloads triggered by its own writes while watching for external edits.

nodes.name: Studio
nodes.summary: Window controls (minimize, maximize toggle, close, show, hide, movable) plus platform and window-controls visibility over the bridge.

nodes.name: WorkspaceRunConfigurations
nodes.summary: Watches the workspace's .studio run configurations, reloading on external change and exposing the list and default configuration as signals.

nodes.name: TabCloser
nodes.summary: Closes a tab by walking unsaved-work sources, prompting through the native confirm-save dialog, and releasing documents before removing the tab.

nodes.name: detectBuildFamily
nodes.summary: Detects the workspace's build family by probing for marker files (solution/csproj, gradle, maven, CMake, Makefile, Cargo.toml, go.mod, package.json).

nodes.name: commandForAction
nodes.summary: Maps a solution-level build action (build, rebuild, clean) to the concrete shell command for the detected build family.

nodes.name: supportsProjectAction
nodes.summary: Reports whether the given project-scoped action is supported by the detected build family.

nodes.name: commandForProjectAction
nodes.summary: Maps a project-scoped build action to a shell command, delegating to the per-family builders with the project's relative directory.

nodes.name: BuildRunner
nodes.summary: The Builds handler: discovers per-family tasks, runs builds and run configurations in terminal sessions, publishes problem-matcher diagnostics, and notifies outcomes.

nodes.name: Builds
nodes.summary: Facade the UI calls for build/run/cancel: delegates to the registered handler and exposes tasks, active runs, running and busy state as signals.

nodes.name: RunFileTaskProvider
nodes.summary: Provides a run-the-active-file task: checks runnability per language, resolves the interpreter command over the run channels, and builds the task.

nodes.name: file-system.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer-side file-system service bridging over IPC to the main process: reads and writes files and drives the native open, save, pick and confirm dialogs.

nodes.name: file-watch.ts
nodes.summary: Reference-counted file watcher: subscribes to main-process file-change events over the bridge and fans them out to per-path callbacks, releasing watchers when unused.

nodes.name: forge-repository.ts
nodes.summary: Per-repository forge (GitHub) state: detects the hosting forge, loads pull requests, issues and workflow runs, polls for updates, and exposes checkout, rerun and cancel actions as signals-backed state.

nodes.name: forge.ts
nodes.summary: Thin renderer client for the forge IPC channels: forge detection, auth token management, and fetching pull requests, issues, comments and workflow runs from the main process.

nodes.name: keybindings.ts
nodes.summary: Central keyboard-shortcut service: registers scoped bindings from the catalogue, dispatches keydown events to the active scope, and validates and applies user chord overrides persisted in settings.

nodes.name: layouts.ts
nodes.summary: Manages user dock layouts and templates: seeds saved layouts from registered templates, handles select, save-as, rename, remove and transient switches, and persists everything through the SettingsStore.

nodes.name: lifecycle.ts
nodes.summary: Handles the window-close request from the main process: walks the unsaved-work registry and prompts to save, discard or cancel before permitting the window to close.

nodes.name: log.ts
nodes.summary: Structured logging service forwarding trace-to-error records over the log IPC channels to the main process, with query, session listing and live record subscription.

nodes.name: minimum-hold.ts
nodes.summary: Signal-based latch that keeps transient UI feedback (a spinner, a saved flash) visible for a minimum duration even when the underlying work finishes near-instantly.

nodes.name: modal-windows.fake.ts
nodes.summary: Test double for ModalWindows that records open requests and simulates window closure without creating real Electron child windows.

nodes.name: modal-windows.ts
nodes.summary: Opens modal dialogs as real Electron child windows: computes window features, fits the frame to content, centres over the parent window or screen, and tracks open children for cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Modals are real OS child windows rather than in-DOM overlays; sizing converts rem to pixels via the root font size.

nodes.name: output.ts
nodes.summary: Multiplexed output-channel service: named channels with bounded scrollback buffers, an active-channel selector, and write/clear event streams consumed by the Output panel.

nodes.name: printing.ts
nodes.summary: Drives printing and export-to-PDF over the print IPC channels, applying print settings and deriving a sensible PDF file name from the document title.

nodes.name: commit-message-generator.ts
nodes.summary: Generates a commit message with AI: builds a prompt from the repository's staged changes, runs it once through the AI runtime, and cleans the result, exposing generating and availability signals.

nodes.name: repository-data.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for git repository data — refs, commits, file changes, stashes and graph rows — plus the statusLetter mapper that turns a change status into its single-letter badge.

nodes.name: repository.ts
nodes.summary: The renderer's git repository model: binds a workspace root to a source-control provider, holds status, graph, branch, stash and diff state as signals, and implements every git action (stage, commit, push, pull, merge, rebase, tags, remotes) with notifications and external-change refresh.
nodes.languageNotes: External file-system changes are classified into bursts and debounced before triggering a status refresh.

nodes.name: FileSystem
nodes.summary: Injectable service wrapping file read/write and the native open, save, image-pick, path-pick and confirm dialogs behind the IPC bridge.

nodes.name: FileWatch
nodes.summary: Reference-counts watchers per path, ensures a path is watched while in use, and dispatches main-process change events to registered callbacks.

nodes.name: ForgeRepository
nodes.summary: Holds one repository's forge state: detection, pull-request/issue/workflow-run sections, watch/unwatch bookkeeping, polling, and workflow rerun/cancel/checkout actions.

nodes.name: sectionFor
nodes.summary: Decides which display section a loaded forge result belongs to, keeping items stable across refreshes by considering their previous placement and timestamps.

nodes.name: Forge
nodes.summary: Typed wrapper over the forge IPC channels: detect, auth status, token set/clear, and fetching pull requests, issues, comments and workflow runs.

nodes.name: Keybindings
nodes.summary: Registers scoped and global bindings, dispatches keyboard events through scope precedence, normalises and formats chords, and validates and persists user overrides.

nodes.name: Layouts
nodes.summary: Owns registered layout templates and saved user layouts: seeding, selection, transient template switches, save-as, rename, remove and persistence.

nodes.name: Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Listens for the main process's close request and resolves unsaved changes through save/discard/cancel prompts before the window may close.

nodes.name: Log
nodes.summary: Structured logger emitting trace/debug/info/warn/error records to the main process, with historic query, session listing and live record subscription.

nodes.name: createMinimumHold
nodes.summary: Creates a MinimumHold latch whose active signal stays on for at least the given duration after each begin, composable with a real busy signal.

nodes.name: FakeModalWindows
nodes.summary: Records modal open requests, exposes fitted sizes and open counts, and lets tests refuse opens or notify closure without Electron.

nodes.name: ModalWindows
nodes.summary: Opens Electron child windows for modals: builds window features, fits and frames content, centres over parent or screen, and destroys children on service teardown.

nodes.name: OutputChannel
nodes.summary: Handle for one named output channel: append, appendLine, clear, snapshot and reveal scoped to the channel's id.

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Central output service managing named channels, bounded buffers, the active channel selection and write/clear event streams.

nodes.name: Printing
nodes.summary: Invokes print and export-to-PDF over the bridge, injecting print styling and deriving the PDF file name from the document.

nodes.name: CommitMessageGenerator
nodes.summary: Builds a prompt from staged changes, runs a single AI completion through the runtime, and cleans the output into a usable commit message.

nodes.name: statusLetter
nodes.summary: Maps a git change status to its single-letter badge (A, M, D, R, U).

nodes.name: Repository
nodes.summary: The full git repository model: signal-backed status, graph, branches, stashes and diffs plus every mutating git operation, network-outcome notifications and burst-classified external refresh.

nodes.name: run-project-model.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the RUN_PROJECT_MODEL injection token through which the workspace view supplies its project model to the shared build runner, letting run configurations resolve real project targets without the runner depending on feature code.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an Angular InjectionToken carrying a Signal to invert a shared-service-to-feature dependency.

nodes.name: task.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the task system: the Task interface describing a runnable unit of work (run a file, build a project), the TaskProvider contract that produces tasks, and the TaskTarget union choosing between terminal and Output-panel execution.

nodes.name: tasks.ts
nodes.summary: Angular service acting as the task registry and dispatcher: task providers register themselves, aggregated tasks are collected on demand, and running a task resolves its command and queues it into the editor's docked terminal.

nodes.name: Tasks
nodes.summary: Registry service where TaskProviders register/unregister; getTasks aggregates provided tasks across providers and run resolves a task's command then queues it on the editor terminal.

nodes.name: terminal-sessions.ts
nodes.summary: Angular service owning the lifecycle of integrated terminal sessions: creating, launching, renaming, activating, and closing PTY-backed sessions over the terminal bridge, tracking exit codes and waiters, and revealing the terminal panel in the dock.
nodes.languageNotes: Signal-based session list with imperative PTY bridge callbacks; exposes TERMINAL_PANEL_ID and a DISPOSED_EXIT_CODE sentinel.

nodes.name: TerminalSessions
nodes.summary: Manages the full terminal session lifecycle — ensureShell/create/launch spawn PTYs via the terminal bridge, waitForExit and resolveWaiter coordinate run-to-completion consumers, and close/rename/activate/setShell manage the session list and active tab, with dock reveal integration.

nodes.name: unsaved-work-registry.ts
nodes.summary: Angular registry service aggregating unsaved-work sources: static sources come from the UNSAVED_WORK multi-token while dynamic sources register at runtime, so close/quit flows can enumerate everything with pending changes.

nodes.name: UnsavedWorkRegistry
nodes.summary: Combines injected static unsaved-work sources with dynamically registered ones; register returns a disposer removing the source, and sources() yields the union for dirty-state checks.

nodes.name: window-lock.ts
nodes.summary: Angular service controlling whether the application window may be dragged: setLocked/toggle flip a locked signal and forward the movability change to the main process via the Studio service, with settings-driven behaviour for releasing when hidden.

nodes.name: WindowLock
nodes.summary: Holds the window-locked signal and mirrors it to the OS window via Studio.setWindowMovable; toggle flips the current state and setLocked applies and logs it.

nodes.name: workspace-capabilities.ts
nodes.summary: Angular service through which the active workspace view publishes its capabilities (project model, build support, etc.) so shared UI like ribbons can adapt; register installs a capability model and unregister clears it if still current.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCapabilities
nodes.summary: Signal-backed holder for the current workspace capability model: register sets the source (logging the workspace kind), unregister clears it only when the caller is still the registered owner.

nodes.name: workspace.ts
nodes.summary: Central workspace service for the open folder: opens/closes folders over IPC, reads and writes files and byte ranges, maintains the file-explorer tree (expand/collapse, filtering, reconciliation), performs create/rename/delete mutations, and refreshes the tree from directory-watch events with burst batching.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large signal-driven service; tree refreshes are debounced into bursts and directory reads are bounded by a concurrency limiter (runBounded).

nodes.name: runBounded
nodes.summary: Runs an async task over a list of items with a fixed concurrency limit, used to bound parallel directory reads during tree refresh.

nodes.name: Workspace
nodes.summary: The workspace root's façade: openFolder/closeFolder manage the open root via the workspace IPC channels, readFile/writeBytes/readDirectoryListing proxy file access, tree methods (expandAll, collapseAll, toggleDirectory, reconcile, filteredRows) drive the explorer tree, and mutate/createFile/rename/delete perform confined file-system mutations with watch-driven refresh.

nodes.name: workspaces.ts
nodes.summary: Small Angular service handing an initial workspace payload from the app shell to the directory view: setInitial stores a pending open-folder request per key and takeInitial consumes it exactly once.

nodes.name: Workspaces
nodes.summary: Pending-map handoff for initial workspace open requests: setInitial records a payload under a key, takeInitial retrieves and deletes it so the request is consumed once.

nodes.name: worktrees.ts
nodes.summary: Angular service exposing a typed client for the worktree-container IPC channels: resolving what a directory is, describing checkout state, and promoting/adding/removing checkouts, built over the generic bridge.

nodes.name: createClient
nodes.summary: Builds the typed worktree IPC client over the generic Bridge, mapping each WorktreeChannel to a strongly typed invoke call.

nodes.name: Worktrees
nodes.summary: Injectable wrapper owning the worktree IPC client; constructs it from the bridge and logs availability.

nodes.name: agent-category-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral IPC contract for user-created agent conversation categories: the AgentCategoryChannel enum (list/save/delete/reorder) and the payload types for category records stored in the main process's user-data directory.

nodes.name: bridge.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the Bridge interface — the generic renderer-to-main messaging transport exposed by the Electron preload as window.bridge, with invoke/send/on primitives. It is the only IPC surface living in shared; each feature names its own channels over it.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately a dumb pub/sub transport; validation stays with each main-process handler.

nodes.name: debug-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral Debug Adapter Protocol IPC contract: the DebugChannel enum (start/stop/request/events) plus session, adapter-entry, and launch-resolution payload types, mirroring the LSP channel design with main-process-owned adapter lifecycles.

nodes.name: file-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral IPC contract for file-system and file-dialog operations: the FileChannel enum (read/write/watch/dialogs) and the FileInfo and payload types shared by the renderer file clients and the main-process file manager and watcher.

nodes.name: forge-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for the forge (GitHub-style host) capability: the ForgeChannel enum for detecting repositories, reading pull requests, issues, and workflow runs, and managing the auth token — all credentials and network calls confined to the main process.

nodes.name: language-slot.ts
nodes.summary: Extends the generic slot contract with per-language keying: a LanguageSlotEntry lists the languages it serves, and helpers filter entries for a language and resolve which entry wins given the user's selection.

nodes.name: entriesForLanguage
nodes.summary: Filters slot entries down to those declaring support for a given language id.

nodes.name: resolveForLanguage
nodes.summary: Resolves which language-keyed slot entry fills the slot for a language by filtering entries then delegating to the generic resolveSlot with the user's selection.

nodes.name: log-format.ts
nodes.summary: Shared log-message formatting helpers: serializeDetail turns an arbitrary detail value into a printable string (JSON with graceful fallback) and appendDetails joins serialized details onto a log message.

nodes.name: serializeDetail
nodes.summary: Serializes an arbitrary log detail value to a string, preferring JSON.stringify and falling back to String() when serialization fails.

nodes.name: appendDetails
nodes.summary: Appends serialized detail values to a log message, joining them after the message text.

nodes.name: package-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for package management: the PackageChannel enum for loading a workspace root's package model, listing configured package sources, and searching a source's packages.

nodes.name: package-management.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral package-management model types: ecosystems (npm/nuget), dependency scopes, upgrade status, and the project/package/source shapes the Package Management panel renders — deliberately distinct from the project-system model.

nodes.name: print-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for print/export: the PrintChannel.ExportPdf channel plus the ExportPdfRequest/result types used by the shared printing client and the main-process print manager.

nodes.name: project-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for the project system: the ProjectChannel enum for loading a workspace root's logical project model, lazily loading a project's items, and renaming solution folders.

nodes.name: project-system.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral logical project model types: ProjectNode/ProjectModel describing a solution's tree of folders and projects (independent of the on-disk layout), project item shapes, and build/run capability descriptors shared by the Solution Explorer and the main-process project systems.

nodes.name: run-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for code execution: the RunChannel.WriteTempFile channel and TempFileResult type, writing an editor buffer to a stable per-key temporary file so a language runner can execute it.

nodes.name: slot.ts
nodes.summary: The generic slot contract: a slot is an application capability multiple implementations may fill, each described by a SlotEntry (id, display name, priority); resolveSlot picks the winner honouring the user's explicit choice over priority.
nodes.languageNotes: Base contract for both unkeyed slots (e.g. container engine) and language-keyed slots layered on in language-slot.ts.

nodes.name: resolveSlot
nodes.summary: Resolves which slot entry fills a slot: the user's chosen entry wins when present among the candidates, otherwise the highest-priority candidate is selected.

nodes.name: source-control-channels.ts
nodes.summary: The git capability's IPC contract: the SourceControlChannel enum covering repository lifecycle, status, staging, commits, branches, merge/rebase, remotes, and history, with payload types — every operation confined in the main process to explicitly opened repository roots, treating the renderer as hostile.

nodes.name: studio-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for .studio persistence: the StudioChannel enum for loading a workspace's merged studio snapshot and independently saving the shared workspace.json and per-developer workspace.user.json files.

nodes.name: studio.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral model of the .studio workspace configuration: run-configuration and workspace/user file shapes plus tolerant parsers, serializers, defaults, compound-configuration expansion, selection/default resolution, and validation of run-configuration issues (duplicate ids, compound cycles).
nodes.languageNotes: Parsers are defensive against hand-edited JSON: unknown fields are dropped and malformed entries skipped rather than failing the load.

nodes.name: parseRunConfiguration
nodes.summary: Tolerantly parses one raw JSON value into a RunConfiguration, validating strings, filtering args and env entries, and parsing compound members; returns null for malformed input.

nodes.name: expandRunConfiguration
nodes.summary: Expands a run configuration into the concrete list to execute: a compound configuration walks its members recursively (guarding against cycles) while a plain configuration yields itself.

nodes.name: parseWorkspace
nodes.summary: Parses the raw shared workspace.json content into a StudioWorkspace, falling back to defaults for missing or malformed sections.

nodes.name: parseUser
nodes.summary: Parses the raw per-developer workspace.user.json content into a StudioUser record, tolerating missing fields.

nodes.name: resolveSelectedRunConfiguration
nodes.summary: Resolves the run configuration a snapshot selects: the user's selected id when it still exists, otherwise the default resolution.

nodes.name: resolveDefaultRunConfiguration
nodes.summary: Picks the default run configuration from a list when no explicit selection applies.

nodes.name: findRunConfigurationIssues
nodes.summary: Validates a set of run configurations, reporting issues such as duplicate ids, dangling compound members, and compound cycles detected by walking member graphs.

nodes.name: window-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for window control: the WindowChannel enum for the custom title-bar's minimize/maximize/close/set-movable operations, plus URL and feature constants for auxiliary panel and modal child windows.

nodes.name: workspace-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for the workspace (open-folder) capability: the WorkspaceChannel enum for open dialogs, confined file/byte reads and writes, directory listings, and workspace mutations, with the payload types shared by the workspace client and the main-process workspace manager.

nodes.name: worktree-channels.ts
nodes.summary: IPC contract for worktree containers: the WorktreeChannel enum for resolving what a directory is, describing a container's live checkout state, and container mutations (promote, add/remove checkout), with confinement to opened roots and trusted paths.

nodes.name: worktree.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral worktree-container model: descriptor/outcome/checkout types, the worktrees.json config shape with schema version, safe UUID checkout ids, tolerant parsing and serialization, and pure helpers to add or remove checkout entries.

nodes.name: isSafeCheckoutId
nodes.summary: Validates that a checkout id is a canonical UUID, rejecting anything that could smuggle path segments into checkout directory names.

nodes.name: defaultWorktreeConfig
nodes.summary: Builds a fresh worktrees.json config for a container from its origin and initial checkouts, stamped with the current schema version.

nodes.name: parseWorktreeConfig
nodes.summary: Tolerantly parses raw worktrees.json content into a WorktreeConfig, skipping malformed checkout entries and deduplicating ids, falling back to a default config when unreadable.

nodes.name: addCheckoutEntry
nodes.summary: Returns a new config with a checkout entry added, replacing any existing entry with the same id.

nodes.name: removeCheckoutEntry
nodes.summary: Returns a new config with the checkout entry of the given id removed.

nodes.name: credential-store.ts
nodes.summary: The per-connection credential store's pure logic: parses the encrypted blob's JSON map (migrating the legacy single-key format), mutates keys per connection id, and resolves credentials and auth status through the auth strategies — free of Electron/Node imports for testability.

nodes.name: parseCredentialMap
nodes.summary: Parses the decrypted blob into a connection-id-to-key map, migrating a legacy raw Anthropic key string onto the built-in Anthropic API-key connection.

nodes.name: CredentialStore
nodes.summary: Holds one API key per connection id behind injected blob read/write ports, and resolves each connection's run credential and UI status through the strategy registered for its auth kind.

nodes.name: model-discovery.ts
nodes.summary: Discovers a connection's models by querying its /models endpoint (OpenAI-compatible providers and Anthropic) with an injected fetch, then merges results into the existing list; unsupported kinds degrade to 'add models manually' rather than failing.

nodes.name: parseModelsResponse
nodes.summary: Parses a /models endpoint response into discovered model entries, tolerating both OpenAI-style and Anthropic-style payload shapes.

nodes.name: mergeModels
nodes.summary: Merges discovered models into the connection's existing list, preserving user-edited entries while appending new ones.

nodes.name: discoveryBaseUrl
nodes.summary: Chooses the base URL discovery should query for a connection, from its configured endpoint or the kind's default.

nodes.name: discoveryTarget
nodes.summary: Builds the full discovery request target — URL and auth headers — for a connection's kind, selecting Anthropic versus OpenAI-compatible header conventions.

nodes.name: runDiscovery
nodes.summary: Runs the whole HTTP model-discovery flow with an injected fetch: resolves the target, queries it, parses and merges models with context-window seeding, and returns a displayable failure when anything goes wrong.

nodes.name: ollama-endpoint.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves where a local Ollama server lives from OLLAMA_HOST/OLLAMA_BASE_URL; deliberately dependency-free so the model-runtime contribution can use it without dragging the AI SDK into the startup module graph.

nodes.name: resolveOllamaBaseUrl
nodes.summary: Resolves the OpenAI-compatible base URL for the local Ollama server from the environment, defaulting to the standard local address.

nodes.name: resolveOllamaOrigin
nodes.summary: Resolves the native API origin of the local Ollama server for the model-runtime contribution.

nodes.name: permission-rule-store.ts
nodes.summary: Persists the user's remembered permission decisions (#241) — tools always allowed globally or per workspace — under userData; only grants are ever stored so a mis-click cannot silently deny a tool.

nodes.name: PermissionRuleStore
nodes.summary: Lazily loads, queries, and appends remembered permission grants keyed by tool display name, scoped globally or per workspace root, validating the stored shape before trusting it.

nodes.name: renderer-bridge.ts
nodes.summary: The main-to-renderer capability bridge: sends a capability request to the renderer over IPC and tracks the outstanding promise until the reply arrives or a timeout fails it.

nodes.name: RendererBridge
nodes.summary: Registers the reply channel, issues capability requests to the focused window with per-request ids, and settles pending promises on reply, error, or timeout.

nodes.name: studio-tools.ts
nodes.summary: The catalogue of Studio's in-app agent tools and their prompt appendices: editor document read/edit/insert with previewed edits, terminal I/O, binary editor reads and writes, API Explorer requests, run configurations, workbench actions, and the AskUser round-trip — all executed against the renderer through the capability bridge.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports fully-qualified MCP tool names (FQN constants) alongside handlers so both the Claude MCP path and the AI-SDK path address the same tool identities.

nodes.name: buildRunPrompt
nodes.summary: Assembles the run's base system prompt from the context's mode, surface, and workspace details.

nodes.name: listRunConfigurations
nodes.summary: Asks the renderer for the workspace's run configurations and returns them to the model.

nodes.name: saveRunConfigurations
nodes.summary: Validates and forwards run-configuration definitions to the renderer to be saved.

nodes.name: deleteRunConfigurations
nodes.summary: Deletes run configurations by id through the renderer bridge, reporting what was removed.

nodes.name: askUser
nodes.summary: Poses a clarifying question with choices to the user through the input round-trip and returns the answer.

nodes.name: readTerminalOutput
nodes.summary: Reads the active terminal's recent output buffer via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: writeTerminalInput
nodes.summary: Writes text into the active terminal, optionally submitting it, through the renderer bridge — a mutating action gated by permissions upstream.

nodes.name: previewedEdit
nodes.summary: Runs a document edit through the preview flow: shows the proposed change in the editor, awaits the user's edit decision (with auto-accept support), then commits or cancels the preview — falling back to the direct edit when previews are unavailable.

nodes.name: readActiveDocument
nodes.summary: Reads the active editor document's content and metadata via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: replaceActiveDocument
nodes.summary: Replaces the active document's entire content through the previewed-edit flow.

nodes.name: setActiveDocumentLanguage
nodes.summary: Sets the active document's language mode via the renderer bridge, validating the requested language id.

nodes.name: runActiveDocument
nodes.summary: Runs the active document through the workspace's run pipeline with a bounded timeout, returning captured output or a timeout report.

nodes.name: editActiveDocument
nodes.summary: Applies an old-string/new-string edit (optionally replace-all) to the active document through the previewed-edit flow.

nodes.name: insertIntoActiveDocument
nodes.summary: Inserts text into the active document at a placement (cursor, start/end, or relative to an anchor) through the previewed-edit flow.

nodes.name: readBinary
nodes.summary: Shared helper issuing a binary-editor read capability (overview, bytes, selection, or disassembly) with an optional range to the renderer.

nodes.name: patchBinaryBytes
nodes.summary: Overwrites bytes at an offset in the open binary document, validating the byte payload before forwarding.

nodes.name: insertBinaryBytes
nodes.summary: Inserts bytes at an offset in the open binary document via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: deleteBinaryBytes
nodes.summary: Deletes a byte range from the open binary document via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: writeBinaryAssembly
nodes.summary: Assembles instructions (Keystone-backed in the renderer) and writes the resulting bytes at an offset in the open binary document.

nodes.name: listApiRequests
nodes.summary: Lists the API Explorer's saved requests through the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: createApiRequest
nodes.summary: Creates a new API Explorer request definition via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: updateApiRequest
nodes.summary: Applies changes to an existing API Explorer request by id via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: sendApiRequest
nodes.summary: Executes a saved API Explorer request and returns the response summary to the model.

nodes.name: openDocument
nodes.summary: Opens a new document tab in the workbench with the given format, title, content, and language via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: saveDocument
nodes.summary: Saves an open document by id through the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: openFile
nodes.summary: Opens a file by path in the workbench through the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: openTerminal
nodes.summary: Opens a new terminal in the workbench through the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: setApiVariable
nodes.summary: Sets an API Explorer environment variable by name via the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: tool-format.ts
nodes.summary: Display formatting for agent tool traffic: strips MCP name prefixes, summarizes tool inputs to one descriptive line, and clamps input/output payloads for the transcript.

nodes.name: summarizeToolInput
nodes.summary: Produces a one-line summary of a tool's input by surfacing the most descriptive common field (path, pattern, command, query, or URL).

nodes.name: clampPayload
nodes.summary: Truncates a payload string to the display budget with an elision marker so transcripts stay bounded.

nodes.name: formatToolInput
nodes.summary: Serializes a tool's input to clamped, display-ready text for the transcript.

nodes.name: formatToolOutput
nodes.summary: Normalizes a tool's output (strings, structured content, errors) into clamped display text for the transcript.

nodes.name: tool-policy.ts
nodes.summary: Per-tool policy values accepted from the renderer, the audit grant-source computation (#311), and sanitization of untrusted policy maps.

nodes.name: coarseGrantSource
nodes.summary: Computes the coarse audit source for an executed tool: explicit allow policy wins, then an auto-allowing posture (auto-edits only for edit tools), else the gated-or-auto bucket.

nodes.name: sanitizeToolPolicies
nodes.summary: Narrows an untrusted renderer value to a map of recognised per-tool policy values, dropping anything malformed.

nodes.name: write-confinement.ts
nodes.summary: Write-confinement logic (#307) for the built-in file-writing tools: extracts a confined tool's target path and range-checks it against allowed roots and deny lists before the write runs; in-app editor tools and reads are intentionally out of scope.

nodes.name: writeTargetPath
nodes.summary: Extracts the filesystem target path from a confined write tool's input, checking file_path, notebook_path, and the defensive path fallback keys.

nodes.name: isWriteWithinRoots
nodes.summary: Determines whether a resolved write target lies within any of the run's allowed roots.

nodes.name: isWriteDenied
nodes.summary: Determines whether a write target falls under an entry of the deny list (resolved against a base), blocking the write even inside an allowed root.

nodes.name: sanitizeWritePaths
nodes.summary: Narrows an untrusted value to a list of usable confinement paths, optionally requiring absolute entries.

nodes.name: claude-executable.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves the Claude Code CLI binary the Agent SDK should spawn: the asar-unpacked bundled binary in packaged builds, a system-installed CLI from PATH, or a user-supplied path, honouring the user's executable choice.
nodes.languageNotes: In a packaged build a native binary cannot be spawned from inside app.asar (ENOTDIR); the resolver returns the app.asar.unpacked copy produced by electron-builder's asarUnpack.

nodes.name: resolveBundledClaudeExecutable
nodes.summary: Returns the app.asar.unpacked path of the per-platform bundled Claude CLI binary in a packaged build, or undefined in development so the SDK resolves it itself.

nodes.name: resolveExecutableOnPath
nodes.summary: Locates a named executable on the user's PATH, returning its absolute path or undefined when absent.

nodes.name: resolveClaudeExecutable
nodes.summary: Resolves the Claude CLI according to the user's executable choice (bundled, system, or custom path), falling back safely when the chosen option is unavailable.

nodes.name: claude-login-parse.ts
nodes.summary: Pure parsing helpers for the in-app Claude login flow, split from the PTY driver so they carry no node-pty/Electron dependency and are unit-testable in isolation.

nodes.name: parseLoggedIn
nodes.summary: Parses `claude auth status --json` output into the app's auth status; any shape that is not an explicit loggedIn:true fails safe as signed-out.

nodes.name: extractLoginUrl
nodes.summary: Extracts the first sign-in URL from CLI output, powering the manual 'open sign-in page' fallback.

nodes.name: claude-login.ts
nodes.summary: Drives Claude sign-in from inside the app: reads the authoritative auth status via the CLI and runs the CLI's own login in a hidden pseudo-terminal so credentials land exactly where the Agent SDK reads them.
nodes.languageNotes: The installed claude CLI stays the login engine; Studio never reimplements Anthropic's OAuth, and the PTY is never shown as a dock terminal.

nodes.name: readClaudeAuthStatus
nodes.summary: Runs `claude auth status --json` and parses the result, distinguishing an expired/absent login from any other run failure.

nodes.name: runClaudeLogout
nodes.summary: Runs the CLI's logout so the stored Claude credentials are cleared through the same engine that wrote them.

nodes.name: ClaudeLoginDriver
nodes.summary: Runs `claude auth login` in a hidden PTY, scans bounded output for the sign-in URL to surface in the modal, and reports success, cancellation, or the error tail on failure.

nodes.name: claude-model-discovery.ts
nodes.summary: Discovers the models a Claude local-login connection offers via the Agent SDK's supportedModels() control channel (no API key needed), mapping SDK model info to Studio's shape and merging it into the connection's existing list.

nodes.name: contextWindowFromDescription
nodes.summary: Infers a model's context window from the SDK description text when the id itself does not encode one.

nodes.name: claudeContextWindow
nodes.summary: Resolves the best-guess context window for a discovered Claude model, combining bracketed-id hints, description parsing, and the shared context-window heuristics.

nodes.name: resolvedVersionLabel
nodes.summary: Derives a human-facing version label from the concrete model id an SDK alias resolves to.

nodes.name: formatClaudeLabel
nodes.summary: Formats a discovered Claude model's display label from its alias, resolved version, and description.

nodes.name: userFlags
nodes.summary: Computes the user-visible flags (such as default marking) for a discovered model entry.

nodes.name: mergeClaudeModels
nodes.summary: Merges discovered Claude models into the connection's existing list, preserving user edits while adding newly reported models.

nodes.name: runClaudeDiscovery
nodes.summary: Runs the whole discovery flow for a Claude login connection through an injected supportedModels call, mapping and merging results and describing failures for display.

nodes.name: claude-remote-control.ts
nodes.summary: Mirrors a live Claude session to claude.ai remote control (#331): the RemoteControlBridge forwards transcript traffic, surfaces permission prompts and questions as requires_action states, and parses inbound grants and answers from the bridge channel.

nodes.name: RemoteControlBridge
nodes.summary: Owns the claude.ai bridge session for a live run: opens it with the user's OAuth token, forwards messages, raises and cancels remote permission/question prompts, and reports worker state transitions.

nodes.name: inboundText
nodes.summary: Extracts the user-authored text from an inbound bridge message, ignoring non-text payloads.

nodes.name: resolveControlResponse
nodes.summary: Routes an inbound control response to the matching pending permission or question, settling the corresponding round-trip.

nodes.name: parseGranted
nodes.summary: Parses a remote permission response payload into a granted/denied decision, failing safe on unrecognised shapes.

nodes.name: parseQuestionAnswer
nodes.summary: Parses a remote question-answer payload into the selected choices for the pending AskUser round-trip.

nodes.name: claude-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and writes the Claude Code user settings file for the couple of keys Studio surfaces — the remote-control push-notification preferences toggled from Studio's own settings UI.

nodes.name: writeRemoteNotificationsEnabled
nodes.summary: Writes the account-level 'push when actions required' preference into the Claude Code settings file, preserving the rest of the document.

nodes.name: codex-agent-provider.ts
nodes.summary: The AgentProvider for OpenAI Codex: drives the Codex SDK's thread API for runs and live sessions, translating thread events (text deltas, tool starts/ends, usage) into Studio events, with the SDK client narrowable to a test fake.

nodes.name: CodexAgentProvider
nodes.summary: Implements AgentProvider for Codex: describes availability from the ChatGPT login, builds client and thread options (including the bundled executable override), and opens sessions or one-shot runs.

nodes.name: CodexAgentSession
nodes.summary: A live multi-turn Codex session over a persistent SDK thread: builds turn input, consumes the event stream per turn, emits deltas/tool/usage events, and supports interrupt and close.

nodes.name: codex-executable.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves the bundled Codex CLI native binary from app.asar.unpacked in a packaged build (returning undefined in development), mirroring the Claude executable resolver.

nodes.name: resolveBundledCodexExecutable
nodes.summary: Returns the asar-unpacked path of the per-platform codex binary for the SDK's codexPathOverride in packaged builds, or undefined so the SDK resolves it from node_modules in development.

nodes.name: codex-model-discovery.ts
nodes.summary: Discovers models for a ChatGPT-backed Codex login from the local Codex runtime's models_cache.json catalogue, since a subscription token gets 401 from the platform /v1/models endpoint.

nodes.name: parseCodexModelsCache
nodes.summary: Parses the visible models out of a Codex models_cache.json document in the runtime's priority order, tolerating unknown shapes.

nodes.name: runCodexDiscovery
nodes.summary: Runs Codex model discovery through an injected file reader (so tests never touch the developer's Codex home), merging catalogue models into the connection and describing failures.

nodes.name: connection-guard.ts
nodes.summary: Pure validation of connection data arriving from the renderer: narrows untrusted values to the fields the providers and run path read before the main process builds providers and endpoints from them.

nodes.name: isConnection
nodes.summary: Type guard determining whether an untrusted value is a well-formed connection carrying the fields the run path reads.

nodes.name: sanitizeConnections
nodes.summary: Filters an untrusted array down to well-formed connections, dropping anything the guard rejects.

nodes.name: sanitizeClaudeExecutable
nodes.summary: Narrows an untrusted Claude executable choice to the recognised modes, falling back to the bundled CLI for anything outside the set.

nodes.name: context-windows.ts
nodes.summary: Pure heuristic resolving a best-guess context window (tokens) for a model id, seeding a newly-discovered model's token-meter denominator; unknown ids resolve to a safe editable default.

nodes.name: resolveContextWindow
nodes.summary: Resolves a context window from known id entries and model-family heuristics (including bare SDK aliases without the claude- prefix), defaulting conservatively when nothing matches.

nodes.name: agent-audit-log.ts
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL audit log recording every granted mutating/exec agent action, with a coarse grant-source classification (policy, posture, or gated-or-auto) and size-based rotation.

nodes.name: AgentAuditLog
nodes.summary: Writes audit entries as JSONL under userData and rotates the file when it exceeds its size cap, keeping only whole trailing lines.

nodes.name: tailWholeLines
nodes.summary: Trims log content to roughly the requested byte budget while keeping only complete lines, so rotation never leaves a torn JSONL record.

nodes.name: agent-category-store.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process store for the user's conversation categories, persisted as a single flat categories.json registry under userData/agent-conversations with graceful degradation on every read.

nodes.name: AgentCategoryStore
nodes.summary: Registers IPC handlers and owns list/save/delete of conversation categories, validating untrusted shapes before writing the single JSON registry file.

nodes.name: agent-conversation-store.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process store for persisted agent conversations: one JSON file per conversation plus a lightweight summary index, scoped by conversation context and keyed by filesystem-safe ids.

nodes.name: AgentConversationStore
nodes.summary: Owns the conversation files and their summary index: load/save/delete conversations, update metadata, clear a category, and sanitize ids so a conversation id can never escape the store directory.

nodes.name: agent-provider.ts
nodes.summary: The AgentProvider seam: type and interface definitions every AI provider implements (availability, run, live sessions, permission/edit-decision round-trips, run context), decoupling AiManager from concrete Claude/Codex/AI-SDK implementations.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure TypeScript interfaces and type aliases; the file compiles to nothing at runtime, making the provider seam a compile-time contract.

nodes.name: ai-auth-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process authentication front door for AI connections: validates keyed-auth IPC requests, persists API keys encrypted at rest via safeStorage, and reports per-connection auth status.

nodes.name: AiAuthManager
nodes.summary: The Electron shell around CredentialStore: registers IPC handlers, encrypts/decrypts the credential blob with safeStorage, checks for local Claude and Codex logins, and resolves auth status per connection.

nodes.name: ai-manager.ts
nodes.summary: The central AI orchestrator in the main process: builds and rebuilds providers from connections, dispatches runs and live-session turns, and mediates every permission, input, edit-decision, and steering round-trip between providers and the renderer.

nodes.name: AiManager
nodes.summary: Owns providers, live sessions, run lifecycle (clocks, reaping, aborts), model discovery dispatch, permission and edit-decision resolution, audit recording, and sanitization of untrusted renderer payloads such as images and context paths.
nodes.languageNotes: A single large coordinator class (~40 methods) whose collaborators are all injected seams (auth, bridge, login, stores), keeping each collaborator independently testable.

nodes.name: ai-sdk-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Implements AgentProvider over the Vercel AI SDK for stateless API-key providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, DeepSeek, Ollama, custom endpoints), resolving endpoints per connection kind and appending a local-model tool appendix where needed.

nodes.name: AiSdkAdapter
nodes.summary: The stateless-model AgentProvider: describes availability from resolved credentials, creates the right AI SDK client for the connection's family, runs a turn through the shared stream consumer, and translates failures into displayable messages.

nodes.name: clientFamily
nodes.summary: Maps a connection kind to the AI SDK client family (anthropic vs OpenAI-compatible) that should serve it.

nodes.name: resolveEndpoint
nodes.summary: Resolves the base URL a connection should call, preferring the connection's own endpoint, then kind defaults, with Ollama resolved from the environment.

nodes.name: ai-sdk-stream.ts
nodes.summary: The AI SDK run pipeline shared by all stateless providers: builds the per-surface tool sets (studio, terminal, workbench, API, binary) with permission gating, assembles the surface prompt, consumes the agent stream, and maps stream parts to Studio's AiEvent shape.

nodes.name: describeRunError
nodes.summary: Turns a thrown run error into a concise, user-displayable message, unwrapping AI SDK error shapes.

nodes.name: consumeAgentStream
nodes.summary: Drains the AI SDK full stream for a run, mapping each part to Studio events and emitting them through the run context.

nodes.name: createAskUserTool
nodes.summary: Builds the AskUser tool that lets the model pose a clarifying question with choices, round-tripping the answer through the renderer.

nodes.name: gated
nodes.summary: Wraps a mutating tool's execute with the permission gate: consults per-tool policy and posture, prompts the user when required, and records the granted action in the audit log.

nodes.name: createStudioTools
nodes.summary: Builds the editor-surface tool set (read/replace/edit/insert active document, set language, run document, run configurations) with edit tools routed through the previewed-edit gate.

nodes.name: createTerminalTools
nodes.summary: Builds the terminal-surface tool set: reading terminal output and gated writing of terminal input.

nodes.name: createWorkbenchTools
nodes.summary: Builds the workbench-surface tool set: open/save documents, open files and terminals, and related gated workbench actions.

nodes.name: createApiTools
nodes.summary: Builds the API Explorer tool set: list/create/update/send API requests and set variables, with mutations behind the permission gate.

nodes.name: createBinaryTools
nodes.summary: Builds the binary-editor tool set: overview/bytes/selection/disassembly reads plus gated patch, insert, delete, and assembly writes.

nodes.name: promptForSurface
nodes.summary: Assembles the system prompt for the run's surface from the studio-tools prompt appendices (studio, terminal, workbench, API, binary, run configuration).

nodes.name: toolsForSurface
nodes.summary: Selects the tool set matching the run's agent surface, composing the surface-specific builders with the shared AskUser tool.

nodes.name: mapStreamPart
nodes.summary: Translates one AI SDK stream part (text deltas, tool calls/results, usage, errors) into the corresponding Studio AiEvent, formatting tool payloads for display.

nodes.name: auth-strategies.ts
nodes.summary: The pluggable authentication seam: an AuthStrategy per AiAuthKind turns a resolved credential context into the credential a run uses and the status the UI shows, deliberately free of Electron/Node imports for isolated unit testing.
nodes.languageNotes: A registry of strategy objects keyed by auth kind; adding an OAuth strategy is a drop-in registration with no caller changes.

nodes.name: strategyFor
nodes.summary: Looks up the AuthStrategy registered for an auth kind, the single entry point callers use to resolve credentials and status.

nodes.name: claude-agent-provider.ts
nodes.summary: The live-harness AgentProvider driving the Claude Agent SDK: builds run options (tools, hooks, sandbox, executable), decides permissions, manages multi-turn ClaudeAgentSession lifecycles with a background message pump, and mirrors sessions to claude.ai remote control.
nodes.languageNotes: The largest file in the AI layer; the SDK query factory is injected (createQuery seam) so multi-turn session behaviour is testable against a fake query.

nodes.name: ClaudeAgentProvider
nodes.summary: Implements AgentProvider for Claude: assembles SDK run options (canUseTool gating, hooks, MCP studio tools, sandbox, resolved executable), handles every SDK message kind into Studio events, tracks usage including subagents, and answers AskUserQuestion round-trips.

nodes.name: ClaudeAgentSession
nodes.summary: A live multi-turn Claude session: feeds turns through a persistent SDK query via an async prompt stream and background pump, settles/rejects turns, publishes slash commands and background-task state, and optionally opens the remote-control bridge.

nodes.name: parseAskUserQuestions
nodes.summary: Parses the AskUserQuestion tool input into validated question/choice structures, rejecting malformed shapes before they reach the renderer.

nodes.name: managedSpawnerOption
nodes.summary: Provides a managed child-process spawner for the SDK that records spawned CLI processes in the pid journal and kills process trees on cleanup, so orphaned agent processes cannot outlive Studio.

nodes.name: buildSandbox
nodes.summary: Builds the SDK sandbox configuration from the run context's confinement settings, translating allowed roots and deny lists into the sandbox shape.

nodes.name: claude-credentials.ts
nodes.summary: Reads the local Claude login's OAuth access token — from the macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json — so Studio can call the claude.ai/code bridge API on the user's behalf; returns null rather than throwing when unavailable.

nodes.name: readClaudeAccessToken
nodes.summary: Resolves the Claude CLI's OAuth access token from the platform credential store, treating any failure as 'remote control unavailable' (null) rather than an error.

nodes.name: readFromKeychain
nodes.summary: Reads the Claude Code credentials entry from the macOS Keychain via the security CLI and extracts the access token.

nodes.name: binary-assembler.ts
nodes.summary: Wraps the Keystone assembler engine to turn assembly source text into machine bytes for multiple architectures, lazily loading the WebAssembly module and registering IPC handlers used by the binary editor.
nodes.languageNotes: Keystone is loaded as a WebAssembly module on first use to keep main-process startup light.

nodes.name: bitnessFor
nodes.summary: Maps an architecture identifier to the Keystone mode and bitness used to configure the assembler.

nodes.name: BinaryAssembler
nodes.summary: Lazily loads the Keystone WebAssembly module and assembles source text into machine bytes per architecture, registering its IPC handler for the binary editor.

nodes.name: binary-disassembler.ts
nodes.summary: Disassembles machine code via the Capstone engine with per-architecture instance caching, including a resynchronising decode that fills undecodable gaps with byte directives so output never silently truncates.
nodes.languageNotes: Caches one Capstone instance per architecture and resyncs after invalid instructions instead of aborting the decode.

nodes.name: architectureSpec
nodes.summary: Maps an architecture identifier to the Capstone architecture and mode constants used to build a disassembler instance.

nodes.name: BinaryDisassembler
nodes.summary: Disassembles machine code through cached per-architecture Capstone instances, resynchronising past undecodable bytes by emitting byte directives so the decode always covers the full range.

nodes.name: code-runner.ts
nodes.summary: Supports running the active document by writing its contents to a session-scoped temporary file and exposing that seam over IPC, cleaning the directory up on dispose.

nodes.name: CodeRunner
nodes.summary: Writes the active document to a session-scoped temporary file over IPC so run configurations can execute it, and removes the session directory on dispose.

nodes.name: api-client.contribution.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process contribution backing the API Explorer: performs HTTP requests on behalf of the renderer, tracks in-flight requests so they can be aborted, and maps failures into a structured result shape.

nodes.name: ApiClientContribution
nodes.summary: Contribution that sends renderer-described HTTP requests from the main process, tracks in-flight requests for cancellation, and normalises errors into a structured failure result.

nodes.name: container-engine.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the ContainerEngine abstraction and the catalogue of known engine descriptors (socket paths, display names), plus a probe that reports whether a described engine's socket is actually reachable.

nodes.name: containerEngineCatalogue
nodes.summary: Returns the catalogue of known container engine descriptors.

nodes.name: isEngineAvailable
nodes.summary: Probes whether a described container engine is actually reachable through its socket.

nodes.name: containers.contribution.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process contribution wiring the container engine into IPC: exposes container and image listing, lifecycle actions, engine selection, event watching, and Docker Desktop launch behind permission checks.

nodes.name: ContainersContribution
nodes.summary: Contribution that exposes container listing, lifecycle actions, engine selection, event watching, and Docker Desktop launch over permission-gated IPC.

nodes.name: docker-desktop.ts
nodes.summary: Computes the platform-specific command needed to launch Docker Desktop and spawns it, so the containers view can offer to start the engine when its socket is not reachable.

nodes.name: dockerDesktopLaunchCommand
nodes.summary: Computes the platform-specific command and arguments used to launch Docker Desktop.

nodes.name: launchDockerDesktop
nodes.summary: Spawns Docker Desktop using the platform-specific launch command and reports whether the launch was accepted.

nodes.name: docker-engine.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the container engine operations against the Docker Engine HTTP API over an injected transport: listing containers and images, start/stop/remove actions, status, and a streaming event watch.

nodes.name: parseEvent
nodes.summary: Parses one line of the Docker event stream into a typed container event, returning null for lines that are not relevant events.

nodes.name: DockerEngine
nodes.summary: Container engine implementation over the Docker Engine HTTP API: lists containers and images, performs start/stop/remove actions, reports status, and watches the event stream through an injected transport.

nodes.name: docker-transport.ts
nodes.summary: HTTP transport for the Docker Engine API over its local socket, providing single request/response calls and long-lived streams for the event watch.
nodes.languageNotes: Talks HTTP over a Unix domain socket (or named pipe) rather than TCP, which is why socket permission brokering exists.

nodes.name: HttpDockerTransport
nodes.summary: Performs HTTP requests and opens long-lived streams against the Docker Engine API over its local socket.

nodes.name: engine-selection.ts
nodes.summary: Persists and resolves the user's chosen container engine: loads the stored choice, filters the catalogue to available engines, and falls back sensibly when the chosen engine is missing.

nodes.name: loadChoice
nodes.summary: Loads the persisted engine choice from the store file, tolerating a missing or malformed file.

nodes.name: availableEngines
nodes.summary: Filters the engine catalogue down to engines whose sockets are currently reachable.

nodes.name: selectedEngine
nodes.summary: Resolves the engine to use: the persisted choice when it is still available, otherwise a sensible available fallback.

nodes.name: chooseEngine
nodes.summary: Persists the user's engine choice after validating it against the catalogue.

nodes.name: describeEngines
nodes.summary: Describes every catalogued engine with its availability and whether it is the current selection, for the engine picker UI.

nodes.name: forge-budget.ts
nodes.summary: Request-budget primitives for forge API calls: an ETag cache that enables conditional requests answered with 304s, and a rate-limit ledger that records limit headers and blocks further calls until the reset time.
nodes.languageNotes: A 304 response carries no body, so the cache stores both the entity tag and the last full body it validated.

nodes.name: EtagCache
nodes.summary: Caches entity tags and the bodies they validated, so forge requests can be made conditional and 304 responses served from the stored body.

nodes.name: RateLimitLedger
nodes.summary: Records rate-limit headers from forge responses and reports until when further calls should be blocked once the remaining budget is exhausted.

nodes.name: forge-credential-store.ts
nodes.summary: Persists per-host forge access tokens encrypted at rest, with parse/serialize helpers for the token map and a resolve path that hands a token to the provider without exposing it to the renderer.

nodes.name: parseTokenMap
nodes.summary: Parses decrypted plaintext into a host-to-token map, rejecting shapes that are not a string record.

nodes.name: serializeTokenMap
nodes.summary: Serialises the host-to-token map to the plaintext form that is encrypted at rest.

nodes.name: ForgeCredentialStore
nodes.summary: Stores per-host forge tokens encrypted on disk, exposing set/clear/has operations and resolving a token for a host without surfacing it to the renderer.

nodes.name: forge-detection.ts
nodes.summary: Detects which forge (e.g. GitHub) a repository belongs to by parsing its git remote URL into host, owner, and repository components across HTTPS and SSH remote forms.

nodes.name: detectForge
nodes.summary: Identifies the forge kind and repository reference for a git remote URL, supporting HTTPS and SSH remote forms.

nodes.name: splitRemote
