nodes.summary: Splits a git remote URL into host and path components across HTTPS, SSH, and scp-like syntaxes.

nodes.name: forge-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the ForgeProvider seam: minimal response and fetch abstractions plus the provider interface a concrete forge (such as GitHub) fulfils, injected so providers are testable without a network.

nodes.name: forge.contribution.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process contribution exposing forge operations over IPC — pull requests, issues, comments, workflow runs, and auth status — validating renderer payloads and constructing the default GitHub-backed store and provider (including a gh CLI token fallback).

nodes.name: asIssueNumber
nodes.summary: Validates that an IPC payload value is a usable issue number.

nodes.name: asRepository
nodes.summary: Validates that an IPC payload value is a well-formed forge repository reference.

nodes.name: readGhToken
nodes.summary: Reads a GitHub token from the gh CLI's stored configuration as a fallback when no token is stored in the credential store.

nodes.name: defaultStore
nodes.summary: Constructs the default encrypted credential store wired to Electron safe storage and the user data directory.

nodes.name: defaultProvider
nodes.summary: Constructs the default GitHub forge provider for a token, wiring in fetch, the ETag cache, and the rate-limit ledger.

nodes.name: ForgeContribution
nodes.summary: Contribution that routes forge IPC — auth status, pull request, issue, comment, and workflow run operations — through a detected provider built from the credential store, validating every renderer payload.

nodes.name: github-forge.ts
nodes.summary: GitHub REST implementation of the ForgeProvider seam: lists pull requests, issues, comments, and workflow runs, re-runs and cancels runs, and rolls check runs and commit statuses into one CI verdict, all budgeted through the ETag cache and rate-limit ledger.
nodes.languageNotes: GitHub reports CI through two systems (check runs and commit statuses); rollUpChecks merges the union into a single status.

nodes.name: rollUpChecks
nodes.summary: Merges GitHub check runs and the legacy commit status into a single CI verdict, taking the union of both reporting systems.

nodes.name: mapRunStatus
nodes.summary: Maps a GitHub workflow run status and conclusion pair onto the shared forge run status enumeration.

nodes.name: describeStatus
nodes.summary: Produces a human-readable description for an HTTP status returned by the GitHub API.

nodes.name: GitHubForge
nodes.summary: GitHub REST implementation of ForgeProvider: identity, pull request, issue, comment, and workflow run queries plus re-run/cancel actions, sending every request through the ETag cache and rate-limit ledger.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Static in-bundle manifest of main-process contributions activated at startup — the backend extension point: a new backend is added by appending to this list, never by editing application construction logic.

nodes.name: main-contribution-registry.ts
nodes.summary: Activates and disposes the set of main-process contributions, with TrackedIpc recording every ipcMain handle/on registration so a disposed contribution never leaks IPC handlers.

nodes.name: TrackedIpc
nodes.summary: Wraps ipcMain registration so every handle and on call made by a contribution is recorded and removed when the contribution is disposed.

nodes.name: MainContributionRegistry
nodes.summary: Activates the manifest of main contributions with their tracked IPC and namespaced loggers, and disposes them all in reverse on shutdown.

nodes.name: main-contribution.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the MainContribution seam: the ContributionContext surface (tracked IPC, namespaced logging, permissions) handed to a contribution at activation, and the lifecycle contract every backend contribution implements.

nodes.name: curated-catalog-source.ts
nodes.summary: In-memory model catalogue source that searches the curated model list by name and description, providing the hand-picked half of the AI Model Manager's catalogue.

nodes.name: CuratedCatalogSource
nodes.summary: Catalogue source that searches the in-bundle curated model list by query text, needing no network.

nodes.name: curated-models.ts
nodes.summary: Static data table of curated local AI models (families, parameter sizes, quantisations, descriptions) plus a converter that maps a curated entry into the shared catalogue model shape.
nodes.languageNotes: Predominantly a static data table; the only logic is the curatedToModel mapping function.

nodes.name: curatedToModel
nodes.summary: Converts a curated model entry into the shared catalogue model shape used by the AI Model Manager.

nodes.name: huggingface-catalog-source.ts
nodes.summary: Model catalogue source that queries the Hugging Face hub API, filtering out gated models, inferring parameter sizes from model ids, and mapping hub results into the shared catalogue shape.

nodes.name: isGated
nodes.summary: Reports whether a Hugging Face model is gated and therefore unusable without extra authorisation.

nodes.name: toCatalogModel
nodes.summary: Maps a Hugging Face hub result into the shared catalogue model shape.

nodes.name: parameterSizeFromId
nodes.summary: Infers a model's parameter size (e.g. 7B) from its Hugging Face model id when the API does not state it.

nodes.name: HuggingFaceCatalogSource
nodes.summary: Catalogue source that queries the Hugging Face hub search API over an injected HTTP function, filtering gated models and mapping results into catalogue models.

nodes.name: model-catalog.ts
nodes.summary: Aggregates model catalogue sources (curated and Hugging Face) into one search, tolerating individual source failures and de-duplicating models that appear in more than one source.

nodes.name: dedupe
nodes.summary: Removes duplicate models that appear in more than one catalogue source, keeping the first occurrence.

nodes.name: ModelCatalog
nodes.summary: Searches all registered catalogue sources, tolerating per-source failures and de-duplicating the combined results.

nodes.name: model-runtime.contribution.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process contribution behind the AI Model Manager: consumer-tracked status polling, catalogue search, and model pulls with streamed progress and cancellation, wired over IPC against a pluggable ModelRuntime (Ollama by default).
nodes.languageNotes: Polling starts only while renderer consumers are registered, and status pushes are suppressed when unchanged.

nodes.name: sameStatus
nodes.summary: Compares two runtime statuses so unchanged polls do not push redundant updates to the renderer.

nodes.name: ModelRuntimeContribution
nodes.summary: Contribution that drives the AI Model Manager over IPC: consumer-tracked status polling, catalogue search, streamed model pulls with cancellation, and runtime install/start/stop against the pluggable ModelRuntime.

nodes.name: model-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the ModelRuntime provider slot the AI Model Manager is built against, covering model enumeration, inspection, removal, and server lifecycle — with a server-absent-safe contract where an unreachable runtime yields empty results rather than throws.

nodes.name: ollama-assets.ts
nodes.summary: Maps platform and architecture to the correct Ollama release asset, its download URL, the executable name, and the conventional system install locations searched during detection.

nodes.name: ollamaAsset
nodes.summary: Selects the Ollama release asset descriptor for a platform and architecture pair.

nodes.name: ollamaAssetUrl
nodes.summary: Builds the full download URL for an Ollama release asset at the pinned version.

nodes.name: ollamaExecutableName
nodes.summary: Returns the platform-appropriate Ollama executable file name.

nodes.name: ollamaSystemLocations
nodes.summary: Enumerates the conventional per-platform filesystem locations where a system-installed Ollama executable may live.

nodes.name: ollama-provisioner.ts
nodes.summary: Detects an existing Ollama installation (managed dir, system locations, PATH) or provisions a managed one: downloads the release asset, verifies its SHA-256, extracts it, and probes the executable's version.

nodes.name: parseVersion
nodes.summary: Extracts the semantic version from `ollama --version` output.

nodes.name: OllamaProvisioner
nodes.summary: Detects an existing Ollama executable (managed install, system locations, PATH) or provisions a managed one by downloading the release asset, verifying its SHA-256, extracting it, and probing its version.

nodes.name: ollama-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Ollama implementation of the ModelRuntime slot: status, installed and running model listing, model detail, streamed pulls with parsed progress, removal, and disk usage, composed from the provisioner, server, and HTTP transport.

nodes.name: parsePullLine
nodes.summary: Parses one NDJSON line of an Ollama pull stream into normalised pull progress, handling layer downloads, verification, and completion states.

nodes.name: hostFromOrigin
nodes.summary: Derives the host header value Ollama expects from a configured origin.

nodes.name: ollamaModelStore
nodes.summary: Resolves the directory where Ollama stores model blobs, honouring the OLLAMA_MODELS override.

nodes.name: readContextLength
nodes.summary: Reads a model's context window length out of Ollama's model info payload, which keys it by architecture.

nodes.name: OllamaRuntime
nodes.summary: ModelRuntime implementation for Ollama composing the provisioner, server, and HTTP transport: status, model listing and detail, streamed pulls, removal, disk usage, and server install/start/stop.

nodes.name: ollama-server.ts
nodes.summary: Owns the lifecycle of a spawned `ollama serve` process: distinguishes an externally running server from one Studio started, waits for health, records the child in the pid journal, and stops owned servers on shutdown.
nodes.languageNotes: Registers the spawned process with the pid journal so an orphaned server can be reaped after a crash.

nodes.name: stopsOnShutdown
nodes.summary: Reports whether a server of the given ownership kind should be stopped when Studio shuts down.

nodes.name: OllamaServer
nodes.summary: Spawns and owns an `ollama serve` process: distinguishes external from Studio-started servers, waits until healthy, records the child in the pid journal, and stops only owned servers on shutdown.

nodes.name: ollama-transport.ts
nodes.summary: HTTP transport for the Ollama API providing JSON request/response calls and NDJSON streaming used for pull progress.

nodes.name: HttpOllamaTransport
nodes.summary: HTTP transport to the Ollama API supporting JSON request/response calls and NDJSON line streaming used for pull progress.

nodes.name: container-socket.ts
nodes.summary: Permission broker factory for container engine socket access: resolves the selected engine's socket path and creates the broker that gates main-process access to it.

nodes.name: resolveContainerSocketPath
nodes.summary: Resolves the socket path of the currently selected container engine for permission brokering.

nodes.name: ContainerSocketFactory
nodes.summary: Permission broker factory that creates the broker gating main-process access to the selected container engine's socket.

nodes.name: grant-policy.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the GrantPolicy interface that decides whether a declared main-process permission is granted, keyed on the requesting contribution's origin, alongside the v0 DefaultGrantPolicy.

nodes.name: DefaultGrantPolicy
nodes.summary: The v0 grant policy: allows every declared permission for first-party contributions and denies all third-party requests, pending the user-driven stored policy planned for the grant prompt.

nodes.name: permission-broker.ts
nodes.summary: PermissionBroker resolves a contribution's permission request into a privileged handle — possession of the handle is the authority — consulting the grant policy and audit-logging every decision.

nodes.name: PermissionBroker
nodes.summary: Mints the handle a granted permission resolves to: consults the GrantPolicy per origin, records a PermissionAuditEntry, and throws PermissionDeniedError when the decision is deny.

nodes.name: permission.ts
nodes.summary: Core permission model for main-process contributions: ContributionOrigin and GrantDecision types mirroring the agent's allow/ask/deny model, the PERMISSION_IDS registry, PermissionDeniedError, and declared-permission sanitization.

nodes.name: PermissionDeniedError
nodes.summary: Error thrown when the grant policy denies a requested permission, carrying the permission id and origin for diagnostics.

nodes.name: sanitizePermissions
nodes.summary: Filters a manifest's declared permission list down to the known PERMISSION_IDS, dropping unrecognised entries so unknown strings can never be granted.

nodes.name: bundled-lockfiles.ts
nodes.summary: Compiles the npm lockfiles for the curated index's npm-provisioned plugins into the application bundle, so installs work offline and while the private repository's published copies 404 on raw.githubusercontent.com.
nodes.languageNotes: Lockfiles are imported as JSON modules so they ship inside the bundle — the only reachable copy while the repo is private.

nodes.name: bundledLockfile
nodes.summary: Returns the compiled-in lockfile document matching a published lockfile URL, or undefined when the URL is not one of the bundled set.

nodes.name: contributed.ts
nodes.summary: Aggregates plugin manifests from the curated index and the sideloaded directory, merges them by id, and derives the contributed plugin descriptors, language-server descriptors and debug-adapter entries for registration.

nodes.name: mergeManifests
nodes.summary: Merges manifest lists from multiple sources by plugin id, letting later sources (sideloaded) override earlier ones (curated index).

nodes.name: pluginIndex
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the singleton PluginIndex rooted in the app's userData directory.

nodes.name: contributedManifests
nodes.summary: Returns the merged set of valid plugin manifests from the curated index and sideloaded plugins.

nodes.name: contributedPlugins
nodes.summary: Maps the contributed manifests to PluginDescriptor entries for the plugin manager's catalogue.

nodes.name: contributedLanguageServers
nodes.summary: Derives LanguageServerDescriptor entries from the contributed manifests for LSP registration.

nodes.name: contributedDebugAdapters
nodes.summary: Derives debug-adapter catalogue entries from the contributed manifests, wiring each to the payload provisioner.

nodes.name: plugin-catalogue.ts
nodes.summary: The static built-in plugin catalogue: descriptors for downloadable language servers and debug adapters (clangd, TypeScript server, debugpy and friends) with install, uninstall and installed-state operations wired to the LSP, archive and debug provisioners.

nodes.name: archivePlugin
nodes.summary: Builds a PluginDescriptor for an archive-provisioned language server, wiring install/uninstall/isInstalled through the archive provision plan.

nodes.name: adapterPlugin
nodes.summary: Builds a PluginDescriptor for a downloadable debug adapter, delegating install and removal to the DebugProvisioner.

nodes.name: pluginCatalogue
nodes.summary: Assembles the full built-in catalogue: language-server plugins, debug-adapter plugins and the debugpy virtualenv plugin, given the plugin context's provisioners.

nodes.name: plugin-index.ts
nodes.summary: The curated plugin index as data: a seed copy compiled into the app and a published copy fetched at runtime, with the higher revision winning; parses and validates manifests and caches the winning document to disk.

nodes.name: parsePluginIndex
nodes.summary: Parses and validates a raw index document into revision plus manifest list, rejecting malformed entries with ManifestError diagnostics.

nodes.name: pluginIndexUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the published index URL, honouring an environment override for testing.

nodes.name: PluginIndex
nodes.summary: Owns the two-copy index lifecycle: reads the disk cache or bundled seed, refreshes from the published URL, keeps whichever revision is higher, and exposes the winning manifests.

nodes.name: plugin-loader.ts
nodes.summary: Converts plugin manifests into runtime artefacts: discovers sideloaded plugin directories, validates manifests, and maps them to provision plans, plugin descriptors, language-server descriptors and debug-adapter entries.

nodes.name: discoverPlugins
nodes.summary: Scans a directory for plugin subdirectories, reading and parsing each one's manifest file into a ManifestResult.

nodes.name: validManifests
nodes.summary: Filters discovery results down to successfully parsed manifests, logging the failures.

nodes.name: toProvision
nodes.summary: Maps a manifest's download declarations to an archive provision plan keyed by platform.

nodes.name: toTreeProvision
nodes.summary: Maps a manifest's npm lockfile declaration to a lockfile-based tree provision plan.

nodes.name: toOrigin
nodes.summary: Determines a manifest's payload origin — bundled lockfile, published lockfile or archive download — deciding where its bytes actually come from.

nodes.name: payloadOps
nodes.summary: Builds the install/uninstall/isInstalled operations for a manifest's payload, choosing archive or lockfile provisioning per its origin.

nodes.name: toContributions
nodes.summary: Summarises what a manifest contributes (language servers, debug adapters) for display in the Plugin Manager.

nodes.name: toDetail
nodes.summary: Builds the detail block (version, publisher, requirements) shown for a plugin in the manager UI.

nodes.name: toPluginDescriptor
nodes.summary: Converts a manifest into a full PluginDescriptor with payload operations and contribution summary for the plugin manager's catalogue.

nodes.name: toLanguageServerDescriptors
nodes.summary: Maps a manifest's language-server declarations to LanguageServerDescriptor entries with resolve logic honouring the payload's install state.

nodes.name: toDebugAdapterEntries
nodes.summary: Maps a manifest's debug-adapter declarations to catalogue entries whose specs resolve through the provisioned payload.

nodes.name: plugin-manager.ts
nodes.summary: PluginManager owns the plugin model's first two layers — the catalogue of what is available and the installed state on this machine — handling install and uninstall with a busy-guard while slot selection stays elsewhere.

nodes.name: PluginManager
nodes.summary: Indexes available PluginDescriptors, performs guarded install/uninstall through their operations, records results in the PluginStore, and summarises each plugin's state for the UI.

nodes.name: plugin-store.ts
nodes.summary: PluginStore persists install records — what was installed and where it landed — to a JSON file in userData, so an uninstall removes exactly what an install put there.

nodes.name: PluginStore
nodes.summary: Loads, parses, mutates and saves the install-record file, exposing get/add/remove over records keyed by plugin id.

nodes.name: plugins.contribution.ts
nodes.summary: The Plugin Manager's main-process backend contribution: wires the built-in catalogue, contributed plugins, store and manager together and exposes list, install, uninstall and index-refresh over the plugin IPC channels.

nodes.name: PluginsContribution
nodes.summary: MainContribution that activates the plugin subsystem: builds the PluginManager from catalogue plus contributed descriptors, refreshes the curated index, and handles the plugin IPC channels.

nodes.name: sideloaded.ts
nodes.summary: Discovers sideloaded plugin manifests dropped into the user's plugins directory, scanned once per launch and cached — mid-session appearance is deliberately not watched.

nodes.name: sideloadDirectory
nodes.summary: Returns the userData subdirectory sideloaded plugins are dropped into, one subdirectory per plugin.

nodes.name: sideloadedManifests
nodes.summary: Returns the valid manifests discovered in the sideload directory, cached for the lifetime of the launch.

nodes.name: metrics-readers.ts
nodes.summary: Pure reader functions that transform systeminformation and Electron app-metrics results into app-usage, network, disk and GPU metric shapes; inputs are structural so the module stays unit-testable without importing systeminformation.

nodes.name: readAppUsage
nodes.summary: Aggregates Electron process metrics into the app's own CPU percentage (normalised by core count) and memory usage.

nodes.name: sumNetwork
nodes.summary: Sums receive/transmit rates across network interface stats into a single NetworkMetric.

nodes.name: readDisk
nodes.summary: Maps filesystem I/O stats to a DiskMetric of read/write rates.

nodes.name: parseIoregGpu
nodes.summary: Parses macOS ioreg output for GPU utilisation, extracting the device utilisation percentage.

nodes.name: pickGpu
nodes.summary: Chooses the most relevant GPU controller from systeminformation's list, preferring one reporting utilisation.

nodes.name: metrics-sampler.ts
nodes.summary: MetricsSampler computes CPU and memory percentages from cumulative per-core time counters between successive samples; the CpuTimes input structurally matches os.cpus() so the sampler stays pure and unit-testable.

nodes.name: MetricsSampler
nodes.summary: Keeps the previous sample's cumulative core counters and derives per-interval CPU utilisation plus memory usage into a MetricsSample.

nodes.name: system-monitor.contribution.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process contribution that samples system and app metrics — CPU, memory, network, disk and GPU (including macOS ioreg) — on a consumer-driven timer and streams MetricsSamples to renderers over IPC.

nodes.name: SystemMonitorContribution
nodes.summary: Tracks IPC consumers, starts and stops the sampling timer with demand, and per tick gathers readings via systeminformation, the MetricsSampler and the pure readers before broadcasting.

nodes.name: dap-client.ts
nodes.summary: DapClient is the Node-side shell around one Debug Adapter Protocol connection: starts the transport, runs the initialize handshake under a 30s timeout, correlates requests and responses, and relays events, reverse requests and runInTerminal to listeners.

nodes.name: DapClient
nodes.summary: Binds a DapTransport to the DapMessageDecoder and DapProtocol, exposing initialize, sendRequest, event/reverse-request/runInTerminal listeners, exit notification and disposal with handshake timeout handling.

nodes.name: dap-protocol.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free DAP framing and sequencing: Content-Length header framing shared with LSP, but DAP's own seq/request_seq envelope rather than JSON-RPC — DapMessageDecoder splits the byte stream and DapProtocol correlates requests, events and reverse requests.

nodes.name: encodeMessage
nodes.summary: Serialises a DAP message with its Content-Length header into a Buffer ready for the transport.

nodes.name: DapProtocol
nodes.summary: Implements DAP sequencing over a message sink: assigns seq numbers, matches responses to pending requests by request_seq, and dispatches events and reverse requests to listeners.

nodes.name: dap-transport.ts
nodes.summary: The three DAP transports: StdioTransport spawns an adapter over stdio, TcpServerTransport spawns a server process and connects once it announces its port, and TcpClientTransport attaches to an already-listening adapter — all registering PIDs in the journal and killing process trees on dispose.

nodes.name: StdioTransport

nodes.name: TcpServerTransport

nodes.name: TcpClientTransport
nodes.summary: Connects to an already-listening host and port to exchange DAP bytes — the attach-style transport with no child process of its own.

nodes.name: debug-adapter-registry.ts

nodes.name: DebugAdapterRegistry

nodes.name: setting-descriptions.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves dynamic help text for settings whose descriptions depend on runtime state — currently the modern-UI-features hint, which names the GPU-derived recommendation from the Display service; settings without a dynamic description fall back to the registry's static text.

nodes.name: SettingDescriptions
nodes.summary: Service mapping setting keys to dynamic descriptions; builds the appearance.modernUiFeatures hint from the detected GPU and recommended mode.

nodes.name: settings.feature.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the settings feature with the application shell: contributes the settings view to the feature registry so the shell mounts it for the settings tab.

nodes.name: provideSettingsFeature
nodes.summary: Builds the environment providers that register the settings feature descriptor at start-up.

nodes.name: terminal-keybindings.ts
nodes.summary: Catalogues the terminal's keyboard accelerators as a keybinding-catalogue entry consumed by the shared keybindings service.

nodes.name: terminal-status-strip.ts
nodes.summary: Status strip contributed by the terminal feature: renders the active terminal's context (such as the running shell) as status segments with icons, reading the per-view TerminalStatus through the active view's injector.

nodes.name: TerminalStatusStrip
nodes.summary: Component computing the status segments for the active terminal tab from the view-scoped TerminalStatus context.

nodes.name: agent-keybindings.ts
nodes.summary: Catalogues the agent tab's keyboard accelerators (stop run, new conversation) as a keybinding-catalogue entry; both defaults are non-typing chords so they never collide with the message composer.

nodes.name: agent.feature.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the agent feature with the application shell: contributes the agent view and ribbon to the feature registry, its keybinding catalogue, and eagerly instantiates AgentEditorCapabilities so in-app editor tools are available whenever an agent runs.

nodes.name: provideAgentFeature
nodes.summary: Builds the environment providers that stand the agent feature up at start-up: feature descriptor, keybinding catalogue, and an app initializer that instantiates the agent's editor capabilities.

nodes.name: binary-agent-capabilities.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the binary editor's AI tool capabilities with the shared AI runtime: reading the open binary's overview, hex/ASCII dumps, selection and disassembly, and mutating it via byte patches, inserts, deletes, and assembled instructions, with read sizes capped so tool calls never flood the transcript.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges the agent tool-call surface (ai-types channel constants) to the BinaryDocuments registry; every write is validated and described back to the model.

nodes.name: BinaryAgentCapabilities
nodes.summary: Service exposing the binary editor to agents: read capabilities render bounded hex/disassembly dumps of the active binary document, and write capabilities patch, insert, delete, or assemble bytes with clamping, validation, and outcome messages for the model.

nodes.name: binary-assembly.ts
nodes.summary: Thin renderer-side service that assembles textual instructions into machine bytes by calling the main process's native assembler over the IPC bridge on the binary channels.

nodes.name: BinaryAssembly
nodes.summary: Service with a single assemble method that forwards assembly source and target architecture to the main-process assembler channel and returns the AssembleResult.

nodes.name: binary-disasm-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Docked disassembly side panel for binary tabs: a read-only Monaco assembly listing of the decoded instruction window, with two-way selection sync — clicking a line selects its bytes in the hex grid, and a byte selection highlights and reveals its instruction line.
nodes.languageNotes: Maintains a per-line instruction map so Monaco line numbers round-trip to byte offsets; registers the shared ASM Monaco language.

nodes.name: BinaryDisasmPanel
nodes.summary: Component rendering the assembly listing in a read-only text editor, applying selection highlights via Monaco decorations, revealing the line for the current byte selection, and emitting byte ranges when instruction lines are clicked.

nodes.name: buildContent
nodes.summary: Builds the panel's DisasmContent from decoded instructions: the one-instruction-per-line listing text plus the parallel line-to-instruction map used for click and highlight resolution.

nodes.name: binary-disassembly.ts
nodes.summary: Thin renderer-side service that decodes a byte range into instructions by calling the main process's native disassembler over the IPC bridge on the binary channels.

nodes.name: BinaryDisassembly
nodes.summary: Service with a single disassemble method that sends bytes, base offset, and architecture to the main-process disassembler channel and returns the decoded instructions.

nodes.name: binary-document.ts
nodes.summary: The binary feature's document model: BinaryDocumentEntry wraps one open binary file with a piece table, a bounded LRU block cache for multi-gigabyte files, undo/redo, in-place and rewrite saves, disk-change reconciliation, and debounced viewport disassembly; BinaryDocuments is the registry that opens, shares, saves, and releases entries and serves as the fallback file opener and unsaved-work source.
nodes.languageNotes: Block cache is 64 KiB blocks capped at 64 resident (~4 MiB) with LRU eviction; format sniffing on the first block drives which disassembly back-end is used.

nodes.name: BinaryDocumentEntry
nodes.summary: Represents one open binary file: signal-based byte access through a piece table over a block cache, overwrite/insert/delete edits with undo/redo snapshots, save-in-place for pure overwrites versus full rewrite, reload on disk change, and windowed disassembly and assembly around the viewport.

nodes.name: BinaryDocuments
nodes.summary: Registry service that opens and reference-counts BinaryDocumentEntry instances per path, reacts to tab closure and disk changes, reports dirty documents as an unsaved-work source, and saves documents on demand.

nodes.name: binary-piece-table.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free piece table for binary documents: represents inserts, deletes, and overwrites as rearranged spans over the original file and an append-only added buffer, supports snapshot/restore for undo, and reports overwrite runs and structural state so pure overwrites can be saved in place.
nodes.languageNotes: The added buffer is append-only, so snapshots capture only the piece list and length — restored pieces still reference valid added ranges.

nodes.name: PieceTable
nodes.summary: Core piece-table implementation: locates logical offsets to original-file or added-buffer bytes, replaces ranges to express edits, snapshots and restores state, detects structural (length-changing) edits, and yields overwrite patches and spans for saving.

nodes.name: insertionIndex
nodes.summary: Binary-search helper returning the piece index and interior offset where a logical offset falls, used by locate and replace to find the affected span.

nodes.name: binary-format.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, dependency-free executable-format sniffing for the binary editor: classifies a file's leading bytes as PE, MZ, ELF, Mach-O, or JVM class, extracts the target architecture, finds the code-section offset to seed disassembly, and renders the human-readable format label shown in the status strip.
nodes.languageNotes: All header reads are bounds-checked DataView accesses; 512 leading bytes suffice because a PE header sits within e_lfanew reach of the first block.

nodes.name: sniffFormat
nodes.summary: Detects a binary's container format and architecture from its magic bytes and header fields, returning a discriminated BinaryFormat union (pe/mz/elf/macho/jvm/unknown).

nodes.name: disassemblyArchitecture
nodes.summary: Maps a sniffed BinaryFormat to the architecture label the native disassembler supports, or null when the format cannot be disassembled.

nodes.name: codeOffset
nodes.summary: Finds the file offset of the executable code section (PE .text or ELF entry section) so disassembly starts at real instructions rather than headers.

nodes.name: describeFormat
nodes.summary: Renders a BinaryFormat as the short human-readable label (for example 'PE · x64') surfaced in the binary status strip.

nodes.name: sniffMachO
nodes.summary: Recognises thin Mach-O magics in either byte order and resolves the CPU type to an architecture label.

nodes.name: sniffPe
nodes.summary: Follows the MZ stub's e_lfanew to the PE signature and reads the COFF machine field and CLR header presence to classify PE binaries (including managed ones).

nodes.name: peCodeOffset
nodes.summary: Walks the PE section table to locate the raw file offset of the first executable code section.

nodes.name: elfCodeOffset
nodes.summary: Walks ELF program/section headers to locate the file offset of the executable code, handling both 32- and 64-bit layouts and endianness.

nodes.name: peArchitecture
nodes.summary: Maps a COFF machine identifier to an architecture label (x86, x64, ARM, ARM64, ...).

nodes.name: elfArchitecture
nodes.summary: Maps an ELF e_machine identifier to an architecture label.

nodes.name: machoArchitecture
nodes.summary: Maps a Mach-O CPU type to an architecture label.

nodes.name: binary-panels.ts
nodes.summary: Signal-backed service owning the docked side-panel state for binary tabs: per-tab visibility and mounted flags for the Disassembly, Inspector, and Agent panels, keyed by tab id and panel kind, with panels staying mounted once shown so their state survives being hidden.

nodes.name: BinaryPanels
nodes.summary: Service exposing reactive isVisible/isMounted accessors and toggle/hide/remove mutations over a map of per-tab panel states, defaulting every panel to closed so a fresh binary tab shows only the hex grid.

nodes.name: binary-status-strip.ts
nodes.summary: Status strip contributed by the binary feature: renders the active binary view's file path, hex cursor offset, selection length, size, sniffed format label, dirty marker, and insert/overwrite mode as status segments, reading the per-view BinaryStatus through the active view's injector.

nodes.name: BinaryStatusStrip
nodes.summary: Component computing the status segments for the active binary tab from the view-scoped BinaryStatus context, formatting byte offsets as hex.

nodes.name: binary-status.ts
nodes.summary: View-scoped service holding one binary view's editor context (path, cursor offset, selection, size, format label, dirty flag, insert mode) for the status strip; provided per binary tab so its lifetime is the view's and nothing needs clearing on tab switches.

nodes.name: BinaryStatus
nodes.summary: Signal wrapper with publish and clear methods over the current BinaryContext, read reactively by the binary status strip.

nodes.name: binary-view.ts
nodes.summary: The binary tab's root view: composes the shared hex BinaryEditor inside a panel layout with the Disassembly, Inspector, and Agent side panels, forwards edit operations and selection/cursor changes to the BinaryDocumentEntry, publishes status-strip context, registers the tab as an agent host with a binary conversation kind, and drives the windowed disassembly around the focus offset.
nodes.languageNotes: Panels are mount-once/hide-inactive via BinaryPanels; agent-host and view-injector registrars follow the shared registration seams.

nodes.name: BinaryView
nodes.summary: Component wiring the hex editor to its document entry: applies edit ops, tracks visible range/selection/cursor to schedule disassembly windows and publish BinaryStatus, and manages side-panel visibility plus agent-host and view-injector registration for the tab's lifetime.

nodes.name: binary.feature.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the binary feature with the application shell: contributes the binary view, ribbon, and status strip to the feature registry, wires BinaryDocuments in as the fallback file opener and an unsaved-work source, and eagerly instantiates the binary agent capabilities so they register with the AI runtime.

nodes.name: provideBinaryFeature
nodes.summary: Builds the environment providers standing the binary feature up at start-up: feature descriptor, BINARY_FILE_OPENER and unsaved-work bindings onto BinaryDocuments, and an initializer instantiating BinaryAgentCapabilities.

nodes.name: code-keybindings.ts
nodes.summary: Catalogues the code editor's keyboard accelerators as a keybinding-catalogue entry consumed by the shared keybindings service.

nodes.name: code-terminal-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Bottom terminal panel embedded in the code editor view, hosting per-editor run terminals through the shared Terminal component with cut, copy, clear, and close controls.

nodes.name: CodeTerminalPanel
nodes.summary: Angular component that renders the editor's run terminal inside a panel arrangement, flushing pending output once the terminal pane reports ready.

nodes.name: code-find-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Find-and-replace adapter binding the shared find panel to a Monaco code editor; computes matches as editor ranges/decorations and drives selection, replace, and undo.

nodes.name: CodeFindAdapter
nodes.summary: Implements the FindAdapter contract over a Monaco editor: recomputes matches on query changes, highlights them with decorations, and supports bounded navigation, replace/replace-all, and undo.

nodes.name: containers-client.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer-side client for the container engine backend: invokes the container IPC channels to list, start, stop, and remove containers and images, query engine status, choose engines, and subscribe to engine events.

nodes.name: ContainersClient
nodes.summary: Injectable service wrapping the container IPC contract with typed methods, an engines signal, and an engine-event subscription for the dashboard.

nodes.name: container-terminals.ts
nodes.summary: Manages interactive shell sessions opened into running containers, creating and disposing terminal-bridge sessions and tracking the active one.

nodes.name: ContainerTerminals
nodes.summary: Injectable service holding container shell sessions as signals: open spawns a docker-exec style pty via the TerminalBridge, activate switches focus, close disposes the session.

nodes.name: containers-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Command registry seam for the Containers feature: the active view registers a handler and ribbon controls invoke start, stop, remove, view-logs, shell, and refresh through it.

nodes.name: ContainersCommands
nodes.summary: Injectable command hub exposing selection-state signals and delegating container actions to whichever view handler is currently registered.

nodes.name: containers-status.ts
nodes.summary: Publishes the running-container count to the application status bar and refreshes it from the containers client when engine events arrive.

nodes.name: ContainersStatus
nodes.summary: Injectable service that registers a status-bar item showing how many containers are running and keeps it current via ContainersClient refreshes.

nodes.name: containers-view.ts
nodes.summary: The Containers dashboard tab: lists containers and images, drives start/stop/remove/logs/shell actions with per-row and ribbon entry points, polls engine readiness, and can launch Docker Desktop when the engine is down.

nodes.name: ContainersView
nodes.summary: Tab view component orchestrating the container dashboard: loads container/image lists, tracks selection for the ribbon commands, opens container shells and log terminals in a panel layout, and retries engine readiness after launching Docker Desktop.

nodes.name: containers.feature.ts
nodes.summary: Feature descriptor wiring the Containers view and its contextual ribbon into the shell's dynamic feature registry; dynamic-imported so the feature lands in its own code-split chunk.
nodes.languageNotes: Dynamic-import feature seam: the shell renders this feature without compiling against it directly (#388 plugin north-star).

nodes.name: markdown-find-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Find-and-replace adapter binding the shared find panel to the Milkdown/ProseMirror markdown editor; scans the document text for matches and applies replacements through editor transactions.

nodes.name: MarkdownFindAdapter
nodes.summary: Implements the FindAdapter contract over a ProseMirror document: scans text nodes for query matches, navigates and selects them, and performs transactional replace, replace-all, and undo.

nodes.name: terminal-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Settings section for the terminal: presents a default-shell dropdown populated from the shells detected on the host and persists the choice through the settings service.

nodes.name: TerminalSettingsSection
nodes.summary: Settings-view section component mapping detected host shells into dropdown options and writing the selected default shell back to settings.

nodes.name: terminal-find-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Find adapter binding the shared find panel to an xterm terminal buffer via the search addon; a search-only surface (no replace or undo) supporting case, whole-word, and regex options.

nodes.name: TerminalFindAdapter
nodes.summary: Implements the FindAdapter contract over a Terminal component's buffer: builds a match list from buffer lines, binds live search results, and navigates matches; replace operations are unsupported by design.

nodes.name: terminal-agents.ts
nodes.summary: Tracks per-terminal-tab agent panel visibility and mount state so an agent side panel keeps its session while its terminal tab is hidden.

nodes.name: TerminalAgents
nodes.summary: Injectable service holding a map of per-tab agent panel states with toggle/show/hide/remove operations, distinguishing visible from merely mounted panels.

nodes.name: terminal-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Command registry seam for terminal tabs: ribbon and menu controls call clear, restart, new-session, clipboard, scroll-lock, navigation, and find operations that the active terminal view's registered handler fulfils.

nodes.name: TerminalCommands
nodes.summary: Injectable command hub exposing active-terminal and scroll-lock state signals and delegating every terminal command to the currently registered view handler.

nodes.name: terminal-status.ts
nodes.summary: Holds the active terminal tab's status-strip context (such as shell and working directory) as a signal for the status bar to render.

nodes.name: TerminalStatus
nodes.summary: Small injectable service with publish/clear operations over a context signal consumed by the terminal's status-strip contribution.

nodes.name: terminal-view.ts
nodes.summary: The Terminal tab view: hosts the shared terminal pane inside a panel layout with an optional agent side panel, registers the terminal command handler and keybindings, and integrates the find panel and status strip.

nodes.name: TerminalView
nodes.summary: Tab view component wiring a Terminal pane to the command seam, keybindings, settings-driven shell selection, the TerminalFindAdapter, per-tab agent panel state, and status publication on tab activation.

nodes.name: find-adapter.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the FindAdapter contract with its FindQuery and FindResultItem types — the seam through which the shared find panel drives per-surface search engines (Monaco, ProseMirror, terminal, workspace) without any engine-specific code.
nodes.languageNotes: Adapter-seam pattern: one shared presentational panel, many per-surface adapter implementations owning all match state.

nodes.name: panel-arrangements.ts
nodes.summary: Service persisting per-layout panel arrangements (edge placement, order, and sizes) to the settings store and applying move and resize mutations before committing them.

nodes.name: PanelArrangements
nodes.summary: Injectable store of named panel arrangements: initializes from persisted settings, exposes arrangement signals per layout key, and commits move/resize-edge/resize-panel mutations back to storage.

nodes.name: panel-drag-handle.ts
nodes.summary: Directive that makes a panel's header a drag handle, forwarding mouse-down to the shared panel-layout drag controller when the panel is draggable.

nodes.name: PanelDragHandle
nodes.summary: Attribute directive resolving its host Panel and beginning a PanelLayoutDrag gesture on mouse-down, using the panel's title for the drag ghost.

nodes.name: panel-layout-context.ts
nodes.summary: Injection token and context contract through which projected Panels resolve their arrangement, flex shares, and divider drags from the owning PanelLayout, avoiding a circular import between the two components.

nodes.name: panel-layout-drag.ts
nodes.summary: Drag controller for the panel-layout system: tracks the ghost position, hot-edge detection, and drop-preview rectangle while a panel header is dragged, and hands the drop edge to the layout on release.

nodes.name: PanelLayoutDrag
nodes.summary: Injectable drag state machine exposing ghost, hot-edge, and preview signals; attaches document-level move/release listeners, measures the workspace, activates past a drag threshold, and invokes the layout's drop handler.

nodes.name: panel-layout-overlay.ts
nodes.summary: Overlay component rendered during a panel drag: draws the drag ghost, directional edge-guide icons, and the drop-preview rectangle over the workspace.

nodes.name: PanelLayoutOverlay
nodes.summary: Presentational component bound to PanelLayoutDrag signals, computing guide icon, rotation, and edge positions for the allowed drop edges.

nodes.name: panel-layout.ts
nodes.summary: The panel-layout host component: stacks projected panels on workspace edges, renders dividers and resize grips, mediates divider and column-width drags, and applies drops from the drag controller through PanelArrangements.

nodes.name: PanelLayout
nodes.summary: Component providing the PanelLayoutContext to projected Panels: computes visible stacks and flex shares, runs divider and edge-resize drag loops with clamping, and persists arrangement changes via PanelArrangements.

nodes.name: panel-types.ts
nodes.summary: Pure model and geometry layer for the panel-layout system: edge and arrangement types, persistence restore/validation, and the move, resize, and pointer hit-test math shared by the layout, drag controller, and overlay.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately class-free pure functions over immutable arrangement objects, keeping layout math independently testable.

nodes.name: constrainPlacementToEdges
nodes.summary: Clamps a persisted placement onto a panel's allowed edges, falling back to the default edge when the stored edge is not permitted.

nodes.name: panelEdgePreview
nodes.summary: Computes the drop-preview rectangle shown when a dragged panel would land on a given workspace edge.

nodes.name: panelEdgeGuideRect
nodes.summary: Computes the on-screen rectangle of an edge's drop-guide icon within the workspace.

nodes.name: resolvePanelEdgeTarget
nodes.summary: Hit-tests a pointer position against the workspace's edge threshold zones to determine which edge a drop would target.

nodes.name: resolvePanelEdgeGuideTarget
nodes.summary: Hit-tests a pointer position against the edge guide icons, returning the guide the pointer is over.

nodes.name: restorePanelArrangement
nodes.summary: Restores a panel arrangement from raw persisted settings data, discarding malformed entries.

nodes.name: normalizeOrders
nodes.summary: Renumbers the panel orders on each edge into a dense zero-based sequence.

nodes.name: movePanel
nodes.summary: Returns a new arrangement with the given panel moved to a target edge and orders normalized.

nodes.name: resizeEdgePanels
nodes.summary: Returns a new arrangement with the panels stacked on an edge resized to a new edge size.

nodes.name: resizePanel
nodes.summary: Returns a new arrangement with a single panel's size changed.

nodes.name: clampPanelWidth
nodes.summary: Clamps a panel width between its minimum and maximum bounds and the available viewport width.

nodes.name: isPersistedPlacement
nodes.summary: Type guard validating that raw settings data has the shape of a persisted panel placement.

nodes.name: panel.ts
nodes.summary: The projected Panel component: declares its identifier, default and allowed edges, and size bounds, resolves placement through the layout context token, and forwards divider presses to the layout.

nodes.name: Panel
nodes.summary: Component representing one dockable panel inside a PanelLayout; reads arrangement and flex share from PANEL_LAYOUT_CONTEXT and begins divider drags through the context contract.

nodes.name: terminal.ts
nodes.summary: The shared <app-terminal> component wrapping xterm.js: creates pty sessions over the TerminalBridge, replays retained scrollback on re-attach, and handles fitting, theming, search, clipboard, scroll lock, exit banners, and session restart.
nodes.languageNotes: Replay-with-sequence-numbers lets a re-attaching pane discard output chunks its scrollback snapshot already contains.

nodes.name: Terminal
nodes.summary: Large component managing the full pty lifecycle for one terminal pane: spawn/restart/terminate, data and exit subscriptions, resize fitting, theme-derived xterm colors, buffer search and text extraction, clipboard operations, and an unavailable-state fallback outside Electron.

nodes.name: terminal-bridge.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer service speaking the pty IPC contract: create, write, resize, dispose, and terminate sessions, list host shells, replay scrollback snapshots, and fan out per-session data and exit events to listeners.

nodes.name: TerminalBridge
nodes.summary: Injectable wrapper over the generic Bridge transport for TerminalChannel: multiplexes the single data channel into per-session listeners and guards every call for non-Electron environments.

nodes.name: terminal-shells.ts
nodes.summary: Loads and caches the list of shells installed on the host from the terminal bridge, exposing them as a signal for shell pickers.

nodes.name: TerminalShells
nodes.summary: Small injectable service that fetches the host shell list once via TerminalBridge.listShells and exposes it as a shells signal.

nodes.name: container-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Names the container IPC channels — the Containers feature's slice of the renderer/main IPC contract, deliberately engine-agnostic so Docker and Podman are peer implementations behind the same channel names.

nodes.name: docker-types.ts
nodes.summary: Normalised container, image, engine-status, and engine-event payload types shared between the main-process container backend and the renderer dashboard; the renderer never sees the engine's wire format.

nodes.name: terminal-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Names the pseudo-terminal IPC channels plus session kinds and creation options shared by the renderer terminal client and the main-process pty manager, including replay and terminate semantics.

nodes.name: title-strip-tab.ts
nodes.summary: Single title-strip tab component: renders icon, label, attention dot and close button, and initiates press-to-activate and drag-to-reorder gestures.

nodes.name: agent-tab-attention.ts
nodes.summary: Service that lights the attention dot on any tab whose agent conversation is waiting on the user, driven from the app-wide pending-requests registry and excluding the active tab.
nodes.languageNotes: Centralised deliberately: per-chat effects missed or leaked dots because chat panels are torn down with the dock, so the requests registry is the one complete source.

nodes.name: api-files.ts
nodes.summary: Service that opens API client documents (.api files) into API Explorer tabs, parsing and validating the ApiDocument JSON payload and recording the file in recent items.

nodes.name: core-menu.ts
nodes.summary: Service contributing the core application menu entries — file open/save, editing roles, view and help commands — built from the Tabs, Documents, Help, and SettingsNavigation services.
nodes.languageNotes: On macOS the native menu is the only binding for clipboard chords, so Cut/Copy/Paste ride as native roles here rather than renderer keybindings.

nodes.name: console-forwarder.ts
nodes.summary: Service that intercepts the renderer's console methods and forwards each entry to the main-process logger over the bridge, while preserving native DevTools output; a safe no-op outside Electron.

nodes.name: display.ts
nodes.summary: Owner of the GPU-rendering display policy: resolves the user's modern-UI-features setting against the main process's GPU recommendation, applies fallback attributes to the document root, and mediates the hardware-acceleration preference and relaunch.
nodes.languageNotes: Outside Electron the recommendation defaults to full effects, so the browser-served build is unchanged.

nodes.name: document-status.ts
nodes.summary: Service holding the status the active document publishes to the well status strip — caret position, end-of-line sequence and encoding for code, or word count and read time for prose.

nodes.name: documents.ts
nodes.summary: Central document store: creates and tracks document entries, opens and saves files (including save-as and save-all), tracks dirty state, watches the disk for external changes and raises conflicts, and syncs content with Monaco models and owning tabs.

nodes.name: editing-chords.ts
nodes.summary: Service handling the Select All chord for plain text inputs directly in the renderer, since a native menu role would steal the accelerator from Monaco, Milkdown, and the terminal.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs in bubble phase after embedded editors have had the keys they own; handled or propagation-stopped events are honoured.

nodes.name: text-input-focus.ts
nodes.summary: DOM helpers that detect whether focus is in a plain text input or textarea and select all text within it, supporting the renderer-side Select All chord.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-exporting the feature registry surface: FeatureRegistry, provideFeature, the feature descriptor types, and the default chrome constant.

nodes.name: file-conflicts.ts
nodes.summary: Service tracking documents that changed on disk while dirty in the editor: raises conflicts, exposes the active conflict per tab, and resolves them by keeping the in-editor version or reloading from disk.

nodes.name: binary-file-opener.ts
nodes.summary: Injection token and interface through which the binary feature contributes its file opener, letting the shared FileOpener route kind-binary files without importing the feature.
nodes.languageNotes: When no implementation is contributed, binary files are simply skipped — the seam degrades gracefully.

nodes.name: file-opener.ts
nodes.summary: Central file-opening router: interactive open dialogs, path routing by classified kind (text, binary, API document, directory), docked document wells versus tabs, and recent-item recording.

nodes.name: help.ts
nodes.summary: Help and About service: gathers version and platform facts for the About dialog, copies a diagnostic summary, and opens the wiki, release notes, and pre-filled issue report in the external browser.
nodes.languageNotes: The issue-form URL carries the version and platform in its query string so bug reports arrive with the facts the About dialog shows.

nodes.name: TitleStripTab
nodes.summary: Renders a single tab and handles press-to-activate, drag-start hand-off to the tab list, and the close button.

nodes.name: AgentTabAttention
nodes.summary: Effect-driven bridge that marks tabs with waiting agent conversations from the pending-requests registry and clears the dot when the request resolves or the tab activates.

nodes.name: ApiFiles
nodes.summary: Opens .api files into API Explorer tabs, parses and validates the ApiDocument JSON (kind and version), holds a pending initial document per tab, and records recents.

nodes.name: CoreMenu
nodes.summary: Registers the core leading and trailing application menu sections, wiring file, edit, view, and help commands to the Tabs, Documents, Help, and SettingsNavigation services.

nodes.name: ConsoleForwarder
nodes.summary: Wraps the native console methods, serializes and truncates each entry, and forwards it to the main-process logger over the bridge while still invoking the native method.

nodes.name: Display
nodes.summary: Applies the GPU display policy to the document root via an effect, exposes the GPU description and reduced-effects recommendation, and toggles hardware acceleration with an app relaunch.

nodes.name: DocumentStatus
nodes.summary: Holds the current document's published status info as a signal, with set and clear operations used by document surfaces feeding the well status strip.

nodes.name: Documents
nodes.summary: Document lifecycle hub: ensures and releases entries, opens files and well documents, tracks dirty state and owning tabs, saves (as/all), watches disk changes, reloads or raises conflicts, and syncs tabs and Monaco models.

nodes.name: EditingChords
nodes.summary: Resolves the platform Select All chord and, when a plain text input is focused, performs select-all in the renderer while leaving embedded editors alone.

nodes.name: focusedTextInput
nodes.summary: Returns the focused element when it is a plain text input or textarea eligible for renderer-side select-all, or undefined otherwise.

nodes.name: selectAllWithin
nodes.summary: Selects the entire contents of the given text input or textarea element.

nodes.name: FileConflicts
nodes.summary: Maintains the list of on-disk conflicts, exposes the active conflict for the current tab, registers per-document resolution handlers, and applies keep, reload, clear, and dismiss actions.

nodes.name: FileOpener
nodes.summary: Routes every open request: interactive dialogs, path-based routing by classified kind to text wells, binary tabs, API documents, or directory views, dock placement and focus, and recent-item recording.

nodes.name: Help
nodes.summary: Builds the About dialog's version facts (app, Electron, Chromium, Node, plugin API, OS/arch), copies the diagnostic summary, controls About visibility, and opens documentation, release notes, and the pre-filled issue form.

nodes.name: terminal.feature.ts
nodes.summary: Feature provider that registers the terminal feature — its view, ribbon, status strip, agent terminal capabilities, and keybindings — with the shared feature registry.

nodes.name: welcome-screen.ts
nodes.summary: Welcome screen component shown at startup: lists recent files and projects with pinning, search, and missing-path recovery, and offers open-file and new-project actions.

nodes.name: directory-status-strip.ts

nodes.name: BinaryEditor

nodes.name: TitleStripTabList

nodes.summary: ProjectSystem implementation for JVM workspaces: detects Gradle or Maven tooling, loads module trees from settings.gradle or pom.xml, and builds the project model and item listing.

nodes.name: NodeProjectSystem
nodes.summary: ProjectSystem implementation for Node.js workspaces: detects package.json roots, expands npm workspaces into member projects, exposes script capabilities, and resolves Node debug targets.

nodes.name: node-workspaces.ts
nodes.summary: Parses the npm workspaces field of a package.json into directory patterns and splits glob patterns into a fixed base and wildcard remainder for expansion.

nodes.name: parseWorkspacePatterns
nodes.summary: Reads the workspaces field of a package.json manifest into a list of directory glob patterns.

nodes.name: splitWorkspacePattern
nodes.summary: Splits a workspace glob pattern into its fixed directory base and wildcard remainder for filesystem expansion.

nodes.name: project-system.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately language-server-agnostic: providers describe structure and callers decide what to do with it.

nodes.name: ProjectSystemRegistry
nodes.summary: Registry of ProjectSystem providers keyed by kind, with lookup by id and matching of a workspace root or project path to the owning provider.

nodes.name: python-project-system.ts
