nodes.name: parsePyprojectName
nodes.summary: Extracts the project name from a pyproject.toml document.

nodes.name: tableName
nodes.summary: Reads a named key from a specific TOML table header section, used to scope name lookups within pyproject.toml.

nodes.name: parseSetupPyName
nodes.summary: Extracts the project name from a setup.py file's setup() call.

nodes.name: parseSetupCfgName
nodes.summary: Extracts the project name from the metadata section of a setup.cfg file.

nodes.name: PythonProjectSystem
nodes.summary: ProjectSystem implementation for Python workspaces: detects manifests (pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg), derives the project name, builds item trees, and resolves debug targets via the venv interpreter.

nodes.name: rust-project-system.ts
nodes.summary: Project-system provider for Rust workspaces that parses Cargo.toml package names and workspace members to model single crates and Cargo workspaces.

nodes.name: parseCargoPackageName
nodes.summary: Extracts the package name from a Cargo.toml [package] section.

nodes.name: parseCargoWorkspaceMembers
nodes.summary: Parses the [workspace] members array of a Cargo.toml into member path patterns.

nodes.name: RustProjectSystem
nodes.summary: ProjectSystem implementation for Rust workspaces: detects Cargo.toml roots, expands workspace members, and models single crates and Cargo workspaces.

nodes.name: solution-folders.ts
nodes.summary: Helpers for .NET solution virtual folders: normalises folder paths and rewrites .sln content to rename a solution folder in place.

nodes.name: normaliseFolderPath
nodes.summary: Normalises a solution-folder path to a canonical separator-delimited form.

nodes.name: renameSolutionFolder
nodes.summary: Rewrites .sln file content to rename a virtual solution folder, updating the project declaration and nested-path references consistently.

nodes.name: archive-provision.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the ArchiveProvision/ArchiveDownload shapes describing per-platform downloadable components with pinned SHA-256 hashes, plus helpers for the current platform key and same-download-everywhere provisions.
nodes.languageNotes: Every download carries a pinned SHA-256 verified before extraction, so tampered archives are never run.

nodes.name: platformKey
nodes.summary: Returns the platform-architecture key identifying the current machine's download variant.

nodes.name: everyPlatform
nodes.summary: Builds an ArchiveProvision that uses the same download descriptor for every supported platform key.

nodes.name: archive-provisioner.ts
nodes.summary: Installs versioned archive-based components (language servers, debug adapters): downloads, verifies, extracts into a version-scoped directory, marks completion, and prunes stale versions.

nodes.name: markComplete
nodes.summary: Writes the completion marker file into an installed component directory.

nodes.name: isComplete
nodes.summary: Checks whether a component directory carries the completion marker from a finished install.

nodes.name: pruneVersions
nodes.summary: Deletes stale versioned install directories of a component, keeping only the specified current version.

nodes.name: ArchiveProvisioner
nodes.summary: Installs a versioned archive component end to end: resolves the platform download, fetches and SHA-256-verifies the archive, extracts it, marks completion, and supports removal.

nodes.name: download.ts
nodes.summary: Low-level provisioning primitives: stream a URL to disk, compute SHA-256 and subresource-integrity digests of a file, and extract tar.gz or zip archives with optional strip-components.

nodes.name: downloadTo
nodes.summary: Streams the response of an HTTPS URL to a destination file on disk.

nodes.name: sha256Of
nodes.summary: Computes the lower-case hex SHA-256 digest of a file.

nodes.name: integrityOf
nodes.summary: Computes a subresource-integrity style digest (algorithm-base64) of a file for lockfile integrity comparison.

nodes.name: extractArchive
nodes.summary: Extracts a tar.gz or zip archive into a destination directory, optionally stripping leading path components.

nodes.name: lockfile-provision.ts
nodes.summary: Parses an npm package-lock.json as a provisioning recipe — a flat list of (path, tarball URL, integrity) triples — with strict validation so an untrusted lockfile cannot describe dangerous paths or hosts.
nodes.languageNotes: Treats the lockfile as the already-resolved dependency tree; nothing resolves version ranges or contacts a registry for metadata.

nodes.name: admits
nodes.summary: Checks whether a value is admitted by an allowlist of exact strings and prefix rules, used to validate lockfile URLs and paths.

nodes.name: parseLockfile
nodes.summary: Parses package-lock.json text into a validated LockfileProvision for the given platform and architecture.

nodes.name: parseLockfileDocument
nodes.summary: Validates an untrusted lockfile document into (path, tarball URL, integrity) package triples, rejecting unconfined paths, unexpected hosts, and applying per-platform optional-dependency filtering.

nodes.name: lockfile-provisioner.ts
nodes.summary: Installs npm-lockfile-described plugin trees by downloading each package tarball, verifying its integrity hash, and extracting it to the lockfile-declared path within a version-scoped directory.

nodes.name: LockfileProvisioner
nodes.summary: Installs an npm-lockfile-described dependency tree: reads and parses the lockfile, then downloads, integrity-verifies, and extracts each package tarball into its declared path within a version-scoped directory.

nodes.name: python-environment.ts
nodes.summary: Manages Python virtual environments for provisioning: detects a supported interpreter, creates venvs, installs and markers packages like debugpy, and resolves a project's own interpreter.

nodes.name: venvPython
nodes.summary: Returns the platform-specific path of the Python executable inside a virtual environment.

nodes.name: detectPython
nodes.summary: Finds a usable Python interpreter, honouring an explicit override before probing well-known executable names.

nodes.name: isSupportedPython
nodes.summary: Runs a candidate interpreter to verify it meets the minimum supported Python version.

nodes.name: isVenvReady
nodes.summary: Checks whether a virtual environment exists and already carries the marker for a required module.

nodes.name: ensureVenvPackage
nodes.summary: Creates the virtual environment if needed and pip-installs a required package into it, writing a marker on success.

nodes.name: removeVenv
nodes.summary: Deletes a virtual environment directory recursively.

nodes.name: projectInterpreter
nodes.summary: Resolves the interpreter of a project's own virtual environment under its root, if one exists.

nodes.name: search-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process search service that spawns ripgrep (via @vscode/ripgrep) over IPC requests, streams JSON-line matches back to the renderer, and confines every search to open workspace roots.

nodes.name: SearchManager
nodes.summary: IPC-registered search service that validates requests, builds ripgrep argument lists, spawns the bundled rg binary, and streams parsed JSON-line matches back to the requesting window.

nodes.name: security-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Owns the renderer security policy: builds and applies the Content-Security-Policy response header per session and manages the user-selectable image-source policy persisted on disk.
nodes.languageNotes: CSP is applied as a response header from the main process rather than a meta tag, surviving strict packaged-build constraints.

nodes.name: SecurityManager
nodes.summary: Builds the Content-Security-Policy header applied to every response, maintains the validated image-source policy, and persists the policy file across sessions.

nodes.name: startup-preferences.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and writes the small set of preferences that must be known before Electron's app-ready event (such as hardware acceleration), stored outside the renderer settings store.

nodes.name: StartupPreferencesStore
nodes.summary: Synchronously reads and writes the pre-app-ready preferences file (such as the hardware-acceleration flag) in the user-data directory.

nodes.name: studio-store.ts
nodes.summary: Persists .studio workspace and user state files over IPC: loads snapshots, saves workspace/user documents, seeds .gitignore entries, and confines writes to open workspace roots.

nodes.name: StudioStore
nodes.summary: IPC-registered store for .studio workspace and user files: loads snapshots, saves parsed documents, seeds .gitignore for user-scoped files, and confines all writes to open workspace roots.

nodes.name: terminal-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process terminal service: creates PTY-backed shell sessions over IPC, tracks scrollback for replay, resolves usable shells per platform, reports session cwd, and kills process trees on dispose.

nodes.name: TerminalManager
nodes.summary: Creates and manages PTY terminal sessions over IPC: spawns shells via node-pty, records scrollback for replay, resolves usable shells per platform, reports cwd (via lsof on macOS), and kills process trees on dispose.

nodes.name: terminal-scrollback.ts
nodes.summary: Retains a bounded scrollback buffer per terminal session so a re-attaching renderer can replay recent output, tracking sequence numbers and exit state.

nodes.name: TerminalScrollback
nodes.summary: Per-session bounded scrollback recorder: appends output chunks with sequence numbers, marks exit, and produces replay snapshots for re-attaching renderers.

nodes.name: terminal-spawn.ts
nodes.summary: Builds the platform-specific spawn specification (executable, args, login-shell flags) for launching a shell or command in a PTY, and gates which input kinds a session accepts.

nodes.name: buildSpawnSpec
nodes.summary: Builds the executable and argument list to spawn a shell or command in a PTY for the given platform, including login-shell and command-wrapping flags.

nodes.name: allowsInput
nodes.summary: Decides whether a terminal session kind accepts the given user input data.

nodes.name: trash-or-remove.ts
nodes.summary: Deletes a file or directory by moving it to the OS trash first, falling back to permanent removal when trashing fails.

nodes.name: trashOrRemove
nodes.summary: Moves a target to the OS trash, falling back to permanent recursive removal when trashing is unavailable or fails.

nodes.name: trusted-paths.ts
nodes.summary: Bounded persistent store of paths the user explicitly opened via an OS dialog, so recent items can be re-authorised across restarts while the hostile renderer cannot open arbitrary paths.

nodes.name: TrustedPaths
nodes.summary: Bounded (500-entry) persistent set of user-chosen paths: remembers dialog-picked paths and answers whether a later open request was genuinely authorised by the user.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the trusted-paths JSON file from disk, tolerating a missing or malformed file.

nodes.name: window-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Creates and tracks the main, auxiliary, and modal Electron windows: applies restored bounds, adopts renderer-opened child windows, persists bounds on move/resize, and manages main-window presence.

nodes.name: WindowManager
nodes.summary: Creates the main window and adopts auxiliary/modal child windows: applies restored bounds via window-state logic, tracks and persists bounds, manages modal backgrounds, and closes secondary windows on shutdown.

nodes.name: window-registry.ts
nodes.summary: In-memory registry mapping Electron window ids to their roles and metadata, with lookups for the main window and enumeration of all tracked windows.

nodes.name: WindowRegistry
nodes.summary: In-memory map of tracked Electron windows with add/remove bookkeeping and lookups by id, entry, main window, and full enumeration.

nodes.name: window-state-store.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and writes per-window persisted state (bounds and flags) to a JSON file on disk, keyed by window name.

nodes.name: WindowStateStore
nodes.summary: Reads and writes named per-window persisted state records to a JSON file in the user-data directory.

nodes.name: window-state.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, unit-testable window-geometry logic: parses stored window state and window.open feature strings, and clamps restored rectangles onto available display work areas so windows never restore off-screen.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors Electron's Rectangle without importing electron, keeping the restore logic pure and unit-testable.

nodes.name: parseStoredWindowState
nodes.summary: Validates an untrusted stored value into a well-formed window state record, rejecting non-finite or malformed geometry.

nodes.name: restoreWindowRect
nodes.summary: Clamps a stored window rectangle onto the available display work areas, ensuring minimum size and that the title strip stays visible so windows never restore off-screen.

nodes.name: parseRequestedPosition
nodes.summary: Parses the requested x/y position from a window.open features string.

nodes.name: parseRequestedSize
nodes.summary: Parses the requested width/height from a window.open features string.

nodes.name: parseNamedSize
nodes.summary: Parses a prefixed size pair (such as minimum dimensions) from a window.open features string.

nodes.name: parseFeatureFlag
nodes.summary: Reads a boolean feature flag from a window.open features string with a fallback value.

nodes.name: parseFeatureText
nodes.summary: Reads a named text value from a window.open features string.

nodes.name: numericFeatures
nodes.summary: Tokenises a window.open features string into its numeric key-value entries.

nodes.name: titleStripVisible
nodes.summary: Checks whether enough of a window's title strip overlaps a display work area to remain grabbable.

nodes.name: targetWorkArea
nodes.summary: Selects the display work area with the greatest overlap with a window rectangle as the restore target.

nodes.name: workspace-context.ts
nodes.summary: Tracks the set of open workspace roots and answers whether a path is confined within one, so every filesystem-touching IPC handler treats the renderer as hostile and refuses out-of-root operations.

nodes.name: WorkspaceContext
nodes.summary: Set of open workspace root paths with confinement checks: add/remove roots, test root identity, and decide whether a path lies within any open root.

nodes.name: workspace-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Central workspace IPC service: opens folders/files via trusted dialogs, performs confined file reads/writes/renames/deletes, loads project and package models through the registries, and detects binary files.

nodes.name: WorkspaceManager
nodes.summary: Central workspace IPC service: opens folders/files through trusted OS dialogs, performs confined reads/writes/renames/deletes with binary detection, and loads project and package models via the registered providers.

nodes.name: worktree-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the worktree IPC channels and delegates each request to WorktreeOperations with logging, wiring git-worktree checkouts into the workspace confinement and trusted-paths stores.

nodes.name: WorktreeManager
nodes.summary: Registers worktree IPC channels and forwards each request to WorktreeOperations with uniform logging and error handling.

nodes.name: worktree-operations.ts
nodes.summary: Implements git-worktree checkout management for unified workspaces: describes repo kind, promotes a repo to worktree layout, adds/opens/removes checkouts, reads status and branches, and persists worktree config.
nodes.languageNotes: Shells out to git via execFile with operand safety checks, and can roll back a failed promotion.

nodes.name: WorktreeOperations
nodes.summary: Implements git-worktree checkout management: describes repository kind, promotes a repo into the worktree layout (with rollback), adds/opens/removes checkouts, reads status and branches, and persists worktree config.

nodes.name: keybinding-catalogue.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the CatalogueBinding and KeybindingCatalogueEntry contracts plus the KEYBINDING_CATALOGUE multi-provider injection token through which each feature contributes its view's accelerators to the shared Keybindings service without the shell naming any feature.
nodes.languageNotes: Angular multi-provider InjectionToken pattern: features contribute entries via provideKeybindingCatalogue and the aggregator injects the token as an array.

nodes.name: provideKeybindingCatalogue
nodes.summary: Wraps one view's keybinding catalogue entry in a multi-provider registration against the KEYBINDING_CATALOGUE token.

nodes.name: monaco-asm-language.ts
nodes.summary: Registers a custom assembly language with Monaco, defining the ASM_LANGUAGE_ID and a Monarch tokenizer so the binary editor's disassembly panel gets syntax highlighting for assembly listings.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards against double registration by checking monaco.languages.getLanguages() before registering.

nodes.name: registerAsmLanguage
nodes.summary: Idempotently registers the assembly language id and its Monarch tokens provider with a Monaco instance.

nodes.name: agent-request-toasts.ts
nodes.summary: Bridges pending agent requests to toast notifications: watches AgentRequests entries against the active tab and a settings gate, raises a toast for agent questions waiting in background tabs, and activates the owning tab when the toast is clicked.

nodes.name: AgentRequestToasts
nodes.summary: Injectable service that computes which agent-request entries deserve a toast (non-active tab, setting enabled), deduplicates already-raised toasts, and routes toast clicks back to Tabs.activate.

nodes.name: open-with.ts
nodes.summary: Routes operating-system 'open with' requests into the editor: subscribes to AppChannel.OpenPath pushes over the bridge, drains paths queued before the renderer was ready via TakePendingOpenPaths, and hands each path to FileOpener.reopenFile.

nodes.name: OpenWith
nodes.summary: Injectable that wires the OS open-path IPC channels in its constructor, disposes the bridge listener on destroy, and opens each received path through the FileOpener.

nodes.name: recent-items.ts
nodes.summary: Signal-backed store of recently opened files and folders, persisted through SettingsStore: records visits with timestamps, supports remove/pin/clear, trims unpinned overflow, and defensively validates raw persisted data on restore.

nodes.name: RecentItems
nodes.summary: Injectable store exposing an items signal with record (upsert with fresh timestamp), remove, togglePin, and clear operations, each committing the trimmed list to both the signal and the persisted SettingsStore.

nodes.name: restoreRecentItems
nodes.summary: Validates raw persisted data field-by-field (kind whitelist, string paths, numeric timestamps) and reconstructs only the well-formed recent items, discarding anything malformed.

nodes.name: scroll-reveal.ts
nodes.summary: Global scroll-reveal service: a capture-phase document scroll listener stamps the scrolling element with an attribute while it scrolls and removes it after a per-element debounce timer, letting CSS reveal scrollbars only during active scrolling.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a capture-phase listener on document so every scrolling container is observed without per-component wiring; cleanup via inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy.

nodes.name: ScrollReveal
nodes.summary: Injectable that marks scroll targets with a data attribute and manages a WeakMap-style timer registry to clear the mark shortly after scrolling stops.

nodes.name: settings-navigation.ts
nodes.summary: Lets any feature deep-link into Settings: open(section) records the requested section in a signal and opens the singleton Settings tab; the settings view then consumes the request to scroll to that section.

nodes.name: SettingsNavigation
nodes.summary: Injectable holding a requestedSection signal with open (set and open the Settings tab) and consume (clear after the settings view honours the request) operations.

nodes.name: status-bar.ts
nodes.summary: Owner-scoped status strip registry: views contribute their StatusSegment lists under an owner key and clear them when deactivated, and the status strip container renders the aggregated segments signal.

nodes.name: StatusBar
nodes.summary: Injectable maintaining a signal map of owner to segments with contribute and clearOwner operations, exposing a derived segments signal for the strip to render.

nodes.name: status-segment.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the StatusSegment interface — id, text, optional icon, and optional hover title — the single contract every feature's status-strip contribution uses.

nodes.name: tab.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the tab model: the TabType union of every top-level tab kind, the AttentionReason type that lets multiple sources claim a tab's attention dot independently, the Tab interface, and the TAB_TYPE_METADATA table mapping each type to its icon and presentation.

nodes.name: tabs.ts
nodes.summary: The application's central tab manager: a signal-backed tab list with open (singleton and resource-reuse semantics), activate, close, rename, reorder, dirty marking, and per-reason attention claims, plus pinned-tab ordering rules.

nodes.name: isPinnedTabType
nodes.summary: Reports whether a tab type belongs to the fixed pinned-tab ordering (tabs that sort ahead of ordinary document tabs).

nodes.name: Tabs
nodes.summary: Injectable managing the tab list and active tab id as signals: open reuses singleton or resource-matched tabs and inserts new ones respecting pin rank; close repairs the active selection; setAttention maintains per-reason claim sets so agent and conflict indicators coexist.

nodes.name: unsaved-work.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the UnsavedWorkSource contract (dirtyDocuments, per-tab dirtyDocumentsFor, save, release) and the UNSAVED_WORK multi-provider token through which document stores contribute themselves, so the Lifecycle service can prompt for all unsaved work at close time without naming any feature.

nodes.name: provideUnsavedWork
nodes.summary: Contributes an existing service class as an UnsavedWorkSource via a multi-provider ExistingProvider registration.

nodes.name: view-injector-registration.ts
nodes.summary: Provides createViewInjectorRegistrar, an effect-driven helper a view component calls to register its Angular injector with ViewInjectors while its tab is active and automatically unregister it on cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Built on Angular's effect() with onCleanup so registration tracks the isActive signal reactively.

nodes.name: createViewInjectorRegistrar
nodes.summary: Injects ViewInjectors and the caller's Injector, then returns a register function that runs an effect binding the injector's registration lifetime to the view's isActive signal.

nodes.name: view-injectors.ts
nodes.summary: Registry mapping tab ids to Angular injectors so dynamically hosted chrome (ribbon and status strip content rendered outside the view's component tree) resolves services from the owning view's injector rather than the root injector.

nodes.name: ViewInjectors
nodes.summary: Injectable holding a signal map of tab id to injector with register (returning an unregister disposer), a computed injectorFor lookup, and token-guarded unregister to avoid clearing a newer registration.

nodes.name: welcome-modal.ts
nodes.summary: Holds the welcome modal's visibility as a signal, exposing open, close, and toggle operations with logging so any surface can show or dismiss the welcome experience.

nodes.name: WelcomeModal
nodes.summary: Injectable exposing an isOpen readonly signal backed by a private openState signal with open/close/toggle mutations.

nodes.name: workbench-agent-capabilities.ts
nodes.summary: Registers the workbench's capabilities with the AI runtime so agents can drive the IDE: open and populate documents, save documents (with save-as fallback), open workspace files by relative or absolute path, and open terminal tabs, resolving language ids and workspace-relative paths along the way.

nodes.name: WorkbenchAgentCapabilities
nodes.summary: Injectable that registers openDocument, saveDocument, openTerminal, and openFile capability handlers with the AI runtime in its constructor; each handler validates agent-supplied arguments, routes through Tabs/Documents/ActiveWorkspace, and normalises paths against the active well's root.

nodes.name: active-workspace.ts
nodes.summary: Tracks workspace context per tab: signal maps of tab id to workspace root path and to document well, with computed rootPath and activeWell views that follow the active tab (falling back to the last well tab), plus set/clear operations for each.

nodes.name: ActiveWorkspace
nodes.summary: Injectable maintaining roots and wells signal maps keyed by tab id, with setWell/clearWell (repairing lastWellTabId on removal) and setRoot/clearRoot operations.

nodes.name: app-channels.ts

nodes.languageNotes: GetDisplayStartup is the one sendSync channel — read by the preload before first paint — while everything else travels over the async Bridge.

nodes.name: binary-channels.ts
nodes.summary: The binary/hex editor's IPC contract: the BinaryChannel enum for disassemble and assemble invokes, the AssembleResult discriminated union, and the DecodedInstruction shape the disassembly renderer consumes regardless of decoder backend.

nodes.name: host.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately types-only: these values are needed before the first paint, so they cannot travel over the asynchronous bridge.

nodes.name: log-channels.ts
nodes.summary: The logging IPC contract shared by renderer and main: LOG_LEVELS and SEVERITIES orderings, the MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH cap, log record payload types, and the consoleLevelToSeverity mapping from console method names to log severities.

nodes.name: consoleLevelToSeverity
nodes.summary: Maps a console method level (log, warn, error, and so on) to the corresponding log severity used by the forwarding pipeline.

nodes.name: plugin-manifest.ts
nodes.summary: The plugin manifest schema and its validating parser: declares PLUGIN_API_VERSION, KNOWN_RUNTIMES, and the manifest type surface (contributions, provisioning, requirements), and implements parsePluginManifest as a hand-rolled reader pipeline that accumulates structured, path-addressed errors instead of throwing.
nodes.languageNotes: Validation is dependency-free and error-accumulating: each read* helper appends to a shared Errors collector so a manifest reports every problem at once. Download and npm-provision readers enforce https URLs and SHA-256 integrity.

nodes.name: isApiCompatible
nodes.summary: Compares a manifest's declared plugin API version against the supported version using parsed semver components to decide compatibility.

nodes.name: readCommand
nodes.summary: Validates a manifest command descriptor: the command string, its argument array, and the optional per-platform command table.

nodes.name: readDownload
nodes.summary: Validates a download provision entry: an https URL, a SHA-256 hash, a known archive kind, and a safe relative executable path (no absolute paths or traversal).

nodes.name: readEntryPoint
nodes.summary: Validates an entry-point path field, rejecting absolute paths and parent traversal so plugin entry points stay confined to the plugin directory.

nodes.name: readNpmProvision
nodes.summary: Validates an npm-lockfile provision: an https lockfile URL, its SHA-256 integrity hash, and the confined entry point.

nodes.name: readProvision
nodes.summary: Dispatches provision parsing by kind (npm versus per-platform downloads), validating platform keys and delegating each platform entry to readDownload.

nodes.name: readContributions
nodes.summary: Parses the manifest's contributions block — language servers and debug adapters — validating each entry's id, display name, languages, priority, and command or entry-point launch shape.

nodes.name: readContributionList
nodes.summary: Generic list reader that validates an array field and applies a per-entry reader callback, collecting the entries that parse successfully.

nodes.name: readRequirements
nodes.summary: Validates the manifest's runtime requirements list against KNOWN_RUNTIMES, recording an error for unknown runtimes or malformed entries.

nodes.name: parsePluginManifest
nodes.summary: Top-level manifest parser: checks API compatibility, reads identity fields, contributions, requirements, and provisioning through the reader helpers, and returns either the parsed manifest or the accumulated error list.

nodes.name: config.ts
nodes.summary: The renderer's Angular ApplicationConfig: wires zoneless change detection, eagerly provides the shell's feature descriptors (agent, code, markdown, terminal, workspace, and friends) and cross-cutting services (open-with, agent-request toasts, unsaved work, console forwarding), and drives registration of the lazily-loaded featureContributions manifest.

nodes.name: feature-contributions.ts
nodes.summary: The renderer's manifest of lazily-loaded features: an array of thunks that dynamic-import api-explorer, containers, model-manager, plugin-manager, and system-monitor feature modules into their own code-split chunks, registered by the driver in config.ts so a new feature needs no shell edits.
nodes.languageNotes: Each entry is a () => import(...) thunk, so bundlers emit a separate chunk per feature and the descriptor resolves at runtime.

nodes.name: global.d.ts

nodes.name: language-select.ts

nodes.name: LanguageSelect

nodes.name: password-field.ts

nodes.name: PasswordField

nodes.name: setting-row.ts

nodes.name: text-field.ts

nodes.summary: Standalone atom wrapping a native input, exposing focus(), emitting value on input plus enter/escape/blurred events, and rendering a leading search icon for the search kind.

nodes.name: debug-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Workspace dock panel hosting the DAP debugger UI: call stack, lazily-loaded variables tree, watch expressions, and execution controls (continue, pause, step, stop).

nodes.name: output-panel.ts

nodes.name: OutputPanel

nodes.name: packages-panel.ts

nodes.name: PackagesPanel
nodes.summary: Standalone component switching between installed and explore modes, sorting and grouping rows for the shared app-table, formatting download counts, and delegating data to the PackageExplorer model.

nodes.name: problems-panel.ts

nodes.name: solution-panel.ts

nodes.name: SolutionPanel
nodes.summary: Standalone component wiring SolutionModel rows into the shared tree view, building context and overflow menus per project, handling rename prompts and restart-confirmation for project actions, and mapping file types to icons.

nodes.name: tree-panel.ts
nodes.summary: File Explorer dock panel: workspace directory tree with git status letters, search filtering, create/rename prompts, delete confirmation modal, and row context menu actions.

nodes.name: TreePanel
nodes.summary: Standalone component projecting Workspace directory nodes into the shared tree view, decorating rows with git status, running new-file/new-folder/rename prompts and delete confirmations, and reporting failures via notifications.

nodes.name: worktrees-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Dock panel managing git worktree checkouts for agent sessions: checkout list with agent state badges, add-worktree modal with branch picking and alias, remove confirmation, and refresh.

nodes.name: WorktreesPanel
nodes.summary: Standalone component listing WorktreeSession checkouts, validating duplicate branches, driving the add/remove modals, and surfacing per-checkout agent state and busy status.

nodes.name: about-modal.ts
nodes.summary: About dialog modal presenting application facts (version, architecture, revision) sourced from the Help service, with copy-to-clipboard feedback.
nodes.languageNotes: Version and arch facts arrive via the synchronous HostEnv startup payload exposed through the Help service.

nodes.name: AboutModal
nodes.summary: Standalone modal component that renders the Help service's fact list, copies the details to the clipboard with a transient 'copied' indicator, and closes via the shared modal shell.

nodes.name: commit-detail.ts
nodes.summary: Source-control commit panel: shows tracked/untracked/conflicted file groups with checkboxes, drives commit and commit-and-push with AI message generation, and handles merge/rebase continue, skip, and abort flows.

nodes.name: CommitDetail
nodes.summary: Panel component managing file staging checkboxes, group expansion, diff opening, discard/stash actions, conflict resolution, and commit message generation against the Repository service.

nodes.name: commit-graph.ts
nodes.summary: Commit history panel rendering the repository log as a lane-based SVG graph with ref badges, computed edge paths, and row selection.

nodes.name: CommitGraph
nodes.summary: Panel component computing lane positions, dot placements, and SVG edge paths for the commit graph, with scroll-into-view row selection.

nodes.name: diff-view.ts
nodes.summary: Dock pane wrapping the shared diff editor to show original-versus-modified file content with change navigation and a diff summary.

nodes.name: DiffView
nodes.summary: Pane component exposing file name, original/modified content, language, and inline-mode inputs, with go-to-diff navigation and change summaries.

nodes.name: issue-agent-confirm.ts
nodes.summary: Confirmation modal shown before dispatching a GitHub issue to the AI agent for automated work.

nodes.name: IssueAgentConfirm
nodes.summary: Modal component that confirms or cancels handing an issue to the IssueAgent service.

nodes.name: issue-document-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Dock panel displaying a forge (GitHub) issue as a document: markdown body and comments, with actions to open it in the agent or externally in the browser.

nodes.name: IssueDocumentPanel
nodes.summary: Panel component resolving the issue and its comments from the issue store, formatting dates, and offering open-in-agent and open-externally actions.

nodes.name: repository-dock-blueprint.ts
nodes.summary: Defines REPOSITORY_DOCK_BLUEPRINT: the dock layout factory composing the source-control sidebar, commit detail, commit graph, terminal, and agent panels into the repository view.
nodes.languageNotes: Blueprint factories run before component constructors, so seeded layout state must live here rather than in panel constructors.

nodes.name: source-control-sidebar.ts
nodes.summary: The source-control sidebar panel: a tree of branches, remotes, tags, stashes, pull requests, issues, and CI runs with full context-menu actions for checkout, merge, rebase, rename, upstream, remotes, tag management, and forge integration.

nodes.name: SourceControlSidebar
nodes.summary: Very large panel component orchestrating branch/tag/stash/remote dialogs, forge pull-request/issue/run rows, per-row context menus, and repository actions through the Repository and ForgeRepository services.

nodes.name: browsableRemoteUrl
nodes.summary: Converts a git remote URL (SSH or HTTPS) into a browser-openable web URL for the hosting forge.

nodes.name: terminal-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Dock panel hosting multiple terminal sessions with tab creation, activation, close, inline rename, and shell selection backed by the terminal-sessions service.

nodes.name: TerminalPanel
nodes.summary: Panel component managing terminal session tabs: create, activate, close, rename, and shell display, gated by panel active state.

nodes.name: tool-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Generic chrome for tool views in the dock: renders a draggable header with icon, title, and optional close button around projected panel content.

nodes.name: ToolPanel
nodes.summary: Wrapper component exposing title, icon, closable, and flush inputs plus a drag handle and close event for hosted tool views.

nodes.name: property-grid.ts
nodes.summary: Editable name/value property grid with draft-row promotion, optional checkboxes, and add/remove/change events, used for key-value style settings tables.

nodes.name: PropertyGrid
nodes.summary: Grid component tracking a draft row, writing edits back through rowChange, and promoting drafts to real rows on completion.

nodes.name: ribbon-strip-actions-button.ts
nodes.summary: Ribbon-strip button that opens a dropdown menu of actions, built on the ribbon menu button and shared menu component.

nodes.name: RibbonStripActionsButton
nodes.summary: Ribbon button component exposing icon, label, and menu items, emitting the selected menu item.

nodes.name: ribbon-strip-split-button.ts
nodes.summary: Ribbon-strip split button pairing a primary action with an adjacent menu trigger, each with its own label and event.

nodes.name: RibbonStripSplitButton
nodes.summary: Split-button component emitting separate action and menu events for its primary and dropdown halves.

nodes.name: status-strip-lsp-menu.ts
nodes.summary: Status-strip popover listing active language servers for the current workspace with per-server status icons and a restart action.

nodes.name: StatusStripLspMenu
nodes.summary: Menu component reading LspStatus and ActiveWorkspace to render server rows with status icons/text and a restart control.

nodes.name: textarea.ts
nodes.summary: Shared multi-line text input atom exposing value, placeholder, variant, and fixed-height inputs plus keyDown/paste/blur outputs for feature forms.

nodes.name: Textarea
nodes.summary: Angular textarea form-control component with signal inputs for value, rows, variant, and disabled state, and programmatic focus support.

nodes.name: toggle.ts
nodes.summary: Shared toggle-switch atom wrapping a boolean checked state with aria labelling and a change event.

nodes.name: Toggle
nodes.summary: Minimal toggle-switch component emitting checked changes and honouring disabled and aria-label inputs.

nodes.name: highlighted-text.ts
nodes.summary: Renders a text string with the portions matching a search query visually highlighted, used by filterable lists and pickers.

nodes.name: HighlightedText
nodes.summary: Component that splits its text input into plain and highlighted segments based on a query string.

nodes.name: app-icon.ts
nodes.summary: The app-icon atom that renders a Phosphor icon token with configurable size, rotation, and colour; the single icon-rendering seam for the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Icon tokens bake in the Phosphor weight, so choosing a token also chooses the visual weight.

nodes.name: AppIcon
nodes.summary: Icon component resolving an Icon token to its glyph with computed size, rotation transform, and resolved colour.

nodes.name: list-view.ts
nodes.summary: Reusable selectable list component with per-row context menus, drag-to-reorder, and empty-state text, built on the shared menu component.

nodes.name: ListView
nodes.summary: List component managing row selection, per-row context-menu resolution, and drag-started/sorted/drop reorder handling.

nodes.name: menu-pointer-guard.ts
nodes.summary: Pointer-movement guard for menus that distinguishes genuine mouse moves from browser re-hit-tests at unchanged coordinates, preventing phantom submenu opens.
nodes.languageNotes: Works around CDK menu-aim re-hit-tests arriving as mousemove events at unchanged coordinates.

nodes.name: MenuPointerGuard
nodes.summary: Zone-aware listener that tracks whether the pointer actually moved since the menu opened, toggling guard state via a renderer-bound mousemove handler.

nodes.name: menu-position.ts
nodes.summary: Exports the MENU_POSITIONS constant: the shared CDK overlay connected-position list used to place dropdown menus consistently.

nodes.name: menu.ts
nodes.summary: The shared dropdown/context menu component rendering MenuItem trees with nested submenus, guarded by MenuPointerGuard and positioned via MENU_POSITIONS.

nodes.name: Menu
nodes.summary: Menu component resolving rows and child submenus from a MenuItem tree and emitting the chosen item on selection.

nodes.name: modal-content.ts
nodes.summary: Structural directive capturing a modal body template so the Modal component can project it into its real-window host lazily.

nodes.name: ModalContent
nodes.summary: Directive that grabs the TemplateRef of the modal's projected content for deferred rendering.

nodes.name: modal.ts
nodes.summary: The modal component that presents its content in a real Electron child window: it mounts the captured template, sizes and clamps the window, copies themed CSS custom properties across, and coordinates backdrop and dismissal.
nodes.languageNotes: Modals are real OS child windows, so themed CSS variables must be resolved to concrete hex colours and copied into the hosted window.

nodes.name: Modal
nodes.summary: Manages the modal lifecycle: presenting into a modal window host, observing content size, clamping requested dimensions to available space, resolving themed colours, and retiring the window on close.

nodes.name: toHexColour
nodes.summary: Normalises a resolved CSS colour value into a hex colour string for transfer into the modal child window.

nodes.name: panel-status.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny presentational shell for the status row rendered at the bottom of dock panels.

nodes.name: PanelStatus
nodes.summary: Content-projection wrapper component providing the standard panel status-bar styling.

nodes.name: panel-toolbar.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny presentational shell for the toolbar row rendered at the top of dock panels.

nodes.name: PanelToolbar
nodes.summary: Content-projection wrapper component providing the standard panel toolbar styling.

nodes.name: agent-conversation-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Dock panel hosting an AI agent conversation: composes the conversation list, chat transcript, and tool strip, wired to the AgentConversation service and visibility-gated by the panel's active state.

nodes.name: AgentConversationPanel
nodes.summary: Panel component binding an AgentConversation context to the agent chat surface, tracking tab identity and active/visible state.

nodes.name: agent-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Thin dock-panel wrapper that embeds the agent conversation panel inside the repository dock layout.

nodes.name: AgentPanel
nodes.summary: Wrapper component exposing the injected DockPanel to an embedded AgentConversationPanel.

nodes.name: folding-placeholder-controller.ts
nodes.summary: Renders Visual Studio-style collapsed-fold placeholders in the Monaco editor by decorating collapsed start lines and expanding a fold when the placeholder is clicked.
nodes.languageNotes: Tracks Monaco hidden-area changes via onDidChangeHiddenAreas and re-derives collapsed lines from fold decorations rather than maintaining parallel state.

nodes.name: foldPlaceholderClass
nodes.summary: Chooses the CSS class for a collapsed-fold placeholder based on the folded line's content, distinguishing comments and region markers from ordinary code.

nodes.name: FoldingPlaceholderController
nodes.summary: Attaches to a Monaco editor instance, maintains a decorations collection marking collapsed fold start lines, and unfolds a region when its placeholder is clicked.

nodes.name: text-editor.ts
nodes.summary: Shared Angular component that wraps a Monaco code editor: creates the editor, wires theme, settings, and zoom reactivity, and exposes an imperative API for text access, selection, paste, and replace operations.
nodes.languageNotes: Zoneless Angular with signals: editor options react to Settings/Theme/EditorZoom via effect() rather than change detection.

nodes.name: TextEditor
nodes.summary: Angular component class that instantiates and manages a Monaco editor lifecycle, exposing getValue/replaceRange/paste/trigger helpers and applying bracket colorization, EOL detection, and layout handling.

nodes.name: block-reorder-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown/ProseMirror plugin enabling drag-and-drop reordering of top-level blocks in the markdown editor, with a drag ghost, drop placeholder, and animated position advancement.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements dragging with manual DOM ghost elements and ProseMirror node decorations instead of native HTML5 drag semantics.

nodes.name: collapse-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown plugin that recognises HTML details/summary blocks in markdown, transforms them into a custom collapsible node with a toggle, and serialises them back to raw HTML.
nodes.languageNotes: Rebuilds the remark AST by pattern-matching <details>/<summary> HTML fragments across sibling nodes before ProseMirror schema mapping.

nodes.name: transformCollapseTree
nodes.summary: Walks a remark tree, detects details open/close HTML markers spanning sibling nodes, and rebuilds the children list with synthesized collapse nodes wrapping the enclosed body.

nodes.name: color-preview-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown plugin that scans document text for CSS colour literals (hex, rgb/rgba, hsl/hsla) and renders an inline swatch widget next to each recognised colour.

nodes.name: parseColor
nodes.summary: Parses a text token against hex, rgb(a), and hsl(a) patterns and returns a normalised CSS colour string, or null when the token is not a valid colour literal.

nodes.name: findColorDecorations
nodes.summary: Traverses the ProseMirror document, locating colour literals in text nodes (skipping code marks) and producing widget decorations that insert a swatch element.

nodes.name: emoji-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Thin Milkdown wrapper registering the remark-emoji transform so shortcodes like :smile: render as emoji in the markdown editor.

nodes.name: footnote-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown plugin adding GFM footnote support: a remark collector gathers footnote definitions and a custom node renders the footnotes section at the document end.

nodes.name: html-image-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown plugin that recognises raw HTML tags in markdown and maps them to a dedicated node type so sized/styled images survive the round trip through the WYSIWYG editor.

nodes.name: media-source.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves relative image sources in the rendered markdown editor to loadable URLs based on the document's directory, using a MutationObserver to rewrite images as they are added, plus a helper to inline files as data URLs.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a MutationObserver on the editor container so dynamically inserted elements get their src rewritten without hooking the renderer.

nodes.name: installImageResolver
nodes.summary: Installs a MutationObserver on the editor container that rewrites relative img src attributes to resolvable media URLs whenever images appear, returning a disposer that disconnects the observer.

nodes.name: fileToDataUrl
nodes.summary: Reads a File object with FileReader and resolves a promise with its base64 data URL, used when pasting or dropping images into the markdown editor.

nodes.name: mermaid-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown plugin rendering mermaid code fences as diagrams: lazily loads the mermaid library, derives a theme configuration from the app's light/dark mode, and renders SVG into a dedicated node view.
nodes.languageNotes: Mermaid is loaded via dynamic import so the heavy library is only fetched when a mermaid fence is actually rendered.

nodes.name: getMermaidConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the mermaid initialization config, selecting theme variables (colours, fonts, contrast) appropriate for the app's current dark or light theme.

nodes.name: renderMermaidDiagram
nodes.summary: Loads mermaid on demand, refreshes its theme, and renders the given diagram source to SVG under a unique element id, returning the SVG markup.

nodes.name: monaco-code-block-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown node-view plugin that hosts a full Monaco editor inside each markdown code fence, syncing edits bidirectionally with the ProseMirror document, handling keyboard escape/collapse, height syncing, and syntax-highlighted placeholders.
nodes.languageNotes: Milkdown nodeView registration is last-registration-wins; this view lazily mounts Monaco per fence and tears it down on a schedule to bound editor instances.

nodes.name: computeChange
nodes.summary: Diffs an old and new string by trimming the common prefix and suffix, returning the minimal replaced span so ProseMirror transactions only touch the changed range.

nodes.name: usesEditContext
nodes.summary: Detects whether an element uses the browser EditContext API, which changes how ProseMirror must treat mutations originating inside the embedded Monaco editor.

nodes.name: MonacoCodeBlockView
nodes.summary: ProseMirror NodeView embedding a Monaco editor per code fence: mounts and disposes editors lazily, forwards edits as minimal transactions, maps arrow-key escapes back to the document, syncs container height, and renders a highlighted placeholder before mounting.

nodes.name: createMonacoCodeBlockPlugin
nodes.summary: Factory that binds the Monaco service and highlighter dependencies and returns the Milkdown plugin registering MonacoCodeBlockView for code_block nodes.

nodes.name: paste-clean-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown paste-transform plugin that sanitises pasted HTML, stripping medium font-weight inline styles that would otherwise be misinterpreted as bold text.

nodes.name: stripMediumFontWeight
nodes.summary: Parses pasted HTML with DOMParser and removes font-weight styles in the medium range so paste does not spuriously produce bold marks.

nodes.name: search-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal Milkdown plugin slice exposing the search integration hook used by the markdown editor's find feature.

nodes.name: subscript-superscript-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Milkdown plugin adding subscript and superscript marks: a remark transform converts inline <sub>/<sup> HTML into marks, and input rules turn ~text~ and ^text^ typing into the corresponding mark.

nodes.name: transformInlineHtml
nodes.summary: Scans a list of remark children for matching inline HTML open/close tag pairs and rewrites the enclosed text into a typed node, powering sub/sup recognition in pasted or authored markdown.

nodes.name: breakpoints.ts
nodes.summary: Signal-based service holding the workspace's debug breakpoints per file path, supporting toggle/add/remove/update, DAP verification results, and persistence through the settings store.
nodes.languageNotes: State is an immutable Map inside an Angular signal; every mutation rebuilds the map and persists a serialisable snapshot.

nodes.name: Breakpoints
nodes.summary: Injectable store for breakpoints keyed by file path: toggles and edits breakpoints, applies and clears debug-adapter verification state, and persists changes to the settings store.

nodes.name: restore
nodes.summary: Rehydrates the persisted breakpoint snapshot into the in-memory map, validating shapes and discarding malformed entries from older stored formats.

nodes.name: diagnostics.ts
nodes.summary: Central diagnostics aggregation service: registers pluggable diagnostic providers (Monaco markers, LSP, build output), merges their results per source, and exposes a sorted merged signal consumed by the Problems panel.

nodes.name: Diagnostics
nodes.summary: Injectable hub that connects diagnostic providers, tracks diagnostics by source, and recomputes a merged, sorted diagnostics list whenever any provider reports changes.

nodes.name: monaco-diagnostics-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Diagnostics provider that mirrors Monaco editor model markers into the Diagnostics service, debouncing marker-change events and excluding LSP-owned markers to avoid duplicates in the Problems panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a shared mirror map so multiple subscribers reuse one onDidChangeMarkers listener; LSP markers are filtered by owner to prevent double reporting.

nodes.name: MonacoDiagnosticsProvider
nodes.summary: Connects to Monaco's global marker change events, collects non-LSP markers into diagnostic records with severity and path mapping, and notifies the aggregation service on a debounce.

nodes.name: editor-commands.ts
nodes.summary: Command-routing service that tracks the active editor handler and dispatches editing operations — cut/copy/paste, undo/redo, find, format, save — to whichever editor surface currently has focus, with a fallback target for text access.

nodes.name: EditorCommands
nodes.summary: Registry of editor command handlers keyed by id: activates or deactivates handlers as focus moves, exposes read/replace text APIs against the active editor, and forwards clipboard, history, find, format, and save commands.

nodes.name: editor-zoom.ts
nodes.summary: Small service holding the shared editor zoom level as a clamped signal, with the discrete zoom steps exported for UI controls like the status strip.

nodes.name: EditorZoom
nodes.summary: Injectable exposing the current editor zoom level signal and a set method that clamps requested levels to the supported range.

nodes.name: editors.ts
nodes.summary: Editor-location registry service mapping file paths to open editor instances and Monaco model URIs, and brokering reveal requests so panels like Problems and Search can jump to a specific file location.

nodes.name: Editors
nodes.summary: Tracks registered editor locations by path, resolves the Monaco model URI for a path, and publishes reveal requests through a signal that editor hosts observe.

nodes.name: font-catalog.ts
nodes.summary: Detects which curated editor/UI fonts are installed on the system by measuring canvas text widths against baseline fonts, and builds the font dropdown options for settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Font availability is inferred by comparing measureText widths against generic-family baselines — no native font enumeration API is used.

nodes.name: FontCatalog
nodes.summary: Runs canvas-based font detection after document fonts are ready, exposes the installed set as a signal, and computes the settings dropdown options including the system default entry.

nodes.name: lsp-settings.ts
nodes.summary: Service managing language-server configuration: loads the server catalogue and installed plugin contributions from the main process, resolves which server handles each language, and persists per-server enablement, executable paths, and argument overrides.
nodes.languageNotes: Server availability merges a static catalogue with installed plugin language-server contributions via the bridge, refreshed when plugin state changes.

nodes.name: LspSettings
nodes.summary: Injectable exposing per-language server resolution, enable/disable toggles, custom paths for Java/dotnet/clangd/TypeScript servers, and argument parsing, persisting all choices through the bridge-backed store.

nodes.name: lsp-capabilities.ts
nodes.summary: Pure helper functions for interrogating LSP server capability payloads: extracting the semantic-token legend, whether save notifications include text, and pull-diagnostics support.

nodes.name: semanticLegendOf
nodes.summary: Extracts the semantic tokens legend (token types and modifiers) from a server's capabilities object, returning undefined when semantic tokens are unsupported.

nodes.name: saveIncludesText
nodes.summary: Determines from server capabilities whether didSave notifications should include the full document text.

nodes.name: supportsPullDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Checks whether the server advertises a diagnostic provider, enabling the client's pull-diagnostics flow.

nodes.name: lsp-client.ts
nodes.summary: The renderer-side LSP client orchestrator: manages server session lifecycle per language/root, syncs document open/change/save/close over the bridge, ingests published and pulled diagnostics into Monaco markers, handles restarts, suspension, start-failure cooldowns, and re-colours sessions on init.
nodes.languageNotes: Serialises all document operations through a per-document queue; guards against the known infinite retry loop by never re-enqueueing syncDocument on an empty catalogue.

nodes.name: LspClient
nodes.summary: Large injectable coordinating language-server sessions: ensures/starts sessions with cooldown and block reasons, queues document sync operations, maps LSP diagnostics to Monaco markers, schedules recolor and reassociation after init, and routes server logs to the Output channel.

nodes.name: lsp-diagnostic-mapper.ts
nodes.summary: Pure mapping functions converting LSP diagnostics into the app's diagnostic records and into Monaco marker data, including severity translation in both directions.

nodes.name: severityOf
nodes.summary: Maps an LSP numeric severity to the app's diagnostic severity enum, defaulting sensibly for unknown values.

nodes.name: markerSeverityOf
nodes.summary: Maps an LSP severity to the corresponding Monaco MarkerSeverity constant for editor squiggle rendering.

nodes.name: toDiagnostic
nodes.summary: Converts a single LSP diagnostic plus document context into the app's diagnostic record, translating the URI to a path and extracting the basename for display.

nodes.name: toMarkerData
nodes.summary: Converts a list of LSP diagnostics into Monaco IMarkerData entries with translated severities and one-based ranges.

nodes.name: lsp-features.ts
nodes.summary: Registers Monaco language feature providers backed by LSP servers — semantic tokens, completion, hover, definition, and references — remapping server token legends onto the app's fixed legend and falling back to heuristic tokenisation for languages without a server.

nodes.name: LspFeatures
nodes.summary: Injectable that wires Monaco provider registrations to LSP requests over the bridge, converting completion items, hovers, and locations, remapping semantic token types/modifiers, and rebasing heuristic tokens when servers cannot supply them.

nodes.name: lsp-marker-owner.ts
nodes.summary: Single shared constant naming the Monaco marker owner used for LSP-sourced markers, so the Monaco diagnostics provider can exclude them and avoid duplicate Problems entries.

nodes.name: lsp-paths.ts
nodes.summary: Pure path/URI helpers for the LSP client: normalising separators, converting between file paths and file:// URIs, and containment checks used when scoping servers to workspace roots.

nodes.name: lsp-status.ts
nodes.summary: Injectable registry tracking each language server's lifecycle state (starting/ready/unavailable) and progress for the status strip, with a 120s readiness watchdog that unlocks a manual restart affordance for stalled servers.
nodes.languageNotes: Readiness is inferred behaviourally (first diagnostics or answered request); the watchdog never declares failure, it only surfaces the stall.

nodes.name: lsp-text-sync.ts
nodes.summary: Pure text-synchronisation helpers computing the minimal LSP replace edit between two document versions, kept free of Angular and Monaco imports for direct unit testing.

nodes.name: milkdown.ts
nodes.summary: Injectable service exposing Milkdown markdown-editor presentation settings (CSS custom properties, font resolution, margins, image sizing/alignment) derived reactively from application settings.

nodes.name: monaco-folding.ts
nodes.summary: Custom Visual Studio-style folding provider for Monaco: computes brace-based, #region, and comment-block folding ranges from tokenized model lines.

nodes.name: monaco-heuristic-tokens.ts
nodes.summary: Heuristic semantic-token builder that colours type and method identifiers for languages whose bundled Monarch tokenizer leaves them plain (C#, Java, Kotlin, Rust, Go, C/C++).

nodes.name: monaco-highlighter.ts
nodes.summary: Shared injectable that colorizes code strings through Monaco's tokenizer for non-editor surfaces (markdown code fences, code blocks), resolving language aliases to registered Monaco language ids.

nodes.name: monaco-languages.ts
nodes.summary: Static language catalogue mapping file extensions and file names to Monaco language ids and back, backing editor language detection across the app.

nodes.name: monaco-themes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Studio's light and dark Monaco editor themes, deriving token colours and the accent-tinted selection colour from the app's CSS custom properties.

nodes.name: monaco.ts
nodes.summary: Central injectable that lazily loads the AMD Monaco editor, registers languages, themes, VS-style folding and heuristic semantic tokens, and produces themed editor/diff-editor option sets for every editor surface in the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Monaco is loaded via its AMD loader script rather than ESM, so registration happens imperatively after a load promise resolves.

nodes.name: language-support-prompt.ts
nodes.summary: Injectable that offers a one-time notification prompting the user to install language-support plugins (e.g. a language server) when a file of an unsupported language is opened.

nodes.name: plugin-consent.ts
nodes.summary: Signal-based state machine for the plugin install consent modal: exposes the pending question and resolves the caller's promise when the user accepts or declines.

nodes.name: plugins.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer-side plugin catalogue service: lists known plugins with install state over the IPC bridge, and performs consent-gated install, uninstall, and slot actions while tracking busy/error state.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: Thin renderer client for workspace search: invokes the main process over the IPC bridge to run ripgrep-backed searches and list workspace files for the composer's @-mention picker.

nodes.name: LspStatus
nodes.summary: Tracks per-server lifecycle entries with signals: registers servers, updates progress/state, arms and clears the readiness watchdog, and issues restarts through the LSP settings service.

nodes.name: minimalReplaceEdit
nodes.summary: Computes the smallest single replace range between the previous and next document text by trimming the common prefix and suffix, avoiding full-document sync on each keystroke.

nodes.name: positionAt
nodes.summary: Converts a character offset into a zero-based LSP line/character position by scanning line breaks in the text.

nodes.name: Milkdown
nodes.summary: Derives Milkdown editor presentation state from settings: builds the CSS custom-property map and resolves the proportional and monospace font families.

nodes.name: registerBraceFolding
nodes.summary: Registers the custom folding-range provider for all supported languages so Monaco uses VS-style brace, region, and comment folding.

nodes.name: computeFoldingRanges
nodes.summary: Entry point that tokenizes the model and merges brace, #region, and comment-block ranges into the final folding-range list.

nodes.name: braceRanges
nodes.summary: Scans tokenized lines for brace pairs outside strings and comments, pairing opening and closing braces via a stack to produce fold ranges.

nodes.name: toBraceRange
nodes.summary: Converts a matched brace pair into a Monaco folding range, choosing the start line so the collapsed placeholder reads like Visual Studio's.

nodes.name: regionRanges
nodes.summary: Finds #region/#endregion style marker pairs per language and emits Region-kind folding ranges.

nodes.name: commentRanges
nodes.summary: Groups consecutive whole-line comment lines into Comment-kind folding ranges using token classification.

nodes.name: isCommentLine
nodes.summary: Determines whether an entire line is a comment by checking that every non-whitespace token on it is comment-typed.

nodes.name: tokenTypeAt
nodes.summary: Finds the token type covering a given column within a tokenized line.

nodes.name: buildHeuristicSemanticTokens
nodes.summary: Builds delta-encoded semantic tokens by pattern-matching Monarch-tokenized lines, classifying capitalised identifiers as types and call-position identifiers as functions.

nodes.name: MonacoHighlighter
nodes.summary: Colorizes code snippets via Monaco's tokenizer for non-editor hosts, lazily building an alias map (e.g. 'js' → 'javascript') and falling back to plain text on failure.

nodes.name: languageForFileName
nodes.summary: Resolves the Monaco language id for a file name, checking exact special-cased names (e.g. Dockerfile) before falling back to the extension map.

nodes.name: accentSelectionHex
nodes.summary: Blends the accent RGB toward the editor background at fixed alpha to produce an opaque selection colour hex Monaco can use.

nodes.name: defineThemes
nodes.summary: Defines the studio-light and studio-dark Monaco themes, mapping token rules and editor UI colours from the app's gray ramp and accent selection colour.

nodes.name: Monaco
nodes.summary: Owns the Monaco lifecycle: loads the AMD bundle once, registers ASM language, themes, folding, and heuristic semantic tokens, suppresses built-in diagnostics where LSP servers take over, and derives editor/diff options from settings and theme.

nodes.name: LanguageSupportPrompt
nodes.summary: Offers install prompts for uninstalled language-support plugins when a language is first encountered, remembering which languages were already offered to avoid nagging.

nodes.name: PluginConsent
nodes.summary: Promise-backed consent gate: request() exposes a pending question to the consent modal and resolves once accept() or decline() settles the user's answer.

nodes.name: Plugins
nodes.summary: Manages the plugin catalogue over IPC: refreshes the known-plugin list, runs consent-gated installs, uninstalls, and generic plugin actions, exposing busy and error signals for the UI.

nodes.name: Search
nodes.summary: Invokes workspace search and file listing on the main process via the bridge, logging failures and returning empty results on error.

nodes.name: security.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer client for the security IPC channels: reads and updates the main-process-owned image-source Content-Security-Policy, exposing the current policy as a signal.

nodes.name: settings-migration.ts
nodes.summary: Settings persistence migrations: restores raw stored overrides into the current profile-aware format, migrating legacy flat settings and older AI connection shapes forward.

nodes.name: settings-profiles.ts
nodes.summary: Pure helpers for per-language editor profiles: add, update, and remove profiles, and resolve the effective text-editor settings for a language by layering profile overrides on globals.

nodes.name: settings-registry.ts
nodes.summary: The data-driven settings registry: declares every setting's key, default, and section metadata (application, appearance, editors, AI, workspaces), plus derived lookup maps and defaults consumed by the Settings service and settings UI.
nodes.languageNotes: Almost entirely declarative data; the registry drives both persistence defaults and the generated settings UI.

nodes.name: settings-schema.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the settings registry schema: setting definitions, control kinds, choice options, and section metadata that the registry instantiates and the settings view renders.

nodes.name: settings.ts
nodes.summary: The central Settings service: loads and validates persisted overrides, exposes typed reactive accessors for every registry key, and provides mutation APIs for application, appearance, editor-profile, markdown, workspace, and AI settings including connections and tool policies.
nodes.languageNotes: Backed by per-key signals so consumers can react to individual settings without a global settings change notification.

nodes.name: problem-matcher.ts
nodes.summary: Problem matchers for task output: built-in regex matchers for .NET compiler, GCC, and javac diagnostics, with a parser that extracts and de-duplicates problems from build output text.

nodes.name: accent-color.ts
nodes.summary: Pure colour-math helpers for the accent-colour system: HSL/RGB/hex conversions, hue normalisation, and saturation clamping used by theming and the accent picker.

nodes.name: theme.ts
nodes.summary: Theme service applying light/dark mode and the accent colour to the document: normalises persisted accent values (presets or custom hue), tracks the system dark-mode preference, and persists choices through the settings store.

nodes.name: lsp-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral LSP IPC contract shared by renderer and main: names every lsp:* channel and the payload types for server lifecycle, document sync, features, and semantic tokens; main owns server lifecycles so the renderer can only reference servers by id.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately free of Node and DOM dependencies so both Electron compilation targets can import it.

nodes.name: plugin-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral plugin IPC contract: names the plugins:* channels and payload types for the three-layer model (catalogue = available, install state = installed, user choice = which installed contribution fills each slot).

nodes.name: search-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Workspace-search IPC contract: names the search:run and search:list-files channels and their payload types; search runs in main because it shells out to a bundled ripgrep binary.

nodes.name: security-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Security IPC contract naming the image-source policy get/set channels; the policy is owned by main, which builds the CSP header before page load.

nodes.name: Security
nodes.summary: Reads the current image-source CSP policy on construction and lets settings UI update it, reflecting availability and the active policy through signals.

nodes.name: restoreOverrides
nodes.summary: Entry point that takes raw persisted settings and returns them in the current profile-aware format, applying legacy and AI-connection migrations as needed.

nodes.name: migrateAiConnections
nodes.summary: Rewrites older persisted AI connection shapes into the current AiConnection format inside the overrides object.

nodes.name: migrateLegacy
nodes.summary: Converts the pre-profile flat settings format into the profile-aware structure, preserving user overrides.

nodes.name: addProfile
nodes.summary: Creates a new editor profile with a generated id for the given languages and settings, returning the extended profile list.

nodes.name: resolveForLanguage
nodes.summary: Resolves effective text-editor settings for a language by layering the first matching profile's overrides on top of the global settings.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: Loads, validates, and persists all application settings; exposes per-key reactive signals plus typed mutators for application, appearance, text/markdown editor, workspace, and AI settings (connections, models, permission postures, tool policies, path and network allowlists).

nodes.name: parseProblems
nodes.summary: Runs each problem matcher's regex across task output lines, mapping captures to diagnostics and de-duplicating identical problems.

nodes.name: hslToRgb
nodes.summary: Converts an HSL colour to RGB channels using the standard hue-to-channel formula.

nodes.name: hexToRgb
nodes.summary: Parses a 3- or 6-digit hex colour string into RGB channels, returning undefined for invalid input.

nodes.name: rgbToHsl
nodes.summary: Converts RGB channels to HSL, computing hue from the dominant channel and lightness/saturation from the min-max range.

nodes.name: normaliseAccent
nodes.summary: Normalises a persisted accent value into a valid preset id or custom hue/saturation object, falling back to the default accent for unrecognised input.

nodes.name: resolveAccent
nodes.summary: Resolves an accent choice (preset id or custom HSL) to the concrete colour values applied to the document.

nodes.name: Theme
nodes.summary: Applies mode and accent to the document root, follows the system dark-mode preference when mode is 'system', and persists mode/accent changes through the settings store.

nodes.name: installedContributions
nodes.summary: Filters a plugin list down to the installed plugins' contributions for a given slot, supporting the choose-among-installed layer of the plugin model.

nodes.name: icon.ts
nodes.summary: Central icon catalogue: the Icon token class mapping every named glyph used across Studio (window chrome, editors, git, agent, dock, settings) to its Phosphor icon and weight.
nodes.languageNotes: Each static Icon token bakes in a Phosphor weight, so picking a token picks a weight — features never choose weights independently.

nodes.name: Icon
nodes.summary: Enum-like class exposing roughly 250 static Icon tokens (SETTINGS, CLOSE, GIT_COMMIT, AGENT, SPINNER, and so on) consumed by app-icon renderers throughout the UI.

nodes.name: severity-icon.ts
nodes.summary: Maps a notification severity to its Icon token so toasts and the notifications menu render severity consistently.

nodes.name: severityIcon
nodes.summary: Returns the filled Icon token (error, warning, info, success) for a given notification severity.

nodes.name: dock-panel.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the DockPanel interface: the metadata the dock chrome renders (id, title, icon, stack role) and the component projected into the panel body by the panel registry outlet.

nodes.name: issue-agent.ts
nodes.summary: Service that starts an AI agent session on a forge issue: confirms replacing an in-progress chat, opens a new conversation, sends a generated issue prompt, and reveals the agent panel.

nodes.name: IssueAgent
nodes.summary: Injectable orchestrating the open/confirm/dismiss flow: if the agent already has messages it awaits user confirmation before starting a fresh chat seeded with the issue prompt.

nodes.name: agentPromptFor
nodes.summary: Builds the natural-language prompt handed to the agent for a forge issue, including the repository reference and issue details.

nodes.name: issue-store.ts
nodes.summary: Signal-backed store of opened forge issues keyed per repository and issue number, tracking comment loading state, comment errors, and pruning issues no longer present upstream.

nodes.name: IssueStore
nodes.summary: Injectable holding a Map signal of OpenIssue entries with put/patch/get/has APIs, comment loading and error transitions, and removeMissing reconciliation against a fresh issue list.

nodes.name: notifications.ts
nodes.summary: Central notifications service managing the toast and history signals: severity-ordered insertion, capacity eviction, keyed dismissal, seen tracking for the bell badge, and clear-all.

nodes.name: Notifications
nodes.summary: Injectable exposing notify/dismiss/dismissByKey/dismissAll plus history APIs (markAllSeen, removeFromHistory, clearAll), inserting toasts by severity and evicting the lowest-priority toast when full.

nodes.name: language-names.ts
nodes.summary: Maps Monaco language identifiers to human display names, shared so the Plugin Manager, install offers, and settings tree all name a language the same way.

nodes.name: languageDisplayName
nodes.summary: Returns a language's display name from the shared table, falling back to the raw identifier for unknown languages.

nodes.name: shell-labels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-aware command labels for revealing and opening paths in the OS file manager (Finder, File Explorer, File Manager), shared so every panel names the command consistently.

nodes.name: shell.ts
nodes.summary: Renderer-side shell client: invokes OS open-path, open-external-URL, and reveal-path operations over the IPC bridge using the ShellChannel contract.

nodes.name: Shell
nodes.summary: Injectable with openPath, openExternal, and revealPath methods that log and forward each request through the Bridge to the main-process shell handler.

nodes.name: agent-conversation-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral IPC contract for persisted agent conversations: channel names (list, load, save, update-meta, delete), context scoping types, agent-kind metadata, and conversation summary shapes shared by main and renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately types-and-constants only (no Node or DOM dependencies) so both the Electron main and Angular renderer compilation targets can import it.

nodes.name: contextIdOf
nodes.summary: Derives the stable string identifier for a conversation context, used to scope conversation storage and listing.

nodes.name: forge-types.ts

nodes.languageNotes: A deliberately provider-neutral model rather than GitHub's own JSON, so a second forge implementation changes nothing downstream; credentials never appear in these shapes.

nodes.name: shell-channels.ts
nodes.summary: Names the OS-shell IPC channels (open path, open external URL, reveal path) shared by the renderer's shell client and the main-process handler, which validates every target.

nodes.name: status-strip-notifications-menu.ts

nodes.name: StatusStripNotificationsMenu
nodes.summary: Angular component behind the status-strip bell: marks history seen on open, removes or clears entries via the Notifications service, and formats severity icons and relative times.

nodes.name: status-strip-tasks-menu.ts
nodes.summary: Status-strip menu showing running agent background tasks with elapsed-time detail and reveal/stop controls per task.

nodes.name: StatusStripTasksMenu
nodes.summary: Angular component listing the AgentTasks service's running tasks, delegating reveal and stop actions to it and rendering elapsed time and task detail strings.

nodes.name: title-strip-button-list.ts
nodes.summary: Title-strip button cluster that opens the Settings tab, the Mission Control tab, and the new-tab welcome modal, alongside the app menu and tab overflow menu.

nodes.name: TitleStripButtonList
nodes.summary: Angular component exposing openSettings, openMissionControl, and openNewTab actions that route through the Tabs service and the WelcomeModal service.

nodes.name: title-strip-button.ts
nodes.summary: Reusable title-strip icon button atom with icon, tooltip label, optional rotation, disabled state, and an action output.

nodes.name: TitleStripButton
nodes.summary: Presentational button component that emits its action output on click, used as the building block for title-strip controls.

nodes.name: title-strip-container.ts
nodes.summary: Top-level title strip composing the tab list, button cluster, optional window-lock toggle, and window controls into the app's custom window chrome.

nodes.name: TitleStripContainer
nodes.summary: Container component wiring the window-lock setting through the WindowLock service and gating whether the lock toggle is shown.

nodes.name: title-strip-menu.ts
nodes.summary: In-window application menu renderer: converts the AppMenu model into CDK flyout menu rows with human-readable accelerators and dispatches selected commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Formats Electron-style accelerators (CmdOrCtrl+…) into platform glyphs (⌘⇧⌥⌃) on macOS via userAgent sniffing.

nodes.name: TitleStripMenu
nodes.summary: Angular component that recursively maps AppMenu sections to renderable rows, formats accelerators per platform, and dispatches selections back to the AppMenu service.

nodes.name: title-strip-tab-menu.ts
nodes.summary: Overflow menu in the title strip grouping open tabs by type metadata, allowing tab activation and closing from a dropdown.

nodes.name: TitleStripTabMenu
nodes.summary: Angular component that computes tab groups from the Tabs service and delegates activation to Tabs and closing to TabCloser.

nodes.name: window-controls.ts
nodes.summary: Minimize, maximize/restore, and close window buttons for custom window chrome, delegating each action to the Studio bridge service.

nodes.name: WindowControls
nodes.summary: Angular component invoking Studio.minimizeWindow, toggleMaximizeWindow, and closeWindow, shown only when visible (non-macOS chrome).

nodes.name: table.ts
