nodes.summary: Styles the password-field atom at a 16rem default width using the shared control height and themed form-control chrome, matching the other single-line inputs.

nodes.name: radio.html
nodes.summary: Template for the radio button form atom: a native radio input bound to checked/disabled/name signals with an aria-label for accessibility.

nodes.name: radio.scss
nodes.summary: Custom-draws the radio button with appearance:none — a themed circle whose inner dot is revealed when selected, with hover, focus-accent, and disabled states.
nodes.languageNotes: Replaces the native radio rendering entirely (appearance: none) and paints the selected dot via a pseudo-element.

nodes.name: setting-row.html
nodes.summary: Template for the setting-row layout atom: a label/description text block on the left with a single projected form control on the right, wrapped in a label element so clicking the text activates the control.
nodes.languageNotes: The label wraps the projected control via ng-content for runtime association; a lint suppression documents that the rule cannot verify this statically.

nodes.name: setting-row.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the setting-row as a flex row with label text and control pushed to opposite ends, with a stacked label/description column that truncates gracefully.

nodes.name: slider.html
nodes.summary: Template for the slider form atom: a native range input bound to min/max/step/value/disabled signals, with a caller-supplied track gradient passed through the --slider-track CSS custom property.

nodes.name: slider.scss
nodes.summary: Custom-draws the range slider track and thumb with appearance:none; the track paints a caller-supplied gradient (e.g. a hue spectrum) via --slider-track, falling back to the neutral form track color.
nodes.languageNotes: Styles the WebKit vendor pseudo-elements (::-webkit-slider-runnable-track / -thumb) directly, which is safe in an Electron-only app.

nodes.name: text-field.html
nodes.summary: Template for the text-field form atom: a native text/search input with an optional in-box search glyph (app-icon), emitting enter/escape/blur events alongside the input handler.
nodes.languageNotes: In search mode the glyph is rendered inside the field so icon and input read as one control rather than an icon parked beside an input.

nodes.name: text-field.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the text-field atom at the shared control height with themed chrome, including the search-variant layout that insets the input text to make room for the in-box glyph.

nodes.name: textarea.html
nodes.summary: Template for the textarea form atom: a native textarea supporting seamless and fixed-height variants, forwarding keydown, paste, and blur events for composer-style consumers.
nodes.languageNotes: Fixed-height mode sets block-size in lh units so the height tracks the row count exactly.

nodes.name: textarea.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the textarea atom with the same chrome as the single-line text field so the two never drift apart, plus seamless (chrome-free) and fixed-height variant rules.

nodes.name: toggle.html
nodes.summary: Template for the toggle form atom: a native checkbox with role=switch, bound to checked/disabled signals with an aria-label for accessibility.

nodes.name: toggle.scss
nodes.summary: Custom-draws the toggle as a sliding pill switch with appearance:none — themed track, animated thumb, and a transparent border at rest that recolors to the accent on focus.

nodes.name: highlighted-text.html
nodes.summary: Template for the highlighted-text component: iterates match segments and wraps matching spans in a mark element, used to highlight filter/search hits in tree and list names.

nodes.name: app-icon.html
nodes.summary: Template for the app-icon atom: a single aria-hidden i element whose class list, font size, color, and transform are all driven by the component's icon-token signals.

nodes.name: app-icon.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the app-icon atom to center the glyph in whatever box the host is given, with a short transform transition so state-driven rotations (like an expanding caret) animate for free.
nodes.languageNotes: The glyph element is made inline-block because rotation transforms have no effect on inline elements.

nodes.name: list-view.html
nodes.summary: Template for the shared list-view component: a CDK drop-list of selectable rows with optional y-axis drag-reordering via a grip handle, per-row context menus through a single shared app-menu, templated row content, and an empty-state message.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets cdkDragPreviewContainer="parent" so the drag-preview clone stays inside the list and consumer-scoped row styling keeps applying, preventing the grip from sliding out from under the cursor.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel file re-exporting the MarkdownEditor component as the markdown-editor module's public surface.

nodes.name: markdown-editor.html
nodes.summary: Template for the Milkdown-backed markdown editor: a scroll container around a document-width wrapper whose margin, image-sizing, and image-alignment classes are signal-driven, with an inner container the editor mounts into imperatively.

nodes.name: markdown-editor.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the markdown editor's scroll container and document-width wrapper, with a theme-switched surface background; the Milkdown DOM itself is themed globally because it lives outside view encapsulation.
nodes.languageNotes: Establishes a container query context so the document width responds to the pane, and uses :host-context([data-theme-mode='dark']) to switch the surface color.

nodes.name: markdown-view.html
nodes.summary: Template for the read-only markdown view: iterates parsed blocks, rendering prose blocks via sanitized innerHTML and code blocks through the app-code-block component.

nodes.name: markdown-view.scss
nodes.summary: Small companion stylesheet for the shared markdown-view component, styling the host container for rendered markdown content.

nodes.name: menu.html
nodes.summary: Template for the app's shared popup menu: a single recursive ng-template surface built on CDK Menu that renders rows, separators, checkable items, tones, and nested submenus from one item tree. Documents the hard constraint that cdkMenu must remain the template's root node or CDK degrades it to an inline menu.
nodes.languageNotes: Recursive template instantiation via cdkMenuTriggerFor pointing back at its own ng-template; trigger data rides along as $implicit so deep submenu rows still act on the original subject.

nodes.name: menu.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the shared popup menu component's host element.

nodes.name: modal-window-host.scss
nodes.summary: Stylesheet for the host that renders modal content inside a real Electron child window: flattens the former in-document dialog card against the window edges, clears the platform window controls with a drag-strip-aware padding, and distinguishes measured (natural-height) modals from filling (whole-surface) modals.
nodes.languageNotes: Reuses the caller's --modal-panel-* custom properties so per-caller modal theming survives the move from in-document overlay to a real OS window; a :only-child selector lets a lone child claim the fill slack.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel for the panel-layout side-panel system, re-exporting the Panel, PanelArrangements, PanelDragHandle, and PanelLayout components together with the PanelArrangement, PanelEdge, and PanelPlacement types.

nodes.name: panel-status.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the panel-status component, styling the status strip shown within a panel.

nodes.name: panel-toolbar.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the shared panel toolbar strip used at the top of tool panels, including the spacer that pushes trailing controls to the end.

nodes.name: agent-conversation-panel.html
nodes.summary: Template for the agent conversation panel: renders the agent tool strip, then swaps between the conversation history list and the active agent chat depending on whether history is open.

nodes.name: agent-conversation-panel.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the agent conversation panel, laying out the tool strip and the panel body.

nodes.name: agent-panel.html
nodes.summary: One-line template for the agent panel that simply hosts the agent conversation panel component.

nodes.name: agent-panel.scss
nodes.summary: Minimal companion stylesheet for the agent panel host.

nodes.name: commit-detail.html
nodes.summary: Template for the source-control commit detail panel: a toolbar of repository actions (refresh, discard all, show diff, stash, expand/collapse all), an error notice, an in-flight merge/rebase operation banner with its resolution actions, and the selected commit's detail view.

nodes.name: commit-detail.scss
nodes.summary: Large companion stylesheet for the commit detail panel, styling the toolbar, error notice, in-flight operation banner, and the commit metadata and changed-file tree sections.

nodes.name: commit-graph.html
nodes.summary: Template for the git commit graph: an SVG gutter drawing lane edges and commit dots over absolutely positioned row buttons showing refs (branches and tags), commit summary, author, relative date, and short hash, with click-to-select wiring.
nodes.languageNotes: Rows are positioned with explicit top/block-size pixel bindings computed by the component rather than document flow, so the SVG lane geometry and the row list stay aligned.

nodes.name: commit-graph.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the commit graph panel, styling the SVG lane gutter, commit rows, selection state, and the branch/tag ref badges.

nodes.name: diff-document-panel.html
nodes.summary: Template for the diff document tab: a toolbar with an inline/side-by-side layout dropdown, previous/next change navigation delegated to Monaco, a trailing file-status badge, and the embedded diff view for the selected changed file.

nodes.name: diff-document-panel.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the diff document panel, styling the layout dropdown and the per-status diff badge.

nodes.name: diff-view.html
nodes.summary: Template for the reusable diff view: hosts the Monaco-backed diff editor with original/modified/language/inline inputs, and shows an empty-state prompt when no file is selected.

nodes.name: diff-view.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the diff view, laying out the editor body and the centred empty-state message.

nodes.name: document-panel.html
nodes.summary: Template for the generic document panel host: dynamically instantiates the resolved document panel component via ngComponentOutlet, passing documentId, isActive, and removeOnDestroy inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses *ngComponentOutlet with the inputs binding so any registered document panel type can be mounted from one template.

nodes.name: document-panel.scss
nodes.summary: Minimal companion stylesheet for the generic document panel host.

nodes.name: issue-agent-confirm.html
nodes.summary: Template for the confirmation modal shown before opening a GitHub issue in the agent when a conversation already holds content: warns that the current transcript will be discarded and offers Yes/No actions bound to the issue-agent service's confirm and dismiss.

nodes.name: issue-agent-confirm.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the issue-to-agent confirmation modal, styling its title, message, and action row.

nodes.name: issue-document-panel.html
nodes.summary: Template for the GitHub issue document tab: a toolbar with the issue's open/closed state badge and Open-in-Agent / Open-on-GitHub actions mirroring the issue row's context menu, the issue-agent confirmation modal, and a scrollable body with title, byline, and facts (labels, assignees, milestone) that omits empty rows entirely.

nodes.name: issue-document-panel.scss
nodes.summary: Companion stylesheet for the GitHub issue document panel, styling the state badge, header, byline, label chips, facts list, and the scrollable issue body.

nodes.name: source-control-sidebar.html
nodes.summary: Template for the source-control view's left rail: an explorer toolbar with repository search plus a tree view whose row template renders section icons, branch delta counts (written/sent/received), staleness notes, status badges, and hover row actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular control-flow syntax (@if/@for/@let) with an ng-template row projected into the shared app-tree-view.

nodes.name: source-control-sidebar.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the source-control rail's filter strip and the row bits projected into the shared tree rows: section labels, branch deltas, the always-visible uncommitted-changes badge, hover row actions, and status badges, all driven by dock/accent theme tokens.
nodes.languageNotes: The uncommitted-changes badge deliberately opts out of the global .tree-row-action hover-reveal so the count stays visible.

nodes.name: terminal-panel.html
nodes.summary: Template for the Terminal dock panel: a tablist toolbar of terminal sessions with inline double-click rename via a text field, per-tab close buttons, a new-terminal button, and the terminal host area.

nodes.name: terminal-panel.scss
nodes.summary: Lays out the Terminal panel as a column of tab strip, terminal body, and status strip; all sessions stay mounted with only the active one visible, and the background tracks the resolved theme so it matches the xterm gutter.

nodes.name: popout-dock-host.scss
nodes.summary: Minimal flex-column styling that makes the popout dock host fill the auxiliary window's content column so the hosted dock container gets the full area.

nodes.name: property-grid.html
nodes.summary: Template for an editable name/value property grid with ARIA table semantics: optional enable checkboxes per row, text-field cells for name and value, and a draft blank row rendered by the same tracked loop so the caret survives the row becoming real.
nodes.languageNotes: Stored rows and the blank draft row share one @for tracked by id, so committing the draft keeps focus in the same DOM element.

nodes.name: property-grid.scss
nodes.summary: Grid layout and cell styling for the property grid: header row, tick/gutter columns, draft-row muting, and embedded text-field alignment.

nodes.name: pulse-dot.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the pulse-dot status indicator: a small solid circle with an animated fading pulse ring, with tone classes (accent, success, etc.) repointing a colour custom property and its rgb triple.
nodes.languageNotes: Tone variants swap both --pulse-dot-color and an rgb-triple variable so the ring can fade the same hue to transparent.

nodes.name: ribbon-strip-actions-button.html
nodes.summary: Template for the ribbon actions dropdown button: icon, label, and caret bound to a CdkMenu trigger, with the dropdown rendered by the shared app-menu into the global CDK overlay.

nodes.name: ribbon-strip-actions-button.scss
nodes.summary: Styles the ribbon actions button's icon/label/caret layout with hover, active, and disabled states matched to the ribbon strip's look.

nodes.name: ribbon-strip-button-small.html

nodes.name: LogArchive
nodes.summary: Persists log records to per-session JSONL files and a rotating human-readable log; offers session enumeration sorted by start time, session read-back with tolerant JSON parsing, and byte-budgeted rotation across numbered archive files.

nodes.name: log-store.ts
nodes.summary: In-memory, bounded ring buffer of structured log records for the current session, with monotonic sequence ids, field-length clamping, and severity/text filtering for the log viewer.

nodes.name: LogStore
nodes.summary: Holds the session's recent log records in a capacity-capped array: add() stamps time and sequence, truncates oversized source/message fields, and evicts the oldest record; filter() narrows by severity set and case-insensitive text match.

nodes.name: menu-manager.ts
nodes.summary: Main-process owner of the native application menu: receives renderer-declared menu sections over IPC, builds the Electron Menu template, executes native window/webContents roles (undo, copy, fullscreen, devtools), and sends command items back to the renderer.

nodes.name: MenuManager
nodes.summary: Registers IPC listeners for menu installation and role execution, translates renderer menu descriptors into Electron MenuItem templates (recursively for submenus), dispatches native roles against the focused window, and forwards command clicks to the renderer over webContents.send.

nodes.name: open-with-paths.ts
nodes.summary: Extracts absolute file paths from process argv so 'Open With' launches can open the requested files, distinguishing POSIX and Windows-drive path shapes and skipping Electron/dev-server flag arguments.

nodes.name: isAbsolutePathArgument
nodes.summary: Returns whether a command-line argument looks like an absolute file path, accepting POSIX '/' prefixes and Windows drive-letter forms.

nodes.name: openFilePathsFromArgv
nodes.summary: Filters process argv down to the absolute file paths a user asked to open, skipping the executable (and script when running from source) and discarding flag-style arguments.

nodes.name: preload.ts
nodes.summary: Electron preload script that synchronously reads the display-startup payload before first paint and exposes two context-bridged globals: window.host (static host facts — platform, arch, versions, homeDir, display policy) and window.bridge (the generic invoke/send/on IPC transport that feature clients wrap).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ipcRenderer.sendSync during preload so corner/effects policy is seeded before first paint, avoiding a squircle-to-round flash; the bridge strips the IpcRendererEvent so listeners receive only payloads.

nodes.name: shell-env.ts
nodes.summary: Captures the user's login-shell environment in the main process (so GUI-launched apps see the same PATH and env as a terminal), with delimiter-based parsing of shell output, per-shell caching, PATH merging, and hydration of process.env at startup.
nodes.languageNotes: Spawns the login shell with a sentinel-delimited `env` dump and parses only the region between delimiters, guarding against shell rc noise; agent-shell overrides are sanitized to reject flag-like values.

nodes.name: resolveDefaultShell
nodes.summary: Picks the user's default shell from environment candidates, trimming and falling back to a platform-appropriate default when unset.

nodes.name: parseEnvironment
nodes.summary: Parses shell stdout into an environment map by locating the sentinel delimiters, splitting the enclosed body into KEY=VALUE lines, and keeping only valid identifier names.

nodes.name: captureShellEnvironment
nodes.summary: Spawns the given shell as a login shell to dump its environment between sentinel delimiters, then returns the parsed environment map (or null on failure).

nodes.name: captureShellEnvironmentCached
nodes.summary: Memoizing wrapper around captureShellEnvironment that returns a per-shell cached capture, so repeated env requests (e.g. per terminal or agent spawn) avoid re-spawning the shell.

nodes.name: mergePath
nodes.summary: Merges a captured PATH with the existing PATH, preserving order while de-duplicating entries via a seen-set.

nodes.name: applyCapturedEnvironment
nodes.summary: Overlays a captured shell environment onto a base environment, applying explicit overrides and merging PATH entries rather than replacing them.

nodes.name: sanitizeAgentShell
nodes.summary: Validates a user-configured agent shell value, rejecting flag-like (dash-prefixed) or empty values so only a plausible shell path passes through.

nodes.name: hydrateLoginShellEnvironment
nodes.summary: Startup hook that resolves the default shell, captures its login environment, and applies the captured variables onto process.env so the GUI-launched app matches a terminal session; logs how many keys changed.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what ONIXLabs Studio is: a cross-platform desktop ADE — an agentic development environment — where AI agents are part of the workbench rather than a chat panel bolted onto an IDE. It sets out the product pillars this tour will trace through code: live persistent agent sessions, a fully rearrangeable dock-based workbench, real language intelligence, and safety by design. Keep those pillars in mind; each maps to a concrete subsystem we will visit.

tour.title: Two Processes, One App
tour.description: Like every Electron app, Studio is split into a privileged main process and a sandboxed renderer. The main entry point's Program class boots the backend: it creates windows and wires every backend manager — LSP, debugging, AI, git, terminals, workspaces, plugins — and registers the IPC surface. The preload script is the narrow gate between the two worlds: it exposes only window.host (static startup facts like platform and GPU recommendation, read synchronously before first paint) and a dumb pub/sub bridge — nothing else from Node.js leaks into the renderer.
tour.languageLesson: Electron's contextBridge deliberately gives the renderer a tiny, serializable API instead of raw Node access. Treating the renderer as untrusted — a core rule in this project — means every capability must cross an explicit, validated IPC boundary.

tour.title: The Generic IPC Bridge
tour.description: Before diving into the UI, meet the single contract that connects the two processes. The Bridge interface defines generic invoke/send/on primitives exposed as window.bridge — it is the only IPC seam in the app, which is why 42 other files depend on it. Alongside it, host.ts types the synchronous window.host startup payload. Because these files live in src/shared/api and are platform-neutral, both the Electron backend and the Angular renderer can share one vocabulary without importing each other.
tour.languageLesson: This is the 'ports and adapters' pattern expressed in TypeScript: a pure interface file with no runtime dependencies acts as the contract, and each side supplies its own implementation. The generic invoke<T> signature keeps channel payloads typed while the transport stays dumb.

tour.title: Renderer Bootstrap & Composition Root
tour.description: Now the front end. The renderer entry point decides whether to reduce visual effects (from persisted settings plus the GPU recommendation delivered via window.host from Step 2), warms icon fonts, and bootstraps the Root component. config.ts is the composition root: it wires zoneless change detection and eagerly provides every feature descriptor — agent, code, markdown, terminal, workspace, and friends. The Root shell component then composes the chrome: title strip, ribbon, status strip, content host, modal and toast hosts.
tour.languageLesson: This is Angular in its modern standalone + zoneless form: no NgModules and no Zone.js. Change detection is driven entirely by signals — reactive values that notify the framework precisely when they change — so config.ts wiring 'zoneless change detection' is a statement of architecture, not just a flag.

tour.title: The Feature Registry
tour.description: How does the shell from Step 4 know what a 'code editor' or an 'agent chat' is? Through the feature registry: a mapping from feature identifiers to their view, ribbon, status-strip, and document-panel components plus chrome settings, consumed by the shell when mounting tabs. The descriptor file defines the contract every feature must satisfy. This indirection is what makes features pluggable — the shell never imports a feature directly; it only asks the registry for components by id.

tour.title: Anatomy of a Feature
tour.description: Here is the other side of that contract. Each directory under src/features is isolated like a plugin: it may only import from @shared/*, never from another feature. Its *.feature.ts file is the single point where it registers with the shell — the code feature contributes its editor view, ribbon, status strip, and keybindings; the workspace feature contributes the directory host and run configurations; the agent feature contributes the chat view and eagerly instantiates its editor capabilities. Deleting a feature directory and its one line in config.ts removes the feature cleanly.

tour.title: Shared Renderer Services
tour.description: Features stay decoupled from each other by collaborating through shared services instead — and the fan-in numbers show who the load-bearing walls are. Tabs is the central tab manager (a signal-backed list with open, activate, close, and dirty-marking semantics; 35 dependents). Documents is the central document store handling open, save, dirty state, and external-change detection. Settings exposes typed reactive accessors for every registered setting, and Log — the single most depended-upon file in the renderer at 215 dependents — forwards structured records over the bridge to the main process.

tour.title: The Dock System
tour.description: The README promised a workbench you can arrange freely — this is the machinery behind it. The layout is a tree of split and stack nodes; dock-tree.ts is its pure functional core, performing structural-sharing queries and mutations, while dock-state.ts is the stateful service holding the layout tree signal and exposing immutable mutations plus undo/redo history. Each view supplies a DockBlueprint naming the panels it can host, and the dock-container component renders the whole tree along with the floating layer and drag overlay.
tour.languageLesson: Structural sharing means each mutation returns a new tree that reuses every unchanged branch. Combined with signals, this makes undo/redo almost free (keep the old roots) and change detection cheap (only rebuilt branches are new object references).

tour.title: The Main-Process Microkernel
tour.description: Back in the main process, the same extensibility philosophy appears as the contributions microkernel. The index file is a static in-bundle manifest of backend contributions activated at startup — adding a backend means appending to this list, never editing application wiring. Each contribution implements the MainContribution seam and receives a ContributionContext of tracked IPC, namespaced logging, and a permission broker. The plugins contribution shows the pattern at full depth: it loads external language servers and debug adapters from lockfile-pinned archives, mirroring the feature registry from Step 5 on the backend.

tour.title: The Agentic Core
tour.description: Now the heart of the ADE. In the main process, the AgentProvider seam defines what any AI backend must offer — availability, runs, live sessions — and the AI manager orchestrates providers built from user connections. Two very different implementations sit behind the same interface: the Claude provider drives the live Claude Agent SDK harness (persistent sessions, tools, hooks, sandboxing), while the AI SDK adapter covers stateless API-key providers like Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, DeepSeek, and Ollama. On the renderer side, the per-conversation agent service owns the transcript, streams model events, and manages runs, modes, and permission prompts — connected to the backend only through the bridge from Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: The key design axis here is live-harness vs stateless-model: a harness (Claude Agent SDK) keeps a real session alive with its own tool loop, while a stateless adapter replays context per request. Hiding that difference behind one AgentProvider interface is what lets the rest of the app treat all agents uniformly.

tour.title: The Rules of the House
tour.description: The architecture you have just seen is deliberately enforced. The agents guide lists the ten non-negotiable rules — feature isolation, no feature code in shared, the renderer is untrusted, and more — that keep the seams from Steps 5, 6, and 9 intact. The contributing guide adds the workflow: the mandatory pre-push 'green gate' (format, lint, coverage, build), the PR-only path to main, and commit conventions. Together they explain why the codebase stays navigable at this size.

tour.title: Build, CI & Release
tour.description: Finally, how it all ships. package.json declares the compiled Electron main entry and the esbuild scripts that bundle the main and preload processes, alongside the Angular build. electron-builder.yml is the single source of truth for packaging: the app ships as an asar with native pieces (node-pty, the Claude/Codex SDKs, ripgrep) unpacked. The CI workflow runs the same green gate from Step 11 on every PR, and the release workflow builds installers for four OS/architecture targets on architecture-matched runners.
tour.languageLesson: The release workflow uses architecture-matched runners because npm installs only the host platform's optional dependencies — cross-building two architectures on one runner silently ships the wrong native binaries. Matrix builds with one runner per target are the safe pattern.
